pages.body:
# Casual skin for the battle HUD and live graphs — Codex brief

> Historical implementation brief: this code survey describes published main `a3f96545`. The completed local UI/HUD and validation are owned by [the integration record](Casual_UI_Integration_20261014.en.md) and [the HUD handoff](Casual_Battle_HUD_20261014.en.md). Do not treat the old survey as missing implementation or restart generation.

Date: 2026-10-14 · [한국어](Casual_Battle_HUD_Codex_Prompt_20261014.md)

Paste the whole code block below into Codex. The mockup material is on the `claude/casual-battle-hud` branch, which is pushed.

| What to hand over | Where |
|---|---|
| Design canvas (12 boards, private) | https://claude.ai/artifact/PK5gEQdR1rrbW8Jzx3nDaA. Codex can open it only if the user shares it; the repository copy below is enough without it |
| Mockup source of truth (sources, 14 reference renders, layout numbers, copy table, seal and potion art, check tool) | `Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual/` ([README](../Design/GlobalHUD/Casual/README.en.md)) |
| This brief | this document |

```text
Rebuild the HELLSCRIPT battle screen's main HUD and battle graph windows to match the casual StyleD mockup. The mockup source of truth is Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual/ (README, 14 reference renders, mockup sources, seal and potion art, check tool). Combat, saves and graph maths stay as they are; this work changes the look, the layout and splits the graph windows.

## Background
- The game's art is moving from dark gothic to bright casual (StyleD, ages 12+). Swapping skins screen by screen, starting with representative screens, is approved; this is the battle HUD's turn.
- Use the same look as the other casual mockups (skill tree, training ground, battle position HUD and others): ink outline #2a3150, cream panels, yellow and orange accents, sky-blue resource, coral danger, Jua numbers and titles over Noto Sans KR body text, chunky drop shadows.
- The user set these directly in the mockup (README "Mockup notes" 1):
  - The Hunt Edict button sits top right, under menu and settings, in every orientation, and its tabs drop down below it.
  - The minimap moves to the lower right.
  - Status effects start above the left edge of the first potion; in portrait they sit above the slot row on the left.
  - Portrait graphs are small windows, and the portrait HUD is stacked.
  - Live DPS, monster damage, boss damage and activity time each move and fold on their own.
  - A folded activity window shows a text-free colour share bar next to its title.

## First
1. Rules: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, AgentRules/ (Shared_UI, UI_Refresh, Workflow, CPU_Performance, Unity_MCP, Wiki_Publish, Artifact_Cleanup). Use one task and one agent. Conversation and development records are in Korean; code comments, commit messages and logs are in English.
2. Create a new worktree and the branch codex/casual-battle-hud from the latest origin/main (other sessions share the main checkout). Bring the mockup in with:
   git fetch origin claude/casual-battle-hud && git checkout origin/claude/casual-battle-hud -- Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual Docs/Implementation/Casual_Battle_HUD_Codex_Prompt_20261014.md Docs/Implementation/Casual_Battle_HUD_Codex_Prompt_20261014.en.md
3. Read Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual/README.en.md to the end and open all 14 files in reference/. That document and the CSS in canvas/Main.dc.html are authoritative for layout numbers, part states, graph rules and copy; what follows is a summary. node Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual/tools/smoke.js checks the mockup rules and is the source for the rules to port into game tests.

## Current state (main a3f96545, code read directly)
- Main HUD:
  - Presentation/GlobalHudView.cs builds the HUD at runtime (shared by the preview and the game).
  - GlobalHudStyle in GlobalHudLayout.cs holds numbers and colours, read from Resources/Data/GlobalHudLayout.json. Coordinates are bottom-left based on a 1600×900 reference. Portrait fits the landscape composition into one row by width, so slots end up about 27 pt on a portrait phone.
  - GlobalHudSnapshot.cs builds slot states (ready, cooldown, not enough resource ◇, in use, locked, empty) and the effect list.
  - GameUI.GlobalHud.cs handles slot and effect descriptions and the observation menu.
- HUD art: Resources/Art/GlobalHUD/*.png (frame-seal, frame-vital, fill-vital, frame-active, frame-status, badge-*, status-*, mask-*, xp-*, control-*, menu-*, potion-hp/mp/utility).
  - The 63 hand-built vector pictures can be rebuilt with Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Resources/v1/build-vectors.cjs (uses sharp).
  - GlobalHudView.Portrait(heroClass) picks the seal portrait: portrait-mage for the mage, SkillAtlas 18+class for the others.
  - Potion bottles come from PotionArt.IconId → Art/GlobalHUD/potion-*, with the bottle crop rectangles hard-coded in PotionArt. Crafted elixirs live in Art/Jeweler/Potions.
  - SkillIconView draws skill slots (frame-active, frame-seal).
- Hunt Edict button:
  - GlobalHudLayout.edict is the spot above the seal, and the "Hunt edict" button (menu-hunt-edict) is in GlobalHudView.
  - Tapping it runs GameUI.EdictQuick.ToggleEdictQuick, which opens quickRoot (sorting order 107). GameUI.EdictSheet.BuildEdictTabIcons lays the menu-edict-* icons of HuntEdictHudRows.Tabs (combat, survival, explore, repeat, presets) to the right of the button at 80% of its size; a tab opens OpenEdictSheet.
  - GameUI.EdictPosition.cs uses the same button as its anchor.
- Minimap: GameUI.Rift.ReflowRiftMinimap (riftMinimapPanel) places it at the top (top 88/122/158), left of the right-hand content dock column, following MapDisplay.Corner. GameUI.BattleLayout.ReflowBattleHud does the layout.
- Live DPS window:
  - GameUI.TrainingGround.BuildTrainingHud/PlaceTrainingHud build trainingHud. Its default spot is left of the map at top 124, width min(320, 30%); it folds, and its position is saved on the device through DpsHudDrag and game.DpsPosition.
  - The chart is TrainingChartView + TrainingDpsChart, with Current #b98230 and Previous #4a87bd. These are shared with the result windows TrainingDpsPanel and RiftCombatGraphWindow.
- Damage-taken graphs: in GameUI.DamageGraphs.cs the monster and boss graphs are children of trainingHud, so they hang under the DPS window and fold with it. The bar is full at 50% and changes colour at 20% and 40%. Data comes from DamageGraph.Monsters/Boss, boss seals from Art/Boss/seal-* and attack icons from Art/Boss/skill-*.
- Activity time:
  - GameUI.RiftActivity.cs builds activityHud; it folds and saves its position through DpsHudDrag and game.ActivityPosition.
  - RiftActivityPanel.cs is shared with the result window and uses UiTheme.Resource/Danger/PaidFatigueText/Success.
  - Positions are stored by Core/DpsHudPosition.cs (directory, file); there are two now (DPS, activity).
- Shared owners: UiTheme and UiFonts own colours, fonts and sizes; StorageSurface paints panels. main has no casual colour tokens and no Jua or Noto Sans KR fonts yet; on 2026-10-14 no other casual branch had changed UiTheme or UiFonts either.
- Related records: Docs/Implementation/Global_HUD_Potions, Damage_Graphs_20261010, Edict_Hud_Sheet_20261011, Rift_Activity_Time (each .md/.en.md), Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/*.
- Related tests: GlobalHudTests, GlobalHudResourceTests, BattleHudLayoutTests, DamageGraphTests, DpsHudTests, CombatActivityTests, HuntEdictHudRowsTests, PotionTests, PotionLoadoutTests.
- Related smokes: RuntimeGlobalHudSmoke, RuntimeBattleLayoutSmoke, RuntimeDamageGraphSmoke, RuntimeHudScaleSmoke, RuntimeTrainingGroundSmoke (.RiftDps, .Activity), RuntimeBattleQuickEditSmoke.

## Work (summary; numbers in the README)
1. Look owner: add the casual colours (ink, cream, yellow, orange, gold, sky, coral, mint, green, empty track, secondary text) as named values to the existing owner (UiTheme, or GlobalHudStyle/GlobalHudLayout.json when HUD-only). HUD and graph code use only those values and do not scatter colour literals.
   - Changing an existing shared UiTheme value affects other screens; if you must, report the reach.
   - Build the panel recipe (cream, ink border, inner dashed stitch, drop shadow) as a casual variant of a shared painter such as StorageSurface, or as one 9-slice sprite.
   - Pick one approach for text outlines and record why. Do not stack several uGUI Outline/Shadow components per label.
2. Rebuild the HUD art:
   - With a casual copy of build-vectors.cjs (for example Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Resources/v2-casual/), regenerate frame-seal, frame-vital, fill-vital, frame-active, frame-status, badge-*, status-*, control-* and xp-* to the README recipes. Keep file names, sizes, 9-slice borders and .meta GUIDs.
   - Make menu-hunt-edict and menu-edict-* casual round buttons (white face, ink outline, drop shadow) with single-colour ink icons.
   - No hand-drawn raster art: use the vector generator or Codex image generation only.
3. Seal and potion art:
   - Seals: bring Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual/assets/seal-{warrior,ranger,mage}-m.png into Resources and make Portrait(heroClass) use the new seal per class. Put the three seal-*-f files in the same folder without wiring them; saving a hero's gender belongs to the character create/select work and is not part of this task.
   - Potions: replace potion-hp/mp/utility.png in Art/GlobalHUD with the casual files, keeping their GUIDs, and re-measure the PotionArt crop rectangles for the new pictures.
   - Leave the SkillAtlas 18+class portraits if other screens use them.
   - Add a row to Editor/ResourceTextureBudget.cs for each new texture and report the size change. The originals stay in Git history.
4. Layout (GlobalHudLayout, GameUI.BattleLayout, ReflowRiftMinimap):
   - Move the Hunt Edict button top right, under the menu and settings buttons, in every orientation. Change BuildEdictTabIcons so the tabs drop down below the button as a vertical menu (cream frame, tab name under each icon). If this collides with the content dock column, put the button at the top of that column (under settings) and report the difference.
   - Leave the spot above the seal empty.
   - Move the minimap to the lower right, above the skill row.
   - Status effects: on PC and landscape they start above the left edge of the first potion; in portrait they sit above the slot row on the left. Eight expanded tiles must not overlap the minimap or graph windows.
   - Stack the portrait HUD from the top as status effects → slot row (spread to both edges) → seal, bars and potion settings → XP, instead of the one-row fit. The bottom layout on landscape and PC stays as it is.
5. Graph windows:
   - Detach the monster and boss graphs from trainingHud into windows of their own. Each window moves, folds and saves its position on the device (two more DpsHudPosition files; the save-failure toast reuses the existing copy).
   - Default positions stack under DPS in order. In a portrait boss fight the boss window opens on the left under the activity window.
   - Folding DPS folds only the DPS window.
   - A folded activity window shows the four-colour share bar beside its title, with no text.
   - Portrait uses small windows (widths 196 and 180, no DPS legend or stat cells); landscape hides the DPS legend. Windows use the casual panel.
   - Chart colours: this run is a solid orange #ff9f1c line over a 30% yellow area; the previous run is dashed sky #35a7ff; draw the end dot and round skill marks. TrainingDpsChart is shared with the result windows, so their charts take the same colours (which match the casual result mockups); report this.
   - Activity colours: movement #35a7ff, attacking #ff5a5f, dodging #ffd23f (line #d9a300), farming #4cbf55. The result window that shares RiftActivityPanel follows.
6. State visuals:
   - Under 30% HP, show a coral ring on the seal and on the HP bar. If the game already has a threshold for this, use it. The pulse is soft, on a 1.1 s cycle.
   - The shield is a mint strip along the top of the HP bar plus text above it (repaint the existing shieldLine and shield).
   - Slot states look as described in README "Parts and states".
7. Copy: reuse existing keys per the README copy table and add new keys in Korean and English together. A missing key falls back to Korean and is logged; never show an empty string or a key name.

## Decisions (go with these defaults and report)
- Decision 1 — Fonts: add no new font in this work. Use the existing UiFonts; if the skill-window casual skin work has landed Jua and Noto Sans KR on main, use those.
- Decision 2 — HUD size: the mockup is tuned for phone legibility (landscape slots 48 pt, portrait 42 pt). Keep GlobalHudLayout's scaling rules (1600×900 reference, 0.4 floor), but make the portrait stack produce slots close to the mockup size, and report the real sizes.
- Decision 3 — Content dock vs edict button: follow the default in step 4 above.
- Decision 4 — Result windows: only the colours of the shared parts (TrainingDpsChart, RiftActivityPanel) may change; result window layouts stay.

## Do not
Change combat, reward or save rules or the graph maths (DamageGraph, CombatFeedback); add hero gender or six-hero saves (the character create/select work); add a class; redraw skill icons, boss art, fields or monsters; bring back the removed text-size setting, its 50–150% checks or the enlarged-text smoke; change colours or layout of other screens; hand-draw art.

## Verification (only related checks while working)
- Related EditMode:
  - Run the related tests listed above.
  - Add layout tests: in all three orientations (portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440, PC 1600×900), status effects (collapsed and expanded), the slot row, the minimap, the open edict menu and the graph windows' default positions must not overlap each other and must stay inside the safe area.
  - Test save and load for the two new DpsHudPosition files, save failure, and restoring an off-screen position.
  - Run the fold states, LocalizationTests (new keys in both languages) and the ResourceTextureBudget check.
  - Port the rules in tools/smoke.js (full at 50%, 20%/40% colours, activity shares sum to 100, tab order, boss window only while a boss is alive) into EditMode.
- Smokes:
  - Update RuntimeGlobalHudSmoke, RuntimeBattleLayoutSmoke, RuntimeDamageGraphSmoke, RuntimeHudScaleSmoke, RuntimeTrainingGroundSmoke (RiftDps, Activity) and RuntimeBattleQuickEditSmoke for the new layout and the split windows.
  - The edict menu must drop down and open its tabs.
  - Move windows with a real mouse drag in a separate Mac player window, and leave proof that the saved positions come back after a restart.
- Screens:
  - Capture portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440 and PC 1600×900, 1280×720 and 1720×720 in Korean and English.
  - States: default, boss fight, danger, and folded with the edict menu and effects open. Compare each side by side with the same state in reference/.
  - Check safe areas, 44 pt touch targets, overlaps and clipped text. Phone aspect ratios come from Mac windows with simulated insets; do not report them as device results.
- Pass python3 tools/check_ui_contract.py --verify and follow the post-save UI refresh rule (AgentRules/UI_Refresh.md).
- Run the full EditMode suite and the macOS development-build runtime smoke once, after the last code change and the latest main merge. Separate failures that already existed from new ones. Documentation-only changes do not need game runs again.
- Performance:
  - Keep the current graph refresh rates (DPS and damage 1 s, activity 0.15 s) and never relayout every frame.
  - Claim performance only with at least three matched before/after runs of the real binaries with CPU and GC data; otherwise write "not measured".
  - Report texture memory changes as size numbers.

## Deliverables
- One PR (codex/casual-battle-hud). Do not merge it; merging waits for the user's approval. Include the mockup package (Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual), and commit related checks and records together.
- Bilingual record Docs/Implementation/Casual_Battle_HUD_20261014(.en).md: what changed, decision results, where you departed from the mockup, check results, and what was not verified. Update the Global_HUD_Potions, Damage_Graphs and Rift_Activity_Time records too. Put evidence screenshots as jpg in Docs/Implementation/CasualBattleHudEvidence/ and link each file.
- If wiki sources change, follow AgentRules/Wiki_Publish.md; follow AgentRules/Artifact_Cleanup.md for cleanup.

## Report (in Korean, short)
Actual changes, the results of decisions 1–4, where and why you departed from the mockup, what you actually checked and what is unverified (devices, performance), size changes, and what is left. Do not report macOS results as device results.
```

   - Add a row to Editor/ResourceTextureBudget.cs for each new texture and report the size change. The originals stay in Git history.
4. Layout (GlobalHudLayout, GameUI.BattleLayout, ReflowRiftMinimap):
   - Move the Hunt Edict button top right, under the menu and settings buttons, in every orientation. Change BuildEdictTabIcons so the tabs drop down below the button as a vertical menu (cream frame, tab name under each icon). If this collides with the content dock column, put the button at the top of that column (under settings) and report the difference.
   - Leave the spot above the seal empty.
   - Move the minimap to the lower right, above the skill row.
   - Status effects: on PC and landscape they start above the left edge of the first potion; in portrait they sit above the slot row on the left. Eight expanded tiles must not overlap the minimap or graph windows.
   - Stack the portrait HUD from the top as status effects → slot row (spread to both edges) → seal, bars and potion settings → XP, instead of the one-row fit. The bottom layout on landscape and PC stays as it is.
5. Graph windows:
   - Detach the monster and boss graphs from trainingHud into windows of their own. Each window moves, folds and saves its position on the device (two more DpsHudPosition files; the save-failure toast reuses the existing copy).
   - Default positions stack under DPS in order. In a portrait boss fight the boss window opens on the left under the activity window.
   - Folding DPS folds only the DPS window.
   - A folded activity window shows the four-colour share bar beside its title, with no text.
   - Portrait uses small windows (widths 196 and 180, no DPS legend or stat cells); landscape hides the DPS legend. Windows use the casual panel.
   - Chart colours: this run is a solid orange #ff9f1c line over a 30% yellow area; the previous run is dashed sky #35a7ff; draw the end dot and round skill marks. TrainingDpsChart is shared with the result windows, so their charts take the same colours (which match the casual result mockups); report this.
   - Activity colours: movement #35a7ff, attacking #ff5a5f, dodging #ffd23f (line #d9a300), farming #4cbf55. The result window that shares RiftActivityPanel follows.
6. State visuals:
   - Under 30% HP, show a coral ring on the seal and on the HP bar. If the game already has a threshold for this, use it. The pulse is soft, on a 1.1 s cycle.
   - The shield is a mint strip along the top of the HP bar plus text above it (repaint the existing shieldLine and shield).
   - Slot states look as described in README "Parts and states".
7. Copy: reuse existing keys per the README copy table and add new keys in Korean and English together. A missing key falls back to Korean and is logged; never show an empty string or a key name.

## Decisions (go with these defaults and report)
- Decision 1 — Fonts: add no new font in this work. Use the existing UiFonts; if the skill-window casual skin work has landed Jua and Noto Sans KR on main, use those.
- Decision 2 — HUD size: the mockup is tuned for phone legibility (landscape slots 48 pt, portrait 42 pt). Keep GlobalHudLayout's scaling rules (1600×900 reference, 0.4 floor), but make the portrait stack produce slots close to the mockup size, and report the real sizes.
- Decision 3 — Content dock vs edict button: follow the default in step 4 above.
- Decision 4 — Result windows: only the colours of the shared parts (TrainingDpsChart, RiftActivityPanel) may change; result window layouts stay.

Change combat, reward or save rules or the graph maths (DamageGraph, CombatFeedback); add hero gender or six-hero saves (the character create/select work); add a class; redraw skill icons, boss art, fields or monsters; bring back the removed text-size setting, its 50–150% checks or the enlarged-text smoke; change colours or layout of other screens; hand-draw art.

## Verification (only related checks while working)
- Related EditMode:
  - Run the related tests listed above.
  - Add layout tests: in all three orientations (portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440, PC 1600×900), status effects (collapsed and expanded), the slot row, the minimap, the open edict menu and the graph windows' default positions must not overlap each other and must stay inside the safe area.
  - Test save and load for the two new DpsHudPosition files, save failure, and restoring an off-screen position.
  - Run the fold states, LocalizationTests (new keys in both languages) and the ResourceTextureBudget check.
  - Port the rules in tools/smoke.js (full at 50%, 20%/40% colours, activity shares sum to 100, tab order, boss window only while a boss is alive) into EditMode.
- Smokes:
  - Update RuntimeGlobalHudSmoke, RuntimeBattleLayoutSmoke, RuntimeDamageGraphSmoke, RuntimeHudScaleSmoke, RuntimeTrainingGroundSmoke (RiftDps, Activity) and RuntimeBattleQuickEditSmoke for the new layout and the split windows.
  - The edict menu must drop down and open its tabs.
  - Move windows with a real mouse drag in a separate Mac player window, and leave proof that the saved positions come back after a restart.
- Screens:
  - Capture portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440 and PC 1600×900, 1280×720 and 1720×720 in Korean and English.
  - States: default, boss fight, danger, and folded with the edict menu and effects open. Compare each side by side with the same state in reference/.
  - Check safe areas, 44 pt touch targets, overlaps and clipped text. Phone aspect ratios come from Mac windows with simulated insets; do not report them as device results.
- Pass python3 tools/check_ui_contract.py --verify and follow the post-save UI refresh rule (AgentRules/UI_Refresh.md).
- Run the full EditMode suite and the macOS development-build runtime smoke once, after the last code change and the latest main merge. Separate failures that already existed from new ones. Documentation-only changes do not need game runs again.
- Performance:
  - Keep the current graph refresh rates (DPS and damage 1 s, activity 0.15 s) and never relayout every frame.
  - Claim performance only with at least three matched before/after runs of the real binaries with CPU and GC data; otherwise write "not measured".
  - Report texture memory changes as size numbers.

## Deliverables
- One PR (codex/casual-battle-hud). Do not merge it; merging waits for the user's approval. Include the mockup package (Docs/Design/GlobalHUD/Casual), and commit related checks and records together.
- Bilingual record Docs/Implementation/Casual_Battle_HUD_20261014(.en).md: what changed, decision results, where you departed from the mockup, check results, and what was not verified. Update the Global_HUD_Potions, Damage_Graphs and Rift_Activity_Time records too. Put evidence screenshots as jpg in Docs/Implementation/CasualBattleHudEvidence/ and link each file.
- If wiki sources change, follow AgentRules/Wiki_Publish.md; follow AgentRules/Artifact_Cleanup.md for cleanup.

## Report (in Korean, short)
Actual changes, the results of decisions 1–4, where and why you departed from the mockup, what you actually checked and what is unverified (devices, performance), size changes, and what is left. Do not report macOS results as device results.

# Casual skin mockup for the skill window

Updated: 2026-10-14

[한국어](README.md)

The game's art concept moved from dark gothic ("Obsidian & Gilt") to a bright, cute, casual medieval fantasy for ages 12+ (style D; see the [concept record](../../../Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/Casual_Art_Concept_20261013.en.md)). This folder holds the **skill window (`../SkillWindow.dc.html`) with the same composition in the new look**: rules, layout, copy and interactions are unchanged; only colours, fonts, borders, shadows and decorations differ.

- Design canvas (approved by the user): https://claude.ai/artifact/JsCKnJUbKkzfBYyJDR3493 (24 boards: 3 classes × portrait / landscape / PC × KO / EN, plus the passives view)
- The original dark mockup is `../SkillWindow.dc.html`, identical to commit `86cfeff1`.

## Files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `SkillWindow.casual.locked.dc.html` | **The reference for the game.** The approved canvas mockup with the few layout-affecting font sizes and the rank-badge size reverted to the original, so every rectangle and font size equals the original. With this file as the mockup, `golden/layout`, `viewmodel`, `interaction` and `rules_golden` must regenerate unchanged. |
| `SkillWindow.casual.dc.html` | The mockup exactly as the user approved it on the canvas. Titles, tabs, panel names, section headings, buttons and badge text are slightly larger than the original (table below). Whether the game adopts those sizes is a separate user decision. |
| `tools/restyle.py` | Original → casual transform (every replacement count-checked, so it fails loudly if the original changes). |
| `tools/lock_geometry.py` | Casual → locked transform (font sizes reverted). |
| `tools/geo_compare.js` | Runs both mockups through 36 combinations (3 classes × 3 layouts × 2 views × 2 languages) and lists rectangle and font-size differences. `node tools/geo_compare.js <original> <locked>` must report 0 font-size differences. |

## What changes visually

- Background: a sky-blue to cream gradient with clouds. Plates are cream (`#fff6e3`) with a 3 px ink (`#2a3150`) outline, a hard bottom shadow (`0 5px 0`), a dashed stitch inset and a round gem on top. The blurred art backdrop (`artWrap`) read as a smudge and was removed.
- Type: Jua for titles, tabs, numbers, buttons and sub-headings; Noto Sans KR 700/900 for body text. Titles are yellow with an 8-direction ink outline.
- Colour roles: invested, selected and key passives `#ffd23f / #ffc21a / #ff9f1c` (text `#e08a00`); passives and info `#35a7ff / #2f8fd8 / #1f6fb5`; available `#8a93b5`; locked `#e6e9f0` dashed; warnings `#ff5a5f`; invest button green `#8ee07a → #4cbf55`; close button coral.
- Lines: 3 px, lit lines get a 7 px ink under-stroke; locked lines are pale grey dashes.
- Skill icons (the sprite sheets) are unchanged.

## Canvas mockup vs locked file (layout-affecting values)

| Element | Canvas mockup | Locked (original size) |
|---|---|---|
| Window title (landscape / portrait / PC) | 28 / 31 / 30 | 24 / 27 / 26 |
| Class tab text (landscape + PC / portrait) | 15 / 16 | 13 / 14 |
| Buttons (refund, invest) text | 16 | 13 |
| Panel name (landscape + PC / portrait) | 18 / 22 | 16 / 19 |
| Panel sub-heading (landscape + PC / portrait) | 14 / 16 | 12.5 / 14.5 |
| Tier badge numeral (first 3 / others) | 14 / 12 | 13 / 11 |
| Tier badge name (landscape / portrait) | 13 / 14 | 12 / 13 |
| Level and points-spent values | 15 | surrounding size |
| Rank badge circle | 18×18 | 16×16 |

Some interior values still differ in the locked file (padding of the passive medal ring, rank-badge line height, right-hand chip padding of panel modifier rows). They are inside elements, not element rectangles.

## Rebuilding

```bash
python3 -I tools/restyle.py <original SkillWindow.dc.html> SkillWindow.casual.dc.html
python3 -I tools/lock_geometry.py SkillWindow.casual.dc.html SkillWindow.casual.locked.dc.html
node tools/geo_compare.js <original> SkillWindow.casual.locked.dc.html   # 0 font-size differences
```

pages.body:
# Chain Lightning hunt-edict implementation record

Date: 2026-09-13 · [한국어](Edict_Chain_Expansion.md)

Status: **all four M03 core options are connected; the full suite, a new macOS launch/restart and 16 selected diagnostic runs are complete.**

## Problem and resulting behavior

Chain Lightning's saved options affected aiming, but executable candidates still came from legacy behavior rules. An opted-in hero with M03 equipped now derives an independent policy from all four saved options. Missing, disabled or condition-blocked legacy rows cannot override the new policy. Duplicate rows yield one candidate without changing the saved rule list. Opting out restores legacy behavior.

M01, M02 and M03 follow the common attack order and display their own names in decision history. A valid first target outside casting range permits an approach; OFF cancels that approach. Unlock level, actual cost, cooldown, action locks and global survival responses retain their execution gates.

## Four connected options

| Option | Runtime behavior |
|---|---|
| Automatic use | OFF excludes new casts. Paid preparation retains its first target and reserved set bonus. |
| Purpose | SINGLE allows one valid first target. LINKED requires at least two distinct targets under the real linking rules. SAVE_CHARGE normally requires two, but permits one when an actual SMB four-piece charge exists and expires within one second. Without the set it falls back to LINKED while preserving the saved choice. No special wait-for-Nova state is introduced. |
| First target | ALL compares all valid candidates. ELITE prefers valid elite/boss candidates and SUPPORT prefers support enemies. If that category is absent or entirely outside first-cast range, other valid candidates are used. An insufficient chain within the preferred category cannot borrow another group's target count. |
| Chain criterion | UNIQUE maximizes distinct targets; TOTAL_HITS includes LM04 revisits. Candidates are ranked within the preferred first-target category, then by distance to the exact global target and by enemy ID. Without LM04, TOTAL_HITS falls back to unique targets while preserving the original choice. |

First targets must be alive, perceived and not excluded by global tracking. They pass the 10 m initial range and line-of-sight checks. Later links use currently perceived enemies under the actual chain rules; first-target exclusion does not grant immunity to subsequent links. Forecasts describe the current formation, so movement during preparation can change the real result.

## Linking, damage and charge boundaries

The next target must be alive, within 4 m of the previous enemy and visible from it. Unvisited enemies take priority, with distance and ID breaking ties. The base hit limit is four, MP03 adds one and an SMB charge reserved at cast start adds two, for a maximum of seven. Forecasts and releases share the limit calculation and next-target selector.

LM04 permits at most two visits per enemy but prohibits consecutive hits on the same enemy. A→B→A is valid. Each hop applies the existing 0.8 decay, and revisits additionally multiply damage by 0.5. LM04 does not increase the total hit cap. A lone boss receives only one hit even with MP03 and a charge.

An actual Frost Nova hit grants two SMB four-piece charges for six seconds. Chain Lightning spends one at preparation start and stores the two bonus hits in the pending action. Forecasting, held conditions, insufficient resources, cooldowns and level locks do not spend charges. SMB two-piece and LC02 discounts retain the 50% total cost-reduction cap.

Release now rechecks the first target's life, perception, initial range and sight. If it dies or moves beyond range or behind a wall, the cast records `ACTION_MISS` and deals no damage. It does not transfer to another enemy or refund the paid resource/charge. This correction also applies to legacy-rule casts. Subsequent links are reevaluated using the release-time formation.

## UI and persistence

The card explains the scope of the four settings and the charge-consumption boundary in Korean and English. `edict:M03` identifies the derived decision. Validation follows the [screen layout specification](../Design/HELLSCRIPT_Screen_Layout_Detail.md): scrollable content, accessible footer actions, enlarged text and compact landscape layouts.

The save schema, legacy rules, scenes, prefabs and packages remain intact. Changing the first-target preference or saving OFF during preparation does not rewrite a paid cast's target or reserved bonus. Validation uses isolated projects and dedicated saves.

## Scope of Chain Control diagnostics

The completed [affix comparison](Affix_Audit_Expansion.en.md) found poor Chain Control clear rates with both profiles. A new observer leaves combat stats unchanged and records time in preparation, cooldown, other actions, no perceived enemy, outside initial range and remaining states, plus actual casts, links and boss damage. Time buckets sample state after each 50 ms step; they are approximate occupancy, not a causal attribution of delay. The remaining-state bucket does not guarantee that every execution gate passes. A test verifies that observing a generated rift preserves its outcome and existing combat aggregates.

The stage-20 sample selects two previous cases from each category: death before boss spawn, timeout before spawn, death after spawn and timeout after spawn. Seed indices 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 14 are outcome-selected, not a random sample. Level 30 and eight legal equipped items are fixed; legacy rules and the current hunt edict use matched maps, enemies and gear. The edict treatment includes global policies, so differences cannot be attributed solely to M03. Current runtime changes also mean this is not a replay of the archived affix experiment's executable.

### Results from the 16 selected runs

Collection completed from 2026-09-12 15:57:47 to 15:59:41 UTC. Seeds, maps, initial enemies, objectives, complete equipment values, maximum HP, base damage and stat sheets matched within every pair and against the archived sample. Starts, releases and hits matched the existing combat aggregates; sampled durations agreed with elapsed simulation time within tolerance in every run.

| Measurement | Eight legacy runs | Eight current-edict runs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Clears / deaths / timeouts | 0 / 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 / 4 |
| Runs reaching boss spawn | 4 | 2 |
| M03 starts / interruptions / first-target misses | 535 / 29 / 6 | 551 / 78 / 13 |
| Actual M03 hits | 1,740 | 1,754 |
| Hits per release, including misses | 3.44 | 3.71 |
| Starts reserving a charge | 116 | 137 |
| Resource-blocked checks | 0 | 0 |
| Pre-boss time with no perceived enemy | 39.7% | 41.2% |
| Pre-boss time performing another action | 41.2% | 40.7% |

Connecting the options and consuming charges did not resolve poor outcomes. This sample supports investigating exploration, other actions and interruptions before resource starvation. No perceived enemy includes normal exploration, and another action is not necessarily an error. The four legacy runs reaching the boss spawned it at an average of 232.63 seconds, consuming much of the 300-second limit. The specified single hit against a lone boss remains intact.

Next, record interruption reasons alongside active threats and survival responses, and connect remaining core policies such as M04 while checking for unnecessary repeated preparation cancellation. Separate time spent reaching the boss from single-boss damage. The selected sample is not a population win-rate estimate; affix weights and damage multipliers were not retuned.

Raw data is `Artifacts/Validation/EdictChain/Diagnostic1/runs.jsonl`, with matched summaries in `diagnostic-summary.json`. The isolated-project entry point is `Hellscript.Editor.BuildIntegrationValidation.RunChainDiagnostics`, accepting `-hellscriptAuditStage`, `-hellscriptChainSeeds` and `-hellscriptAuditOutput`. Existing output directories are not overwritten.

## Validation and executable

The final **292-test focused run** and **1,566-test full Edit Mode suite** passed. The full suite ran from 2026-09-12 15:56:55 to 16:01:59 UTC in 304.19 seconds, with zero failures or skips. New coverage includes 51 M03 cases and one observer noninterference case. Integration includes an actual Frost Nova granting two charges, followed by two Chain Lightning casts consuming one each and producing seven hits apiece.

The first focused run passed 289 of 290 tests. Its single failure came from incompatible corridor data retained in a synthetic sight-blocking fixture. The fixture was corrected; actual Nova integration and observer coverage were added before the passing final run. The initial failed report is preserved.

| Native macOS check | Result |
|---|---|
| Editing and persistence | Actual buttons selected SAVE_CHARGE, SUPPORT and TOTAL_HITS. The saved source stayed unchanged while editing; memory and a fresh file read matched after applying. An actual button enabled the edict. |
| Charge hold and start | One uncharged target held the cast. Supplying a short-lived fixture charge and linked enemies selected a support first target and consumed one charge at preparation start. Actual Frost Nova charge generation was separately verified in Edit Mode. |
| Independent process restart | ELITE/OFF was saved during preparation before exiting. Restart restored the original first target, resource, time and reserved bonus, producing one seven-hit release. Each enemy received at most two nonconsecutive hits. No duplicate payment, extra charge consumption or new OFF-state cast occurred. |
| Layout and pause | Korean/English and 140% text were checked at 1280×720, 720×1280 and 640×360. Text-height, missing-translation and footer safe-area checks passed. Closing translated decision screens preserved running and manually paused entry states. |

The first native attempt exited because its new command-line flag collided with an existing rift-objective smoke flag. The new smoke now uses `-hellscriptChainEdictSmoke` and `-hellscriptChainEdictResume`. The final build and both `Native2` processes passed from 2026-09-12 15:58:14 to 15:58:34 UTC. Those two smoke flag names are the only difference between the full-suite/diagnostic source and the final app source; the variant is preserved explicitly. Combat and UI behavior did not change after the full suite began.

Ten screenshots were retained. Enlarged English options, compact landscape options, Korean restored decisions and the post-restart combat screen were visually inspected. Inputs use actual UI callbacks with controlled combat placement and time. This is not mobile-device touch, rotation or performance evidence.

The app is `Builds/macOS-EdictChain/HELLSCRIPT.app`, with evidence under `Artifacts/Validation/EdictChain/`. All 242 C#/English-table inputs, including 172 Runtime C# files, match the final build source. No C# metadata is missing and no asset GUID is duplicated. `validated-source.tar.gz` preserves 653 source/design-input/authored-setting files, including the old smoke-flag variant. SHA-256: `55cec1caeb98aa741755e80e16714679c1e000e213b22e13368e21b56090cbd2`. Unity-added URP Editor version metadata in the validation copy's material is recorded separately; the authored asset is preserved.

## Remaining work

Next: connect remaining fixed policies such as M04 and record the reasons for interrupted preparation. Investigate Chain Control's boss-arrival time alongside survival responses and interrupted attacks. Multi-stage progression and farming value, remaining legendary/set equipment boundaries, mobile execution and overall release quality remain open.

The completed affix comparison found poor Chain Control clear rates with both profiles. A new observer leaves combat stats unchanged and records time in preparation, cooldown, other actions, no perceived enemy, outside initial range and remaining states, plus actual casts, links and boss damage. Time buckets sample state after each 50 ms step; they are approximate occupancy, not a causal attribution of delay. The remaining-state bucket does not guarantee that every execution gate passes. A test verifies that observing a generated rift preserves its outcome and existing combat aggregates.

The stage-20 sample selects two previous cases from each category: death before boss spawn, timeout before spawn, death after spawn and timeout after spawn. Seed indices 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 14 are outcome-selected, not a random sample. Level 30 and eight legal equipped items are fixed; legacy rules and the current hunt edict use matched maps, enemies and gear. The edict treatment includes global policies, so differences cannot be attributed solely to M03. Current runtime changes also mean this is not a replay of the archived affix experiment's executable.

Results from the 16 selected runs

Collection completed from 2026-09-12 15:57:47 to 15:59:41 UTC. Seeds, maps, initial enemies, objectives, complete equipment values, maximum HP, base damage and stat sheets matched within every pair and against the archived sample. Starts, releases and hits matched the existing combat aggregates; sampled durations agreed with elapsed simulation time within tolerance in every run.

MeasurementEight legacy runsEight current-edict runs
Clears / deaths / timeouts0 / 4 / 40 / 4 / 4
Runs reaching boss spawn42
M03 starts / interruptions / first-target misses535 / 29 / 6551 / 78 / 13
Actual M03 hits1,7401,754
Hits per release, including misses3.443.71
Starts reserving a charge116137
Resource-blocked checks00
Pre-boss time with no perceived enemy39.7%41.2%
Pre-boss time performing another action41.2%40.7%

Connecting the options and consuming charges did not resolve poor outcomes. This sample supports investigating exploration, other actions and interruptions before resource starvation. No perceived enemy includes normal exploration, and another action is not necessarily an error. The four legacy runs reaching the boss spawned it at an average of 232.63 seconds, consuming much of the 300-second limit. The specified single hit against a lone boss remains intact.

Next, record interruption reasons alongside active threats and survival responses, and connect remaining core policies such as M04 while checking for unnecessary repeated preparation cancellation. Separate time spent reaching the boss from single-boss damage. The selected sample is not a population win-rate estimate; affix weights and damage multipliers were not retuned.

Raw data is Artifacts/Validation/EdictChain/Diagnostic1/runs.jsonl, with matched summaries in diagnostic-summary.json. The isolated-project entry point is Hellscript.Editor.BuildIntegrationValidation.RunChainDiagnostics, accepting -hellscriptAuditStage, -hellscriptChainSeeds and -hellscriptAuditOutput. Existing output directories are not overwritten.

Validation and executable

The final 292-test focused run and 1,566-test full Edit Mode suite passed. The full suite ran from 2026-09-12 15:56:55 to 16:01:59 UTC in 304.19 seconds, with zero failures or skips. New coverage includes 51 M03 cases and one observer noninterference case. Integration includes an actual Frost Nova granting two charges, followed by two Chain Lightning casts consuming one each and producing seven hits apiece.

The first focused run passed 289 of 290 tests. Its single failure came from incompatible corridor data retained in a synthetic sight-blocking fixture. The fixture was corrected; actual Nova integration and observer coverage were added before the passing final run. The initial failed report is preserved.

Native macOS checkResult
Editing and persistenceActual buttons selected SAVE_CHARGE, SUPPORT and TOTAL_HITS. The saved source stayed unchanged while editing; memory and a fresh file read matched after applying. An actual button enabled the edict.
Charge hold and startOne uncharged target held the cast. Supplying a short-lived fixture charge and linked enemies selected a support first target and consumed one charge at preparation start. Actual Frost Nova charge generation was separately verified in Edit Mode.
Independent process restartELITE/OFF was saved during preparation before exiting. Restart restored the original first target, resource, time and reserved bonus, producing one seven-hit release. Each enemy received at most two nonconsecutive hits. No duplicate payment, extra charge consumption or new OFF-state cast occurred.
Layout and pauseKorean/English and 140% text were checked at 1280×720, 720×1280 and 640×360. Text-height, missing-translation and footer safe-area checks passed. Closing translated decision screens preserved running and manually paused entry states.

The first native attempt exited because its new command-line flag collided with an existing rift-objective smoke flag. The new smoke now uses -hellscriptChainEdictSmoke and -hellscriptChainEdictResume. The final build and both Native2 processes passed from 2026-09-12 15:58:14 to 15:58:34 UTC. Those two smoke flag names are the only difference between the full-suite/diagnostic source and the final app source; the variant is preserved explicitly. Combat and UI behavior did not change after the full suite began.

Ten screenshots were retained. Enlarged English options, compact landscape options, Korean restored decisions and the post-restart combat screen were visually inspected. Inputs use actual UI callbacks with controlled combat placement and time. This is not mobile-device touch, rotation or performance evidence.

The app is Builds/macOS-EdictChain/HELLSCRIPT.app, with evidence under Artifacts/Validation/EdictChain/. All 242 C#/English-table inputs, including 172 Runtime C# files, match the final build source. No C# metadata is missing and no asset GUID is duplicated. validated-source.tar.gz preserves 653 source/design-input/authored-setting files, including the old smoke-flag variant. SHA-256: 55cec1caeb98aa741755e80e16714679c1e000e213b22e13368e21b56090cbd2. Unity-added URP Editor version metadata in the validation copy's material is recorded separately; the authored asset is preserved.

Remaining work

Next: connect remaining fixed policies such as M04 and record the reasons for interrupted preparation. Investigate Chain Control's boss-arrival time alongside survival responses and interrupted attacks. Multi-stage progression and farming value, remaining legendary/set equipment boundaries, mobile execution and overall release quality remain open.

pages.body:
# Character Plaza art handoff

2026-10-14 · [한국어](CharacterPlaza_Art_20261014.md)

The [design README](../Design/CharacterPlaza/README.md) and [source art README](../Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/CharacterPlaza/README.md) remain authoritative. This handoff covers source assets and static checks. Unity import, actual presentation, interaction and memory measurements await the single integration run.

## Delivered files and provenance

`Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Art/CharacterPlaza/` contains 41 PNG textures, two scene JSON files and `art.json`. Two background PNGs and twelve pose PNGs preserve their original bytes. Twelve subject cutouts, twelve clean-plate patches and three crest crops decode the existing authored WebP pixels into PNG. Full clean plates and the obsolete equipment atlas are excluded from Resources.

Run [prepare_character_plaza_art.py](../../tools/prepare_character_plaza_art.py) with `--from-webp` to reproduce this delivery, or `--verify` for read-only checks. The [receipt](../../tools/character_plaza_art_receipt.json) records all original/output SHA256 values, paths, GUIDs and processing.

Native regeneration was attempted first. `lift.swift` compiled successfully, but the first landscape `warrior_m` extraction failed with macOS Vision Code 9: `Could not build inference plan / failed to load ANE model`. Portrait extraction was not started. The authorized authored-WebP fallback was then used. PNG decoding cannot recover detail already lost in WebP compression; check cutout/background edge seams in Unity. No new image generation occurred.

## Runtime contract

Scene coordinates use a top-left origin. `scene_landscape` and `scene_portrait` provide `width`, `height`, `background`, `heroes[]` and `focus[]`. Each hero contains `artId`, resource and x/y/width/height in `cut` and `patch`, `headX/Y`, `feetX/Y` and `cheerHeight`. All twelve hero rectangles, anchors and portrait focus entries match authored `scene_data.json` exactly. Art IDs named `archer_*` map to `HeroClass.Ranger`.

`art.json` provides `poses[]` containing six art IDs and their cheer/fight resource, UV rectangle and trimmed dimensions; `crests[]` contains `heroClass` and `resource`. Pose UV bounds use alpha > 8 because very faint source pixels extend to the image edge. PNG bytes remain unchanged. UV y uses Unity's bottom origin.

Twenty-four baked 64×64 hit masks cover twelve cutouts and twelve poses. Base64 rows run from top to bottom; bits are little-endian within each byte. Runtime texture CPU reads are unnecessary. New deterministic UUIDv5 GUIDs and `.meta` files specify GPU-only textures, disabled mipmaps, Clamp and Bilinear sampling.

## Budget requested from the common owner

PNG files total **31,524,964 bytes (30.07 MiB)**. Full-size uncompressed RGBA would total 95,228,440 bytes. The capped ASTC6×6 estimate is 5,956,496 bytes (5.68 MiB), which is not a measured Unity resident-memory result.

The common `ResourceTextureBudget.cs` was not edited. Request these prefixes in order: `landscape_bg` and `portrait_bg` at 2048; `cheer_` and `fight_` at 1024; `crest_` at 256; remaining `Art/CharacterPlaza/` at 512. New metadata already uses these caps with Android ASTC6×6, Standalone BC7 and WebGL ETC2_RGBA8.

## Pixel review and remaining differences

All 28 reference JPEGs were visually inspected through four contact sheets, including landscape/portrait/PC, KO/EN and every supplied browse/new/created/gear/entering/rift state. Both source scenes and all twelve pose images were also viewed. The contacts are review aids, not replacement reference images.

The source composition retains warriors at the tavern, rangers at the fruit stall, and mages at the distant magic shop. Portrait focus uses Mage/Ranger/Warrior crests, a cream top mist and pose swaps. The documented 1.2× mage focus softness remains. The six cheer poses are unarmed; the six fight poses have fixed illustrated swords, bows or staves. They do not dynamically depict arbitrary equipped-item appearances. The female warrior fight pose uses a sword rather than her model sheet's axe. All twelve poses have maximum alpha 254; faint alpha speckles and existing edge contacts remain in the originals.

Vision-derived cutouts are not native alpha. Every record remains `productionApproved:false`; the female warrior outfit retains the source brief's age-rating review requirement.

The separately approved six standing portraits under `2026-10-13/task-4/output/hellscript-main-characters-6/delivery/` were verified against `DIRECTOR_STATUS.json` and `FINAL_MAIN_CHARACTERS_QA.json`: six exact hashes matched, and the light-background contact pixels were viewed. Their exact hashes are listed in the Korean companion. These portraits were not substituted for the new natural town activities.

Old `Art/CharacterSelection/{Warrior,Mage,Ranger}` atlases remain shared through `CharacterEquipmentView` and `CharacterFigure.Load`, including blacksmith consumers. Preserve them. Preserve `SelectionCourtyard` until reference and actual-screen replacement checks finish. No old resource, metadata, history or 3D hero asset was moved or deleted.

## Validation and retention

Static checks passed for 17 original hashes, 41 runtime hashes/GUIDs, 12 scene layouts, 24 masks, six pose pairs, three crests, GPU-only/mipmap settings and exclusion of full clean plates. Unity runs: zero. Integration owns the final build, save and input checks.

The temporary Swift binary, module cache, failure input, review contacts and results remain under `validation/character-plaza-art/` with an artifact lifecycle record. No Unity/game/web build, commit, push, merge or permanent deletion was performed.

pages.body:
# Character create/select screen (town scene): Codex task brief

Written: 2026-10-14 · [한국어](Casual_Character_Plaza_Codex_Prompt_20261014.md)

Paste the whole code block below into Codex. The mockup, pictures and tools are on the `claude/casual-art-concept` branch (pushed to the remote; the local worktree for it is `/Users/t8g-2410-pn-005/Documents/MyProject/HELLSCRIPT/wt-casual-art`).

| What to hand over | Where |
|---|---|
| Design page (28 boards, private) | https://claude.ai/artifact/M43Cy6wg7BJUqpKxofu21M — Codex can open it only if the user shares it. If it cannot, the repository copy below is enough |
| Authoritative mockup (published source, 28 reference renders, specification, copy, check tools) | `Docs/Design/CharacterPlaza/` ([README](../Design/CharacterPlaza/README.en.md)) |
| Art originals, prompts and the scene lifting tool | `Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/CharacterPlaza/` ([README](../Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/CharacterPlaza/README.en.md)) |
| This brief | this document |

**Decision made:** Decision 1 (the save structure) was settled by the user on 2026-10-14 as **Option A, six saved heroes**. If the user wants to change any of the other defaults in the "Decisions" section below, they can tell Codex.

```text
Replace HELLSCRIPT's character selection screen (page "characters") with the new "character create/select screen". After login (or guest entry), one screen lets the player create a character that has not been created yet and enter with a created one. The pictures already exist. This task puts the screen, its state rules, its copy and its verification into the game. The save structure follows the user's settled "Decision 1" (six saved heroes).

## Background
- The game art moves from dark gothic to a bright casual look (style D, ages 12+). Each class now has two genders, so there are six heroes (warrior, ranger, mage, each male and female). There is no nickname field (the nickname is created later, in a tutorial once the player has progressed).
- It is a homage to the Dungeons & Dragons arcade character select: before setting off, the party hangs out in town and each hero does something believable at a believable place (the warriors on a tavern terrace with a tankard and a drumstick, the rangers haggling at a fruit stall, the mages with a book and a potion at a magic shop). The user once rejected a staged formation as unnatural, so follow the mockup's scene exactly.
- Concept record: Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/Casual_Art_Concept_20261013(.en).md (section "Character create/select screen: town scene" on that branch).

## First
1. Rules: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, AgentRules/ (Shared_UI, UI_Refresh, Workflow, CPU_Performance, Unity_MCP, Wiki_Publish, Equipment_Comparison). One task, one agent. Conversation and development notes in Korean; code comments, commit messages and logs in English.
2. Create new branches as worktrees from the latest origin/main (other sessions use the same checkout): codex/casual-hero-slots for PR 1 (save structure) and codex/casual-character-plaza for PR 2 (the new screen), which starts on top of PR 1 or from main after PR 1 merges. Bring the mockup and the art onto the PR 2 branch:
   git fetch origin claude/casual-art-concept && git checkout origin/claude/casual-art-concept -- Docs/Design/CharacterPlaza Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/CharacterPlaza Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/Casual_Art_Concept_20261013.md Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/Casual_Art_Concept_20261013.en.md
   (main has not touched those two concept documents, and that branch merges into main cleanly.)
3. Read Docs/Design/CharacterPlaza/README.en.md to the end and open the 28 reference renders in reference/. That document is authoritative for screen rules, specification, copy and state transitions; the text below is a summary. node Docs/Design/CharacterPlaza/tools/smoke.js is the mockup's state-flow check (the source of the flow to port into game tests).

## Current state (main 305744d3, code read directly)
- Screen: Presentation/GameUI.CharacterSelection.cs (ShowCharacterSelection, page id "characters", backdrop TitleAtmosphere + Art/CharacterSelection/SelectionCourtyard), CharacterSelectionView.cs, CharacterSelectionStage.cs (movement, poses and idle of three heroes), CharacterFigure.cs (transparent-image click mask), state Core/CharacterSelectionState.cs (preview, rift-owner lock LockedHero), commit Presentation/GameController.CharacterSelection.cs (CommitEntryCharacter, EnterFirstStart, SaveEntryCharacter). Art Resources/Art/CharacterSelection/ (Warrior, Mage, Ranger atlases + SelectionCourtyard.png), check tool tools/inspect_character_atlases.py, evidence Docs/Implementation/CharacterSelectionEvidence/, smoke -hellscriptCharacterSelectionSmoke (11 checks), tests Tests/Editor/CharacterSelectionTests.cs, description Docs/Implementation/Character_Selection(.en).md.
- The first start skips this screen: GameUI.OpenCharacterSelection calls EnterFirstStart when GuideTutorial.FirstStart is true, which enters the warrior at once.
- Saves: AccountSave.heroes is exactly three heroes (the validation at GameStore.cs:66 rejects anything else on load). HeroClass is { Warrior, Ranger, Mage }, and many places use the hero index as the class index (selectedHero 245 places in 146 files, heroes[ ] / heroes.Count 150 places in 92 files, class-index casts 218 places in 124 files). The hero id (HeroSave.id) separates tutorial slots (Tutorials.Switch/Take/Park) and the rift in progress (suspendedRun.heroId). HeroSave has neither a gender nor a "created" flag. The art name archer is HeroClass.Ranger in code. Do not create a new class or save ID.
- Equipment: per hero, the equipped items of HeroSave.inventory. Shared parts CharacterEquipmentView.Create(parent, HeroSave hero, ...), EquipmentSlotView, ItemDetailView. Caution: CharacterEquipmentView's hero picture is the old dark class atlas (CharacterFigure.Load(heroClass)), which would clash with the new look if dropped into this popup.
- Touch targets stay at 44 pt (commit 9697bd9e). The mockup's + button (32 / 38 px) and person button (28 / 32 px) are smaller, so keep the visible size and enlarge only the hit area to at least 44 pt.
- Copy: the Korean source text is the key and Resources/Localization/en.txt holds the tab-separated English. A missing key shows Korean instead and is recorded; never show an empty string or a key name.

## Screen requirements (mockup summary; exact numbers in the README)
- Scene: the six heroes stand in one town scene, each in their own spot: the male and female warrior on the tavern terrace in front, the rangers at the fruit stall in the middle, the mages at the magic shop by the fountain in the back. Landscape (956×440) and PC (1152×648) cover the frame with the whole scene. Portrait (440×956) uses the scene redrawn tall; the three crests on the right (mage, ranger, warrior from top to bottom, 65 px, centred on the screen height, 112 px apart) move the camera to that class's pair and zoom in (0.9 s). Choosing a hero makes the camera follow its class.
- The top has only "‹ 타이틀" and the heading "나만의 모험가를 골라요". There are no motion or language buttons on this screen (user decision: the game always plays the motion and the language is changed in Settings). This screen does not read TitleSession.MotionEnabled and always plays. The two buttons on other screens are out of scope.
- Unselected heroes look inactive (saturation .45, brightness .88). Tapping one restores its colour, adds a white outline with a class-coloured glow and puts a class name tag (class name + gender glyph) at its feet.
- Choosing a hero that has not been created shows a green + button above its head. Tapping it hides the painted hero with a background patch, stands the cheer pose (cheer_*) in its place for 1.8 seconds with a speech bubble line that fits the hero, then returns to the original pose; creation is done and a Lv.1 pill plus a person icon appear above the head. The person icon opens the equipped-gear popup (8 slots: weapon, head, chest, hands, feet, belt, amulet, ring). The popup shows what the hero actually wears, drawn with the shared parts.
- Choosing a created hero shows a green "PLAY" at the bottom centre. Pressing it switches the hero to the battle-ready pose (fight_*, equipped weapon) with a personality line, turns the button into a disabled "Entering…" and continues into the existing entry (CommitEntryCharacter -> EnterPlaza(true)).
- While creating or entering, taps on other heroes and crests are ignored.
- With a rift in progress only the hero that owns it can be chosen; the rest show greyscale with a padlock (existing LockedHero rule).
- Nothing is saved while previewing. Save only when "+" creates a hero and when Play confirms entry. On a failed save restore the previous state and show a toast (the existing SaveEntryCharacter way).
- Keep the PC keys (left/right selects, Esc returns to the title, Enter starts when no button is focused) and extend them to cycle the six heroes (front row male and female warrior, middle male and female ranger, back male and female mage).
- Hero lines (created / entering): male warrior "좋아, 한판 붙어 보자고!" / "다 덤벼라! 앞장은 내가 선다!", female warrior "배도 채웠겠다, 덤벼!" / "몸 다 풀렸어. 전부 날려 줄게!", male ranger "흥정 끝! 이제 사냥 시간이야." / "한 발이면 충분하지!", female ranger "조용히, 확실하게. 따라와." / "숨 고르고… 놓치지 않아.", male mage "책에 다 나와 있었다고!" / "계산 끝. 불꽃 맛 좀 봐라!", female mage "반짝반짝, 마법 시작이야!" / "자, 마법 쇼를 시작해 볼까?" (English text and all new copy are in the README's copy table).

## Decisions
Decision 1: settled by the user on 2026-10-14: six saved heroes (Option A, matches the mockup).
- Structure: AccountSave.heroes always holds all six heroes. Indexes 0-2 are the male warrior, ranger and mage exactly as today; 3-5 are the female warrior, ranger and mage. Then assumptions such as heroes[(int)heroClass] stay true for the male heroes, and the hero id (HeroSave.id) and HeroClass stay as they are. Add gender (default male) and created to HeroSave, and add one place that finds a hero index from (class, gender). An uncreated hero exists in the save as a default hero; "+" turns created on and starts that hero's tutorial share the existing way.
- Migration: raise the save schema (GameStore.MaximumSchemaVersion, today 22 with D4 on and 21 in legacy mode). On load, grow a three-hero save to six (the three female heroes are default heroes built like NewAccount does) and mark the existing three as male and created. Keep the original as .schema<N>-before-six-heroes.json like the existing migrations. Change the heroes.Count!=3 check in Read to accept only 3 (an old save to migrate) or 6. The D4 legacy developer mode (schema 21) neither reads nor writes the new save and refuses it while preserving the original (the existing D4 refusal way).
- Audit: classify and change the places that assume "hero index = class index" (selectedHero 245 places, heroes[ ] 150 places, and those of the 218 class-index casts that are really hero indexes). The places I found: GameStore.cs lines 33, 66 and 422, GameStore.CharacterSwitch.cs, Tutorials.cs Switch/Take/Park and GuideTutorial.WarriorIndex, PuzzleTutorial.cs 229 and 240, CombatSimulation.ClassSkillValidation.cs 32, CombatSimulation.SkillPreview.cs 30, CharacterSelectionState.LockedHero. Account-wide loops (daily quests, offline rewards, telemetry, codex, ...) must not touch uncreated heroes. Existing screens that list heroes (the in-game character switch, class buttons, ...) show only created heroes. Fix test assumptions of exactly three heroes.
- Stages (recommended): PR 1 = save structure, migration and tests. The old selection screen shows only created heroes so it behaves as before, and a new account still starts with all three male heroes created as today. PR 2 = the new screen and the new-account default (Decision 2). Write the audit results and the staged plan in the PR description and go ahead (do not wait for an answer). If the impact turns out much larger than expected, stop and report.
- Make the screen read a single "six slots (class, gender, created, level, rift lock, equipped gear)" list instead of the save structure. Until PR 1 is done, fill the slot provider with the mockup's example account (male warrior Lv.24, female ranger Lv.17, female mage Lv.31 with a rift in progress, the other three not created) as a fake and build the screen, state rules and tests first.
Decision 2: first start of a new account (default): EnterFirstStart keeps entering the male warrior at once. pages.body:
```
# Character create/select screen mockup (town scene)

Written: 2026-10-14 · [한국어](README.md)

After login, **creating a character and choosing one to enter with happen on the same screen.** It is a homage to the Dungeons & Dragons arcade games: the party hanging out in town before setting off. The six heroes (warrior, ranger, mage, each male and female) each spend their time believably in a market street.

- Design canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/M43Cy6wg7BJUqpKxofu21M (28 boards, private: Codex cannot open it until the user shares it. The copy in this folder is authoritative)
- Art originals, prompts and the lifting tool: [Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/CharacterPlaza](../../Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/CharacterPlaza/README.en.md)
- Game implementation brief: [Casual_Character_Plaza_Codex_Prompt_20261014.en.md](../../Implementation/Casual_Character_Plaza_Codex_Prompt_20261014.en.md)

## Folder

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `source/` | The files exactly as published to the canvas: one component (`PlazaSelect.dc.html`), 27 thin per-board wrappers and `canvas.json`. Images are referenced as `/_blob/<id>`; `art_map.json` maps them to local files |
| `assets/` | The canvas images (webp): 2 scenes, 12 lifted hero layers, 12 cheer patches, 6 cheer poses, 6 battle-ready poses, 3 crests, 1 equipment icon sheet (the old dark style, mockup only) |
| `reference/` | Renders of the 28 boards (JPEG), the reference for side-by-side comparison with the game screen |
| `scene_data.json` | Picture-pixel data of the two scenes (lifted box per hero, head and feet anchors, cheer box, portrait camera framing), produced by `tools/prep_scene.py` |
| `tools/` | `smoke.js` (state flow and layout checks), `render_reference.js` (reference render), `to_jpg.py` |

## Layout

One component (`source/PlazaSelect.dc.html`) draws every state and size. Props: `locale` (ko, en), `orient` (portrait, landscape, pc), `hero` (none or one of six), `start` (normal, cheer, created, gear, entering, rift), `focus` (portrait camera class). `layout()` is the authority for the layout numbers and `renderVals()` for the state rules.

- **Landscape (956×440) and PC (1152×648 scaled 1.25)**: the whole scene covers the frame. The male and female warrior sit on the tavern terrace in front, the rangers at the fruit stall in the middle, the mages at the magic shop by the fountain in the back.
- **Portrait (440×956)**: a scene redrawn tall. The three crests on the right (mage, ranger, warrior from top to bottom) move the camera to that class's pair and zoom in (0.9 s, `cubic-bezier(.45,.05,.2,1)`). Crests are 65 px, centred on the screen height, 112 px apart; the focused class gets a class-coloured ring and glow. Everything above the focused pair is fogged with cream so two heroes read at a time.
- **Top**: only the back button (‹ Title) and the heading. **There are no motion or language buttons** (user decision: the game always plays the motion and the language is changed in Settings).
- **Bottom**: a hint pill before a choice; the green Play button at the centre once a created hero is chosen.

## States and transitions

| State | What shows | Next |
|---|---|---|
| Browsing | All six inactive (saturation .45, brightness .88). Hint "Tap a hero to choose" | Tap a hero -> selected |
| Selected (never played) | White outline plus class-coloured glow, a class name tag at the feet (class name and gender glyph), a green + button above the head. Hint "Tap + to create this adventurer". No Play | Tap + -> cheer |
| Cheer (create) | The painted hero is hidden with a background patch and the cheer pose stands in its place. 1.8 s hop (1.7 s animation) with a speech bubble line that fits the hero | After 1.8 s the hero returns to its pose, creation is done -> Lv.1 |
| Selected (created) | Lv. pill and a person icon above the head, Play at the bottom centre. Hint "Enter the sanctuary with your selected character." | Person icon -> gear popup, Play -> entering |
| Gear popup | A centred panel with 8 equipped slots (weapon, head, chest, hands, feet, belt, amulet, ring; name, slot, level, grade colour). Close at the top right | Close |
| Entering | The painted hero is hidden and a battle-ready pose with the equipped weapon stands in; a speech bubble line; the Play button turns into a disabled "Entering..."; a light cream veil covers the screen. Hint "Entering sanctuary..." | Enter the game |
| Rift in progress | Only the rift hero can be chosen (the mockup uses the female mage, Lv.31); the rest are greyscale with a padlock. Hint "Continue with the character in your active rift." | Play |

While creating or entering, other heroes and the crests ignore taps. Choosing a hero makes the portrait camera follow its class.

## Specification

- Colours: ink #2a3150, cream #fff6e3. Class colours (ring / text / soft fill): warrior #ff9f1c / #e08a00 / #fff1d6, ranger #4cbf55 / #2a8a36 / #e5f7e0, mage #35a7ff / #1f7fd1 / #e3f2ff. Play button #8ee07a -> #4cbf55 with a 3 px ink border and a 4 px hard shadow, white text with a 2 px ink outline. Heading yellow #ffd23f with an ink outline. Fonts are Jua (heading, numbers, buttons) and Noto Sans KR (body); in the game use the fonts `UiTheme` owns.
- Name tag 96×22 (landscape), 108×24 (portrait, PC). Row above the head: + button 32 (landscape) / 38, level pill height 26 / 30, person button 28 / 32, speech bubble max width 200 / 210 with 13 / 15 px text. The row is clamped to stay on screen (centre 112 to W-112 in landscape, 118 and up elsewhere) and below the heading row (landscape 60, portrait 160, PC 108).

- Timings: cheer 1.8 s (hop 1.7 s), battle-ready bounce 0.55 s, speech bubble pop 0.5 s, + button bob 1.2 s loop, Play shine 5.6 s loop, portrait camera 0.9 s.
- Mockup example account: male warrior Lv.24, female ranger Lv.17, female mage Lv.31 (rift in progress); the other three are not created. The gear popup's names, levels and icons are placeholders; the game shows the gear the hero actually wears through the shared components.

# Character create/select screen, town scene: art originals

Written: 2026-10-14 · [한국어](README.md)

The screen mockup and its rules are in [Docs/Design/CharacterPlaza](../../../../Design/CharacterPlaza/README.en.md). This folder holds the original pictures made by Codex, their prompts and manifests, and the tool that lifts the heroes out of the scene. The concept record is the section "Character create/select screen: town scene" in [Casual_Art_Concept_20261013.en.md](../Casual_Art_Concept_20261013.en.md).

## Files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `scene_landscape.png` · `scene_portrait.png` | The town scene with the six heroes in it (1536×1024, 1024×1536), each at their own place: tavern terrace (male and female warrior), fruit stall (male and female ranger), magic shop (male and female mage) |
| `clean_landscape.png` · `clean_portrait.png` | The same scene without the heroes (it hides the painted hero during the cheer and battle-ready poses) |
| `cheer_<hero>.png` ×6 | Cheer poses (no weapon, transparent background, 1024×1536) |
| `fight_<hero>.png` ×6 | Battle-ready poses with the equipped weapon (warrior sword, ranger bow, mage crystal staff; transparent background, 1024×1536). The male ranger's "aiming the bow" request was blocked by the Codex safety filter, so he holds the bow with a thumbs-up |
| `crests.png` | The three class crests (warrior, ranger, mage) on one picture; the mockup cuts it into three |
| `PROMPT_*.md` · `manifest_*.json` | The request prompts and records of source path, SHA-256 and size. The tool does not report a model name, so model is `unknown` |
| `tools/` | `lift.swift` (macOS Vision subject lifting), `prep_scene.py` (layer maker), `spec_landscape.json` · `spec_portrait.json` (crop ranges and seed points per hero) |

`PROMPT_cheer_*.md` also describes a prop pose requested in the same run for the first attempt (heroes with props on an empty plaza); those pictures were dropped. `PROMPT_fight_rangers.md` is the run where the male ranger request was blocked and only the female ranger came out; the male ranger was requested again with `PROMPT_fight_archer_m.md`.

## Rebuilding the layers

```bash
swiftc -O tools/lift.swift -o tools/lift
python3 tools/prep_scene.py tools/spec_landscape.json --out /tmp/plaza --format png
python3 tools/prep_scene.py tools/spec_portrait.json  --out /tmp/plaza --format png
```

For each picture this writes `<pic>_bg` (the scene), `<pic>_cut_<hero>` (the hero lifted from the scene), `<pic>_patch_<hero>` (the clean plate piece at the hero's place) and `scn_<pic>.json` (coordinates). It was checked to produce the same boxes and anchors as the already published canvas (all 12 heroes match).

- Screen data: in `scn_*.json`, `cut` is the lifted hero's place in the scene, `head` and `feet` are the anchors for the name tag, speech bubble and pose pictures, `cheer` is the box a pose picture stands in (feet x, feet y, height), `patch` is where the covering piece goes. The portrait camera framing is `focus` (per class: x, y, zoom, screen x).
- The pose pictures (`cheer_*`, `fight_*`) are originals with transparent margins. Trim them to the alpha bounds, centre the feet on `feet` and set the height to `cheer[2]`.

## Processing and rules

- The hero layers are cut from the scene with macOS Vision subject lifting, so they are **not native alpha**. That differs from the repository art rule (no chroma key or background removal, original alpha). When importing into the game, register them as replaceable development art (`productionApproved: false`) and write this processing into the provenance. Replace them with 3D heroes and animation or native-alpha pictures before release.
- The scenes and pose pictures are Codex's original pixels (no post-processing). The model name is unknown (`unknown`); the C2PA chunk records the generation tool.
- The female warrior's outfit (bare midriff) needs a 12+ rating check. The male warrior's tankard stays (user decision).
