# Character creation and selection handoff — 2026-10-14

[Korean details](Character_Plaza_Handoff_20261014.md) · [Save audit](Character_Plaza_Save_Audit_20261014.en.md) · [Art provenance](CharacterPlaza_Art_20261014.en.md)

## Delivery and dependency order

The approved six-hero save model and casual village screen are implemented in the isolated `task-21/character-plaza` source workspace, branch `codex/casual-character-plaza`. The original checkout, real saves and other Chrome profiles were not modified. No Library/Builds/Temp clone, remote PR, push, main merge or web deployment occurred.

Apply `e38096240d1d54f680204212f583340708d798e0` → `93219e3fef4f7a07f2e3249b9598b1e0e7f014a8` → common integration `4148241a` → this PR2 commit. PR2 directly descends from `4148241a`. Integration owner task-6/skill-skin waits for this source and the basic HUD handoff before one final Unity validation.

`HeroSlots.Index(class,gender)`, `Created(account)` and `IsCreated(account,index)` are stable. Slots0–2 are male Warrior/Ranger/Mage;3–5 are female counterparts. Schema23 archives three-hero input byte-for-byte before migration and preserves IDs/progress/equipment. An existing archive with different bytes refuses migration without replacing either file. New production accounts create only the male Warrior, preserving first-start direct entry. Later logins create the other five. Fresh legacy developer accounts keep the original three heroes and reject schema23 reads/writes.

The screen supports browse/select, 1.8-second cheer, atomic creation with rollback/retry, level/equipment, battle-ready speech and existing `CommitEntryCharacter → EnterPlaza(true)`. Preview/camera/equipment never save. Busy input and suspended-rift ownership are enforced. Keyboard order is Warrior male/female, Ranger male/female, Mage male/female.

## Implementation boundary

`CharacterSelectionState` owns pure phases, timing and12 personality lines; `CharacterPlazaSlots` is the screen's store boundary. `CharacterPlazaStage` aligns background/cutouts/patches with one transform, interpolates portrait class focus over0.9 seconds, and uses baked64×64 input masks with GPU-only textures. One shader and six material instances provide inactive/locked/selected appearance. There are no per-frame save/JSON/list rebuilds and no measured performance claim.

`CharacterSelectionView(.Equipment)` explicitly consumes `UiSkin.Casual.WithEquipmentArt(CasualEquipmentArt.Provider)` and shared fonts/buttons/StorageSurface/ContentWindowView/EquipmentSlotView/ItemDetailView. Eight equipment categories retain both hands and both rings inside their existing categories. Shared Escape consumption prevents closing equipment and returning to title with one key. Resize includes Canvas scale; create/equipment hit rectangles retain a minimum44 screen units on both axes.

PR2 owns the character page/controller partials, created-only gendered settings/legacy town lists, and Hunt Edict preview gender fallback. Item ownership integrity continues across all six bags. Common commit4148241a owns `GameController.SelectHero`, D4 host/class availability and the41-texture budget; those files are not duplicated here.

## Reference, assets and differences

The requested MD was absent at the original path, so the authoritative sibling wt-casual-art commit13a1ce7322ae69f5b518503b52598fbadf7ee5b8 was used; MD SHA256 c1ad2137e8f6f81a3e319dbbacea33ac102428e45175ea0012666bb3ff523f6f. Chrome's Hoosung Lee / dakrdong@gmail.com profile was verified in UI before using only that window. The Claude artifact title loaded but its content timed out twice (one retry). The MD explicitly permits the local28-board/source fallback, which was inspected.

The explicit character brief replaces the old three-actor geometry with village coordinates and class cameras; this exception to the general skin geometry rule was reported to integration. Layout adapts440×956 portrait,956×440 short landscape and1152×648 PC design units to safe areas. The equipment grid uses2/4 columns; displaying both real hands/rings and shared detail extends the single-item examples in the mockup.

All17 original PNG hashes and the separately approved six hero portraits/pixels were checked. Two backgrounds and12 poses preserve original PNG bytes. Vision compiled but first extraction failed with ANE Code9, so authored WebP cutouts/patches/crests were decoded to PNG. No new image generation occurred. Runtime assets are under `Resources/Art/CharacterPlaza/`:41 PNGs,31,524,964 bytes. Originals, metadata and old assets remain intact. The old CharacterSelection resource family is about9.23MB and still has shared equipment-atlas consumers; cleanup awaits actual-screen validation.

Remaining visual checks: Unity pixel comparison, WebP cutout seams, enlarged mage softness, shared font wrapping/long equipment names,44-unit targets and popup safe areas. Fixed painted battle weapons do not depict arbitrary equipped appearances; the female Warrior battle pose uses a sword instead of her model-sheet axe. Village/pose art remains **productionApproved:false**, and her exposed midriff requires the brief's **age12 rating review**.

## Verification and integration entry

[Static evidence](CharacterPlazaSourceEvidence20261014/summary.json) records exact scope: Runtime/Editor/Tests Roslyn compilation with zero errors; UI contract15 cases; refresh16 bindings;17 original/41 runtime hashes, new GUIDs,12 layouts and24 masks;22 new Korean keys and8 retired lines. The reference Node smoke passes912 combinations/28 boards; it does not execute the Unity implementation.

**Unity import, shader compilation, EditMode execution, player execution, physical-device checks and performance measurements: zero.** Fifteen save tests, state/asset tests and the new runtime smoke were authored and compiled only. Real saves and network accounts were not used.

After all sources freeze, include `HeroSlotsTests`, `CharacterSelectionTests`, `LocalizationTests`, `BuildResourceTests`, `TutorialHeroSlotsTests`, `SettingsRevisionTests` and D4 host checks in the single full EditMode pass. Run the same development build with `-hellscriptCharacterSelectionSmoke -hellscriptSavePath <fresh disposable save> -hellscriptScreenshots <evidence> -hellscriptServerBase invalid -nosound`. The smoke requires one created male Warrior, creates the other five, enters the female Mage, and captures five ratios, KO/EN, equipment/rotation and rift locks. Google authentication remains in its established account-validation path. Native input and side-by-side reference review remain required; desktop simulated insets are not physical-device validation.

After source freeze the integration owner owns further changes. Local validation logs, compiler inputs, contacts and failed Swift evidence remain under `validation/` with the parent artifact lifecycle record. No permanent deletion occurred.

# Character plaza save audit — 2026-10-14

[Korean and exact integration edits](Character_Plaza_Save_Audit_20261014.md)

PR1 implements the approved six-hero contract in the isolated source workspace. Schema 23 keeps male Warrior/Ranger/Mage at indices 0–2 and female counterparts at 3–5. Hero IDs and class IDs remain stable. `HeroSlots.Index`, `Created`, and `IsCreated` own mapping and eligibility. The default `NewAccount` factory keeps three created male heroes; PR2 opts the production constructor into `onlyWarriorCreated:true`.

Three-hero input is archived byte-for-byte as `.schema<N>-before-six-heroes.json` before mutation. Archive failure stops loading. Existing heroes become explicitly male and created; female defaults use the same catalog-aware factory as new accounts. Legacy developer mode remains schema 21 and rejects newer/six-slot reads and writes before normalization or temporary-file writes, without falling back to an older backup. Detached sandbox fixtures expand without disk access.

`CreateCharacter(index)` uses the existing staged transaction, starts and parks the hero's tutorial share through `Tutorials.Switch`, restores current selection/share, and adopts only after a successful write. Duplicate creation, switching to uncreated slots, and creation during a suspended rift are refused. Class-equality fallbacks now include gender; replay kits use their real gender slot.

Created-only aggregation covers unlocks, first-clear rewards, recommendations, operations rewards, rune grades, tutorial history/exemption and skill activation. Daily quests and telemetry reject uncreated selected heroes; codex, offline supplies and repeat state preserve ID ownership and reject uncreated owners. D4 allocation, Hunt Edict editing and potion preparation reject hidden uncreated targets. Queued forge jobs reject uncreated owners and do not settle for them. All six slots still undergo item/ownership/reference integrity checks. The attendance seed still uses the original first hero ID.

The shared UI owner must update settings/legacy character lists, the controller’s hardcoded index clamp, the Hunt Edict preview fallback, and D4 host class lookup. `Single(class)` is invalid with six heroes; select the active matching hero ID or a created same-class fallback and disable unavailable class tabs. The Korean record provides exact locations and proposed substitutions. Character selection state/UI tests belong to PR2.

Validation: `git diff --check` passed. Thirteen focused `HeroSlotsTests` were authored for migration, exact backup preservation, archive failure, creation rollback/retry, female ownership, lock rules, aggregate/queued forge exclusion and legacy rejection. Existing schema/count/refund/tutorial assertions were adapted. **No Unity compilation, EditMode execution, runtime smoke, physical-device checks or performance measurement was performed.** Integrate PR1, shared UI dependencies and PR2 before the single final validation. No original checkout, real saves, Library or build outputs were touched.


## PR2 follow-through

The production constructor now opts into a single created male Warrior when D4 is enabled. Fresh legacy developer accounts retain three created heroes, since legacy mode has no six-slot creation command. `GameStore.NewAccount` keeps its three-created-male default for explicit existing-account fixtures. Existing multi-hero tests now call `ContentTestAccounts.ExistingMaleRoster` at the point that prerequisite is needed; first-start, creation and migration expectations remain separate. Two cross-hero unlock fixtures were also corrected after independent review. Two additional `HeroSlotsTests` cases cover the production/legacy first-account split and a different existing migration archive (15 total). These tests compile but await Unity execution.

PR2 supplies the settings and legacy town roster (created heroes only, with gender), plus the Hunt Edict preview gender fallback. Item integrity still traverses all six owned bags. Integration owns `GameController.SelectHero`, D4 class host/tabs and the texture budget.

pages.body:
# Class skill trees and progression

Updated: 2026-10-07 · [한국어](Class_Skill_Trees.md)

Each class now has **16 normal actives, 19 passives and two ultimates: 37 skills**. We reviewed direct effect dependencies across the original 108 skills and split each dual-ultimate support passive into two dedicated passives. One addition per class brings the total to 111.

[Warrior HTML](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/Warrior.html) · [Ranger HTML](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/Ranger.html) · [Mage HTML](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/Mage.html)


**Native integration:** [Hunt Edict](../Implementation/Hunt_Edict_Skill_Tree.en.md) uses four normal active slots plus a separate ultimate slot, with all unlocked passives always active. The original HTML slot model below is historical prototype context, not the current game rule.

Native update, 2026-09-28: the first three actives of every class unlock at level 1. Zero-rank allocation and the starting-point refund after an explicit reset follow the [runtime integration record](../Implementation/Hunt_Edict_Skill_Tree.en.md). The free-base-rank description below documents older builds and the HTML prototype.

Native update, 2026-09-29: the skill catalog now also unlocks all three first-row actives at level 1. A new character starts with no learned skill and uses only basic attacks; the one point it has at level 1 learns one first-row active. Existing characters keep their allocation.

## 2026-10-07: no more "this or that" prerequisites

The user pointed out that choice prerequisites ("unlock skill A or skill B") make the skill tree messier. The ten skills that had one (`oneOf`: Warrior WP11, WP17; Ranger AP11, AP12, AP13, AP16; Mage MP07, MP08, MP10, MP11) now require **one skill**. When an effect reads several skills, the one already on the same branch is required and the others stay as optional targets mentioned only in the effect text.

- Nine of them already had the chosen skill in their parent chain, so who can unlock what, and when, is unchanged. Only Ranger AP12 lost its trap condition (only Retreat Leap A04 is needed). Traps sit in another branch and could not be linked; without a trap the effect simply never triggers.
- The `optional` table in `audit-dependencies.cjs` adds the required skill and the optional targets and compares the total with the direct targets in the source text; the build refuses any new choice prerequisite.
- The ultimate gate ("one skill from the preceding stage") has no branch link and is a design rule, so it is unchanged.

## 2026-10-06 escape unlocks

Ranger Retreat Leap (A04) and Mage Teleport (M04) open at hero **level 5**. Warrior Leap Slam (W02) remains at level 1. The two movement roots move into their first bands while descendant levels and prerequisites remain unchanged. [Implementation](../Implementation/Escape_Skill_Unlock_Level.en.md).

## 2026-10-05: branch parents and a clean link layout

The user asked for the links in the skill tree to stop looking arbitrary and to read like the Diablo 2, 3 and 4 trees, with a clear before-and-after order. Until now 70 independent skills (about 23 per class) opened on level alone and hung from the branch trunk, while links existed only for the few skills whose effects read each other. This request replaces the earlier rule below that shared branch membership is not a dependency: **branches now have parent skills**.

- **One parent per skill.** Every skill except the ultimates has one parent (`lineage`) in its own branch. Each class has four starting skills (Warrior W01, W02, W03, W05; Ranger A01, A02, A03, A04; Mage M01, M02, M03, M04). The result is a tree that only forks and never merges: each of the 93 skills that has a parent draws exactly one link.
- **No unlock level changes.** A parent never opens later than its child, so the level table is untouched and the only new rule is that the parent must be open. It does not require spending points on the parent first (the same open-or-not test the effect prerequisites already use).
- **Effect prerequisites are audited as before.** The direct relations (`all`; no `oneOf` since 2026-10-07) are still compared with the source text by the independent validator. The structural parent is a separate field and never counts as effect evidence; when an effect prerequisite already is the parent it is not recorded twice. An effect prerequisite that is an ancestor of the parent is not drawn again (transitive reduction), so Hold Formation WP16 hangs from its nearby parent instead of a distant Whirlwind W01.
- **Hand-set layout, tool-checked.** The socket grid in `tree-design.cjs` (branch × stage × row, two columns per row) sets positions, and `tree-layout.cjs` refuses to build when a link would cross a skill, run upward, leave its branch or share a socket. The HTML planner and the game (`row`, `col`, `links` and `via` in `ClassSkillTree.json`) use the same layout.
- **Ultimates keep the shared gate.** They have no branch link, only "level 40 plus one preceding-stage skill". Only each ultimate's dedicated passive hangs directly below it.
- **Effect targets in another branch are not linked.** A direct target in a different branch, such as the trap requirement of Prepared Escape AP12, is listed in the detail panel only.

| Class | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Starting skills (no parent) | 12 |
| Effect prerequisite only (the effect target is the parent) | 18 |
| Structural parent only | 58 |
| Effect prerequisite and structural parent | 17 |
| Ultimates (shared gate) | 6 |

## Dedicated ultimate support

| Class | Ultimate | Dedicated passive | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Warrior | War of the Ancestors W17 | Ancestral Legacy WP18 | Resources on ancestor hits |
| Warrior | Titan's Judgment W18 | Titan's Bulwark WP19 · new | Barrier per directly hit enemy |
| Ranger | Killing Rain A17 | Silent Execution AP18 | Extra damage to a marked first-wave target |
| Ranger | Shadow Pursuit A18 | Relentless Pursuit AP19 · new | Two extra seconds and two extra total procs |
| Mage | Triune Collapse M17 | Archmage's Testament MP18 | Resources on a third-stage hit |
| Mage | Sage Incarnate M18 | Sage's Ward MP19 · new | Add 10% maximum HP to its barrier |

All six passives require **level 40 and unlocked base rank 1 of their own ultimate** in the HTML planner. The other ultimate cannot unlock them. Each is placed immediately below its matching ultimate. Existing magnitudes are divided between dedicated effects without duplication or increases.

## Progression and dependency rules

Levels 1–9 establish foundations, 10–19 survival and resource management, 20–29 status and placed-effect combinations, 30–39 advanced builds, and 40 ultimates and their dedicated passives.

**35 skills use level plus direct effect targets/triggers** and **six ultimates use the shared stage gate**. The other 70 independent skills now also need their branch parent to be open, except the 12 starting skills (section above). General mark, barrier, health, or BASIC conditions do not force an arbitrary source skill. Equipment-only additions do not become base skill prerequisites.

General passives with multiple actual targets accept one unlocked target. Prepared Escape AP12 additionally requires Retreat Leap A04, whose cooldown it reduces, and one triggering trap. The default view draws the 93 branch links from the section above, and a selected skill additionally lights its effect prerequisites and followers. Details list every actual target and keep the structural parent apart from effect prerequisites, which are never mixed.

Ultimates retain **level 40 plus any unlocked skill from the same class's preceding level 30–39 stage**. Any active, passive or branch qualifies without equipping it. No individual candidate wires are drawn for this shared gate.

Base rank 1 unlocks free when conditions are met. Earn one upgrade point per level after level 1, reaching 39 at level 40. Normal skills cap at rank 5 and ultimates at rank 1. No extra prerequisite ranks or arbitrary cumulative investment gates apply. Equipment limits remain four actives, three passives and one ultimate; passive slots open at levels 3, 6 and 10.

## Complete dependency audit

The [audit](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/evidence/dependency-audit.json) records all 111 original effects, referenced targets, exclusions and unlock classifications. An [independent validator](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/audit-dependencies.cjs) extracts named skills and IDs from source descriptions separately from the configured tree. Explicit negative references are excluded; aliases and runtime-only links carry owner-code evidence.

Mutation tests remove the Ancestral Legacy prerequisite, omit one of multiple direct targets, and remove a runtime burning source, verifying each omission fails validation. Trap Hunter AP04 directly extends Venom Trap A03 roots. Briar Trap A09 does not apply that passive in its root path and is not connected.

| Endless Spin WP02 | Whirlwind W01 | — |

## Ownership and persistence

Names, effects and runtime values are generated from `Docs/Design/ClassSkills/catalog.json` and `runtime_parameters.json` into `ClassSkills.json`. The split effects are implemented in actual combat code. HTML levels and dependencies remain a separate `tree-design.cjs` proposal; they are not applied wholesale to game unlock rules. Existing runtime unlock levels are preserved for save compatibility; new P19 skills are registered at level 40. General player release remains disabled.

Old game saves and HED4 documents containing 36 rank entries migrate to 37. When the second ultimate is selected, the old P18 investment and equipment move to P19 without adding points or slots. HTML exports follow the same migration. Migration produces a detached copy and leaves the source unchanged.

Browser storage uses `HELLSCRIPT_SKILL_TREE_PLANNER_V1`, separate from game accounts. The preview supports class-specific allocations, level-reduction refunds, undo, JSON export/import, search, kind filters, Korean/English, and portrait/landscape layouts. It adds no game window, scene, prefab or font owner. Game UI integration must use existing `ClassSkillReadModel`, `ClassSkillLoadout`, `GameStore` and shared UI components.

Descriptions, prerequisites and follow-up skills display localized skill names. Ice Echo shows Frost Nova and Glacial Lance instead of `M06` and `M09`; `BASIC` displays Basic Attack. Nodes and detail headings omit development IDs. Korean particles follow the resolved name's final consonant. Source data, saved IDs and graph relationships stay intact; names are resolved only for presentation.

## Verification and regeneration

Run `python3 tools/class_skills.py build`, `python3 tools/class_skill_runtime.py build`, then `node Prototypes/SkillTree/build.cjs` to regenerate documentation, runtime data and HTML data. [Graph results](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/evidence/graph-validation.json) establish reachability of all 111 skills at their unlock levels. [Model checks](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/evidence/engine-tests.txt) pass 39 cases, including matching versus opposite ultimates, direct alternatives and old-save migration.

[Browser checks](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/evidence/browser-validation.json) cover 111 icons, actual actions and persistence, ten language/viewport combinations and offline HTML. See the [ultimate links](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/evidence/warrior-split-ultimates.png) and [icon comparison](../Art/ClassSkillIcons/qa/ultimate-support-64-dark.png). Actual Unity/macOS counts and scope are recorded in the [final validation summary](../../Prototypes/SkillTree/evidence/validation-summary.json). No physical mobile testing was performed. Public wiki publication accompanies a later main merge.

# Code research notes (read-only, before implementation)

Written: 2026-10-12 · [한국어](README.md)

Notes on how today's code meets each part of the plan, written before Codex implements anything. Nothing was changed; the code was only read. The base is `main` `a3fe67c5` (the base of this branch). **Line numbers are from that commit** and drift as the code changes; search by function and class name.

| File | Contents | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `ui_infrastructure.md` | drawing tools (`UiMesh` ...) with their gaps, adapter window units, scrolling and input, text, animation, smoke framework, EditMode UI tests, icons and masks, file conventions, risks | UI spec |
| `combat_warrior.md` `combat_ranger.md` `combat_mage.md` | per-class combat hooks. Every skill classified A (numbers only), B (new behaviour on an existing path) or C (new mechanic); passives and key passives; test fixtures; open questions | combat spec |
| `save_migration.md` | storage model, migration order and algorithm, level cap 40 -> 60 impact, test patterns | plan chapter 7, step 2 brief |

Why English: they are mostly code identifiers and `file:line` citations, which are harder to find when translated. The deliverables (plan, specs, briefs) are kept in both Korean and English.

pages.body:
# Codex 작업 프롬프트: 자동 생성형 던전(균열 필드)을 캐주얼 StyleD로 교체

## 목표
균열(자동 생성형 던전)의 6개 필드(F0 묘지, F1 성채, F2 사막, F3 동굴, F4 초원, F5 고원)의 화면을 어두운 고딕에서 밝고 아기자기한 캐주얼 StyleD로 바꾼다. 게임 규칙·방 배치·시드·저장 키·전투 결과는 바꾸지 않는다. 첫 단계는 F4 한 필드(대표)이고, 대표가 통과하면 나머지 5개로 넓힌다.

## 현재 상태 (확인한 사실)
- main에는 필드/던전의 캐주얼 적용이 없다. 캐주얼은 몬스터 초상화·도감, 타이틀, 일부 UI까지 들어갔다.
- 던전의 어두운 표현 소유자: `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Presentation/FieldLook.cs`(필드별 조명·안개·후처리·입자), `WorldView.Rift.cs`(바닥·벽·트림 타일, 벽 기둥·횃불), `WorldView.Props.cs`(장애물·장식 `Fields/F<n>/F<n>_<Kind>`), `Resources/World/Fields/F0..F5`(어두운 FBX와 타일 `_A/_N`), `WorldArt.cs`·`WorldArtImporter`(임포트 규칙).

## 참조 (먼저 열어서 본다)
- `Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/battle_encircled_v02_styleD.png`(밝은 초원 전투 장면, 필드 색감의 기준)
- `Docs/Art/CasualConcept/2026-10-13/Town/town_overview_gameview_v01.png`, `title_key_art_v05_styleD.png`

## 해야 할 일 (단계)
1. **대표 F4**: 1차 키트의 F4 타일·모델을 `Resources/World/Fields/F4/`의 같은 이름(`Floor_A/_N`, `Wall_A/_N`, `Trim_A/_N`, `F4_Pillar` 등)으로 연결한다. 어두운 원본은 삭제하지 말고 Git 이력으로 보존한다. 노멀맵은 평평한 `_N`을 만들어 로더 규격(`_A` 알파=매끈함, `_N`)을 지킨다. `.meta`·GUID 규칙과 `WorldArtImporter` 설정을 따른다.
2. `FieldLook.Fields[4]`(grassland)를 밝은 프리셋으로: 낮은 채도 보정 제거, 밝은 하늘색 환경광, 옅은 안개, 따뜻한 햇빛 키라이트, 약한 비네트, 노을 입자 → 꽃가루·나비 같은 밝은 입자. 안개 시작/끝은 가독성을 우선하고, 미탐색 바닥이 검게 그려지는 규칙(카메라 배경 검정)은 유지하되 보이는 범위의 밝기를 해치지 않는다.
3. 장애물 크기: 장식이 아닌 장애물(Pillar, Rubble, Wall 등)은 기존 footprint·height 계약(`manifest`의 footprint/height, 게임 판정 반경)과 어긋나지 않게 맞춘다. 충돌·시야·AI 경로는 건드리지 않는다.
4. **가독성이 최우선**: 빨간 예고 장판·적 탄·영웅 90px 캐릭터가 바닥 위에서 또렷해야 한다. 바닥은 중간 밝기·저대비를 유지하고, 예고색(빨강)·피해 표식과 겹치는 색을 바닥에 쓰지 않는다.
5. 대표 F4가 통과하면 F0, F1, F2, F3, F5를 같은 방식으로 한 필드씩 추가한다. 필드마다 `FieldLook`·타일·모델을 함께 바꾸고, 필드별 분위기 이름(수정 동굴=보랏빛, 눈 고원=밝은 흰색 등)은 키트 팔레트(`PAL`)를 따른다.
6. 보스·훈련장·레거시 링(`FieldLook.Legacy`)·마을은 이번 범위가 아니다.
7. **튜토리얼 균열 (사용자 결정 2026-10-14)**: 튜토리얼 균열은 항상 F0이므로 F0을 밝게 바꾸면 튜토리얼도 함께 밝아진다. 이 변화를 그대로 받아들인다(F0만 어둡게 남기는 분기 금지). 대신 F0 단계에서 튜토리얼 대사·연출·가이드(여신) 문구·토스트·설명 이미지에 "어둡다·으스스하다·묘지·달빛·안개·무덤" 같은 이전 분위기를 전제한 표현이 있는지 점검한다. `Localization`의 한·영 키와 튜토리얼 코드(`Tutorial*`, 가이드 단계, 프롤로그)를 검색해 목록을 만들고, 밝은 화면과 어긋나는 문구만 한·영 키로 함께 고친다(키 이름·저장 키는 유지, 두 언어 모두 채움). 어긋나지 않는 문구는 건드리지 않는다. 점검한 파일과 고친 키, 고치지 않은 이유를 보고에 적는다. 튜토리얼 스모크(관련 `Tutorial*` 테스트와 가이드 스모크)를 F0 변경 뒤 한 번 돌려 흐름이 깨지지 않았는지 확인한다.

- 게임 문구는 한·영 키로(새 문구가 생기면). 변수·주석·커밋 메시지·로그는 영어. 저장 키 변경 금지. 기본 글자 크기·UI 변경 없음.
- 새 Resources 텍스처는 `Editor/ResourceTextureBudget.cs`에 행을 추가한다(`hellscript-apk-size-budget`). 용량이 늘면 수치를 보고한다.

- 작업 중에는 관련 테스트만: `FieldTests`, `AuthoritativeRiftTests`, `TownGroundMaskTests`, `ResourceTextureBudget` 검사, 필드 스모크(`RuntimeFieldSmoke`). 필드마다 macOS 개발 빌드 또는 에디터 화면 캡처 2장(균열 진입 직후, 전투 중 예고 장판이 보이는 장면)을 `Docs/Implementation/CasualFieldEvidence20261014/`에 jpg로 두고 문서에서 파일마다 링크한다.
- 최종 코드 변경과 최신 main 병합 뒤 한 번만 전체 EditMode, 런타임 스모크, `python3 tools/check_ui_contract.py --verify`를 돌린다. 이미 main에서 실패하던 검사와 새 실패를 구분한다. 문서만 바꾸면 게임 실행 검사는 다시 하지 않는다.
- 성능 주장은 같은 조건의 이전·이후 바이너리 각각 3회 이상 원자료가 있을 때만 한다. 없으면 "미검증"으로 적는다. macOS 결과를 실기기 결과로 보고하지 않는다.
- 위키 원본이 바뀌면 `AgentRules/Wiki_Publish.md`대로 병합 후보에서 한 번 생성·검사하고 병합 뒤 공개 반영까지 확인한다.

## 보고 (한국어, 짧게)
바꾼 필드와 파일, 가독성 확인 장면, 테스트 수치(통과·실패·제외), 용량 변화, 미검증 범위(실기기·성능·빌드 크기), 남은 필드.

# Combat Implementation Spec (for Codex)

Updated: 2026-10-12 · For: Codex implementation work · [한국어](D4_Skill_Tree_Combat_Spec_20261012.md)

Author: Claude (specification and research). Codex implements, verifies and commits.

This document expands section 8 (combat) of the plan document [`D4_Skill_Tree_Plan_20261012.en.md`](D4_Skill_Tree_Plan_20261012.en.md) to a level at which it can be implemented. Its basis is the research notes, written by reading the code only (`Docs/Design/D4SkillTree/research/combat_{warrior,ranger,mage}.md`, `save_migration.md`, `dependents.md`). **Line numbers are against `main` `a3fe67c5`**, so they drift when the code changes. Find the code again by function and class name. The source of the numeric values is `skill_tree_d4.json` and `golden/rank_values.json`; for rules and decisions, the plan document takes precedence.

## 0. Scope

- In scope: per-rank values for the 30 actives (10 per class, including 2 ultimates), the **84 modifiers**, the 24 passives and the **6 key passives**, the 3 ultimate ranks, cleanup of the absorbed and removed legacy skills, and where all of this meets auto-battle.
- Out of scope: the skill window screen (UI spec), save and migration (plan section 7, step 2), icons (step 3), and tutorial, edict and quick edit (step 6). This document lists only what those steps **require from the combat side**.
- All combat changes are switched on behind `SkillTreeD4.Enabled`, and the shipping path does not change until step 7.

**Classification result of the 84 modifiers** (the categories are defined in section 3):

| Class | A (values only) | A* (needs a modifier value accessor) | B (new behaviour on an existing path) | C (new mechanism or state) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Warrior | 6 | 0 | 18 | 4 | 28 |
| Ranger | 1 | 1 | 19 | 7 | 28 |
| Mage | 0 | 3 | 21 | 4 | 28 |
| **Total** | **7** | **4** | **58** | **15** | **84** |

## 1. What the new system requires from combat (summary)

1. A base skill has **ranks 1–5** (ultimates 1–3). Per-rank values are linear `from → to` (`golden/rank_values.json` is the golden file).
2. For each skill you choose **one** modifier (only one takes effect), and its rank is at most `min(base rank, max)`. A modifier effect changes the **shape or the extra effect of the base skill**.
3. Passives unlock by hero level only (no separate condition in combat), and of the two key passives only one can hold points.
4. Only the 4 equipped actives plus 1 ultimate are cast. A skill that has not been learned (rank 0) cannot be equipped.
5. Hero level cap 60, points = level (plan section 3).

## 2. Common framework (the first job: step 5.0)

The per-class work (5a, 5b, 5c) starts after this common framework is finished. The common framework is one PR.

### 2.1 The two engines

| Engine | Skills | Execution path | Source of values |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Legacy hero action** | Warrior W01–W06, Ranger A01–A06, Mage M01–M04·M06 (+ passives 01–06) | `TryClassSkillCore` → `StartHeroAction` (`Act:49-82`) → `ResolveSkill` (`Sim:291-353`) | `GameCatalog.cs`, `SkillEffects.cs`, **literals**. Changing `ClassSkills.json` does not change combat |
| **Native cast** | Warrior W08·W09·W17·W18, Ranger A07·A14·A17·A18, Mage M07·M08·M11·M17·M18, absorbed legacy skills | `ClassSkillCast` → `ResolveClassSkill` (`Fx:93-163`) → `ClassSkillEffect` tick (`Fx:167-271`) | `ClassSkills.json` (`catalog.json` + `runtime_parameters.json`) |

17 of the 30 new skills are legacy and 13 are native. The **rank curve of a legacy skill lives in the code** (`SE`, `Cost()`): values such as cost (e.g. W01 6→4, W03 25→21, M01·M03 25→21), duration (Blizzard 6→8), stun (Nova 1.5→1.9) and reuse time (M04) have no rank term today. These values are covered by the file that pins `GameCatalog.cs` and `SkillEffects.cs` by sha256 (`tools/class_skills.py`) and by the Balance1000 hash (`tools/balance_1000.py:222-231`): when you change them, **update the fingerprints in the same PR** and rerun `python3 tools/balance_1000.py`.

### 2.2 Source of values and ranks

- **Data-driven.** Per-rank values of skills, modifiers and passives are read from `SkillTreeD4.json` (`value: {from, to, unit}`). Do not put the formula (`×(1+0.1(r−1))`) in code. Today this formula happens to fit most values, but some values do not fit (section 4). `golden/rank_values.json` gives the golden value for each rank (linear; for count units `명 회 발 개`, `floor`).
- **Base skill damage comes from the base rank**, and **a modifier's values come from the modifier rank's** `from→to` (plan 5.4). A modifier value does not multiply the base-rank scale again. Native `SkillHit`, `Dot` and `Placement` multiply by `a.rankScale` (`Fx:12-13,40,84`), so pass modifier values through a **path that does not multiply** (a separate `source` or a bypass argument).
- **Ultimates (all three classes)**: `RankScale` is fixed at 1 for ultimates (`Cat:65`). Change it to `1 + 0.2(r−1)` (rank 3 = 1.4). The persistence validation cap (`ClassSkillPersistence.cs:37`, rankScale ≤ 1.401) accommodates this. The cooldowns 60/55/50 are set inside the **shared timer** of the two ultimates (floor 45s, `Sk:163`, validation 45–60 `Pers:26`).
- The gear +1 rank (`HeroStats.Blacksmith.cs:17`) is **not applied** to passives, ultimates or modifiers (plan D5).
- Legacy `rank` rule: a hit labelled `"M0x"` gets the base rank (`runeSkillPower` +10% per rank, `Sim:494`, `Dmg:66-67`), and `"EXTRA:M0x"` does not. Where the design requires the modifier rank (M04-1 and so on), the label must be changed.

### 2.3 Extension point: `ClassSkillCast`

Options (`ClassSkillOptions`, 55 groups · 166 choices) change only **when, to whom and where the hero stands**, and never **what** the skill does. A modifier cannot be carried in the options (there is no rank field, entries are capped at 55 and defaults are cleaned up, and the preset copy rules apply). Instead:

1. **Save**: add `modifier` (−1..2, ultimates −1..1) and `modifierRank` to `SkillInvestment` (v5). `JsonUtility` keeps the field's initial value for a missing key, so `modifier = -1` is the right default (0 means "modifier 1 selected"). In v5, `Rank(id)` returns **0 for a missing id** (it returns 1 today).
2. **Cast object**: add `mod` (starting from 1; 0 = none, so old saves stay valid) and `modRank` to `ClassSkillCast` (`ClassSkillState.cs:28-38`, saved), and fill them **once** in `CaptureClassCast` (`Ps:20-46`). Both engines pass through this function (native `Sk:161`, legacy `OriginalClassCast` at `Sk:223`). Validate next to `rankScale` (`Pers:37`).
3. **Reading side**: effect code finds the cast object with `Cast(root)` (`Sk:54`) and looks at `a.mod`/`a.modRank`. The **decision side** (planner, cost, forecast, aiming, auto-cast) has no cast object, so it reads `Loadout.Modifier(id)` (next to `Rank()`, `Sk:84`). An effect whose cast object is null (30-second cleanup, `Sk:218`) or that outlives its cast (`Ps:124`) must **copy the values when it is created** (`Placement` is the precedent, `Fx:84`).
4. **Value override**: `SkillTreeD4Values.Modifier(id, key, rank)`, which overlays the modifier value on `N(id,key)` (`Sk:28`).
5. **Test fixture**: many tests call non-public methods by reflection (positional arguments, `Single(name)`: `RT:17-22`, `PT:21`). **Do not create overloads**; append optional arguments at the end.

### 2.4 Effect ids and the cleanup rule (the most common trap)

- Effects, DoTs and shields of ids that are not equipped are **cleared every tick** (`ResetClassSkillEquipment`, `Sk:237-239`). The absorbed legacy skills (W07·W10–W16, A08–A13·A15·A16, M05·M09·M10·M12·M14·M16) are **never equipped** in the new system. A modifier effect must create a new id or **attach the base skill id as its `source`**. For the same reason, the "is equipped" checks in `InspectClassSkill`'s `NOT_EQUIPPED` (`Sk:122`) and `Reduce` (`Sk:72`), in the cancellation of a cast in progress (`HuntEdictChanges.cs:46`) and in the resume validation (`Pers:39-40`) must also be changed to judge a modifier effect as **parent + modifier**.
- The **secondary damage** that a modifier effect deals (forks, bounces, echoes, turrets) is `DamageKind.Set` with id `EXTRA:<original>`: no crit, not `Native`, not a direct hit (`Fx:12`, `Ps:101,121`). Keep the existing "it is not another skill" rule.
- There are many **hardcoded ids** (`"W07"`, `"M12"`, `"A11"`, `"M05"` …). When reusing an absorbed body, replace the literals with a modifier check. The locations are in the "Trap" column of each row.
- The gear and set hooks `DES_LW41–45` and `DES_LM41–46` hang off absorbed skills. Apply them **only when that modifier is chosen** (plan section 12).

### 2.5 Auto-battle and forecast

- Auto-cast: `TryAutomaticClassSkill` (`Cast:179-201`) walks through `Loadout.order`. The condition of a legacy skill is always true, and the real decision is in the edict planners (`PlanEdictWhirlwind/Leap/IronWall/Shout/Slam/…`, `Rules:159-262`). The condition of a native skill is `ClassAutoDefaultCondition` (`Au:97-147`).
- **The forecast and the release must match** (enforced by the `Identity:107-117` test). A modifier that changes the shape (W03-1 cone → circle, W04-2 circle → line, M01-1 Meteor, M03-2 reflection …) must **change the planner and the forecast too**.
- **Cautions from plan 8.5**: a modifier that stops to aim (A05-1), placed objects (the A03-3 turret, the 3 orbs of M11-2), a zone that follows the hero (M02-1) and a clone (A18-1) collide with auto-movement. Decide each item's auto-battle behaviour before implementing it and pin it with a test (the defaults in section 8).

### 2.6 Save and resume

- A modifier's `mod`/`modRank` live in `ClassSkillCast`, so **a cast in progress and its effects look the same after a resume** (`ClassSkillRuntimeState` saves them). Adapt the allow list of the persistence validation (`ClassSkillPersistence`) (`Pers:42,47-50`: the only intent ids are W02/M13, and the only persistent effects are the M13 channel and the W15 loan) to the new persistent effects (A03-3 turret, M11-2 orbs, W18-2 form buff and so on). An id that is not on the list throws an exception on resume, so the **saved run can no longer be read**.
- If a run is in progress during migration, handle it on the safe side (save research F1, the new decision in plan section 17).
- Skill id strings in statistics and logs (`statistics.skills`, `damageEvents`, `procHits` …) are not validated on load. A modifier effect's `definitionId` uses the base skill id, and the modifier number goes in a separate field.

### 2.7 Test fixture

- Basic fixture: `ClassSkillRuntimeTests.Fixture(skill, passive, equipment)` (`RT:23-41`). A level 40 hero (**change it to a level 60 hero**), equipped `[skill]`, one stationary enemy with 100000 HP (2m ahead), `Stats` overwritten with damage 100, HP 1000 and crit 0, and `decisionTime = 100000`, so **only manual casts** run, seed 42. Helpers: `Advance` (`RT:42`), `CastSkill` (`RT:44`), `Use` (`PT:24`), `AddSkill` (`RT:49`), `ExtraEnemy` (`GT:12`), `Begin`/`Land`/`Status` (`PT:12-23`).
- Legacy path: `T/ActionTests.cs:12-24`, `SkillRankEffectTests.cs:17-33` (`ContentTestAccounts.Legacy()`). The projectile and trap count tests and the forecast = release tests are here.
- Reading results: `State.damageEvents` (`definitionId`, `kind`, `critical`, `finalDamage`, `rootCastId`), `effectEvents`, `classSkills.{casts,effects,dots,cooldowns}`, `projectiles`, `traps`, `shields` and the `ClassSkillChanged` stream.
- **Determinism**: `Hit` always draws from `State.rng` (`Dmg:70`). A new roll shifts all later rolls, so compare with crit 0 and the same seed.
- Mage tests must know that `Stats.passives = new bool[6]` (RT:38) turns off MP05 and MP06 (turn them on with `sim.Stats.passives[4|5] = true`, or use the legacy Mage fixture `PassiveTests.cs:21-33`).
- **One test per modifier (paired test)**: run the same fixture with no modifier (`modifier = -1`) and with the modifier, and assert the difference.
```csharp
// helpers are real; r.modifier / r.modifierRank are the new v5 fields
int HitsOnSide(int modifier){
  var s=Fixture("W09");var r=s.State.build.classSkills.ranks.Single(x=>x.id=="W09");
  r.modifier=modifier;r.modifierRank=modifier<0?0:1;
  var side=ExtraEnemy(s,s.State.position+Vector2.right*2);Call(s,"Sense");
  Assert.IsTrue(CastSkill(s,"W09"));Advance(s,.6f);
  return s.State.damageEvents.Count(d=>d.definitionId=="W09"&&d.kind==DamageKind.Direct&&d.targetId==side.id);
}
[Test] public void SpinningRendReachesBesideTheCone(){Assert.AreEqual(0,HitsOnSide(-1));Assert.AreEqual(1,HitsOnSide(2));}
```
- Tests that will break (to be rewritten): `RT:16,54-66` (counts 37/16/19), `PT:11,36-96`, `Identity:88-150`, `SkillPresetCombatPreviewTests.cs:105-115`, `ClassSkillNativeSmoke.cs:47-66`, and the ability measurement tool `ClassSkillPassiveMeasurement` (old id names; its requirement of empty passive slots is forbidden in v3+).

### 2.8 Acceptance criteria for one modifier (common to every row)

1. **Values**: at rank 1 and at the maximum rank they equal the design's `from → to` (`golden/rank_values.json`).
2. **Behavioural difference**: the paired test shows the difference between no modifier and the modifier.
3. **Forecast**: for a skill that has a forecast, the forecast and the release match.
4. **Auto-battle**: auto-cast does not stall or spin idle.
5. **Resume**: saving and restoring a cast or an effect gives the same result.
6. **Cleanup rule**: the effect does not disappear when absorbed ids are cleaned up (2.4).
7. **Old behaviour kept**: with no modifier chosen, the base skill behaves as the design's default "no modifier" form (e.g. M07 is fire element with no extra effect, plan D8).

## 3. The 84 modifiers

**Categories**: **A** = only values change (keys and literals are turned into values). **A\*** = values only, but the value comes from the **modifier rank** (needs the accessor from 2.3). **B** = new behaviour on top of an existing code path. **C** = needs a new mechanism or state (a state field, a new effect kind, a new check). Abbreviations: `Sk` = `CombatSimulation.ClassSkills.cs`, `Fx` = `…ClassSkillEffects.cs`, `Au` = `…ClassSkillAuto.cs`, `Ps` = `…ClassSkillPassives.cs`, `Po` = `…ClassSkillPolicies.cs`, `Id` = `…SkillIdentity.cs`, `Sim` = `CombatSimulation.cs`, `Act` = `…Actions.cs`, `Dmg` = `…Damage.cs`, `Eff` = `…Effects.cs`, `Cs` = `…ClassSets.cs`, `Proj` = `…Projectiles.cs`, `Fc` = `…Forecast.cs`, `Aim` = `…EdictAim.cs`, `Cast` = `…ClassSkills.cs`. The other abbreviations and the exact locations are at the head of each file of the research notes. **The modifier number follows the design order (1–3), and the implementation's modifier number `modifier` is 0–2.**

### Warrior modifiers (28)

| ID | Name | Effect (rank 1 → max) | Category | Implementation point | Trap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `W09-1` | Blood Reclaim | HP per target 1.0% → 2.0% | **B** | On every 3rd cast, `CashDot`+`Heal` (reuse the W10 body). The cast count uses `Counter()` | The W10 hooks (Au:110, Po:39,89) become dead code |
| `W09-2` | Deep Wound | Bleed per stack +20% → +40% | **B** | Hit only one enemy and stack the bleed as `Dot(additiveBank,cap)` entries (up to 3 stacks) | Unclear whether +20% per stack is additive or multiplicative (question W-1) |
| `W09-3` | Spinning Rend | Bleed lasts 2s → 3s | **A** | `width` 90→360 (skip the angle check when `arc>=360`), `duration` | `Po:53` and `Au:85` read the same key. A shorter duration raises DPS (`bank/duration`) |
| `W08-1` | Lunging Hook | Extra resource +4 → +12 | **B** | Reuse the W11 movement skill (prepare+.25s, `Lerp`) to move to a stopping point in front of the enemy. Add W08 to the landing list | Walking is blocked while moving (Sim:364). Extra resource on arrival |
| `W08-2` | Piercing Hook | Pierces 3 → 7 targets | **B** | `SkillHit` several targets with `Line(origin,aim,6,width,3..7)`, `Pull` only the last one | Add a new width key |
| `W08-3` | Branding Hook | Damage from brand −10% → −18% | **B** | Reuse the W07 mark (`ApplyStatus(Mark,"W07",6)`). The kill resource uses a new `ClassHitFlags` bit | Literal "W07" (`HasAmplifyingMark` Sk:90, Ps:179, Au:51), DES_LW41 (Fx:103). A new mark erases the previous mark (Eff:106-107) |
| `W01-1` | Swift Whirl | Move speed ×2.0 → ×3.0 | **B** | Apply the move speed ×2~3 **after** the `SpeedWithBonus` cap (1.5x) (EdictWhirlwindMovement.cs:40, Sim:437) | Outrunning the enemies can trip the 0.5s empty-tick cutoff |
| `W01-2` | Wide Whirl | Hit area ×1.6 → ×2.0 | **A** | Radius multiplier inside `RuneSkillRadius` (every call passes through this function) | The walking logic stays pinned at 2.3~2.5m (EdictWhirlwindMovement.cs:29) |
| `W01-3` | Rapid Whirl | Tick interval ×0.7 → ×0.5 | **A** | Turn the tick interval literals (Act:80, Sim:458) into values | Cost, pull and crit roll on every tick: at interval ×0.5 the cost per second is 2x. Adjust the cost together (question W-3) |
| `W03-1` | Earth Shatter | Blast radius 2.0m → 3.0m | **B** | Cone → circle: arc 100→360, radius 2→3 (Sim:313, Forecast.cs:98, EdictAim.cs:20). Use `Cast.area` | The design calls the base a 'single strike' (SD4:581), but the implementation is a 100° multi-hit (question W-4) |
| `W03-2` | Execution Strike | Execute below 20% → 30% HP | **B** | Coefficient ×2 at HP ≤ threshold (same check as WP06, Dmg:31) | Refund amount undecided |
| `W03-3` | Aftershock | Aftershocks D40% → D80% ×2 | **B** | `ScheduleExtra` 'burst' ×2, +1s (Cs:111-114, Fx:233) | Being `Kind.Set`, it gets no WP15, WP17 or legendary credit |
| `W05-1` | Iron Stance | Counter on block D80% → D120% | **B** | Use the W12 counter body (`AfterClassHurt` Ps:164-165, 2 times at 1s intervals) under the `OwnIronWall` condition | W12's +15% block (Ps:192) is not in the design |
| `W05-2` | Guardian Oath | CC immunity 1.0s → 2.0s | **B** | W16: `ClearHeroControl` + `Buff("W16:immune")` (Fx:120-126) | Retarget the W16 special handling (Sk:190, EdictOrder.cs:132, Au:116) to the new target |
| `W05-3` | Thorn Armor | Reflect absorbed 30% → 50% | **B** | In `ReactShield` (Id:77-90), deal absorbed amount × ratio to `Nearby(..,3)` as secondary damage | Separate from the thorns attribute (Attributes.cs:115). The `IronWallAmount` pre-check has the literal .3 (EdictWarriorSupport.cs:10) |
| `W06-1` | Rallying Cry | Move speed +20% → +40% | **A** | Add `shoutTime>0` to `ClassMoveBonus` (Ps:168-174) | Total +50% cap (Economy.cs:45). 'Crowd control reduction' appears only in the design's behaviourKo |
| `W06-2` | Frenzy Cry | Attack speed +20% → +40% | **B** | Apply `ClassAttackSpeedBonus` (Ps:193), skip the resource refill (Sim:325, EdictWarriorSupport.cs:85) | Attack speed cap 1.5 (Act:57) |
| `W06-3` | Debt of Battle | Extra resource +40 → +60 | **B** | W15 loan (`BorrowResource/RepayResource` Id:22-38) | The design says 'resource regeneration stops for 6 seconds', but the implementation is borrow and repay (question W-8). The validator is tied to "W15" (ClassSkillPersistence.cs:47-50) |
| `W02-1` | Breach Charge | Charge distance 3m → 5m | **C** | Push along the path: `Line`+`BreakFront` (Id:11-21, W11 Fx:109-112) + a push width key | Whether to keep the landing damage; turning off `HeroAirHeight` (Act:28); the `EdictLeapLandingValid` minimum of 2m; the meaning of the 'space' policy (Po:177) |
| `W02-2` | Quake Landing | Landing quake D60% → D100% | **B** | Add a +2s 'burst' and a stun (`ApplyStatus`) to the landing (`ClassLanding` Ps:57-69). Add a stun branch to 'burst' |  |
| `W02-3` | Double Leap | Recharge 8s → 6s | **C** | There is no charge concept. Many places read `State.cooldowns[]` (EdictWarrior.cs:79, Dmg:156-157, Legendaries.cs:111,128, ClassSkillReadModel.cs:24-25) | Recharge 8→6s vs cooldown 6.4s (question W-5) |

| `W04-3` | Repeated Stomp | Per stomp 40% → 60% ×3 | **B** | A stomp on cast + a 'burst' twice (at 0.6/1.2s), with a stun on the last one. Anchored to `a.origin` | Being `Kind.Set`, it gets no WP17 |
| `W17-1` | Ancestral Legion | 3 ancestors · 6s → 8s | **A** | `summons`, `duration` and `ticks` keys |  |
| `W17-2` | Ancestral Technique | Copied skill 50% → 70% | **C** | A last-skill record field (`ClassSkillRuntimeState`) and replay | The copy must not pass through `CaptureClassCast` (WP15 history Ps:25-26) and uses an `EXTRA:` id |
| `W18-1` | Judgment of the Earth | Area 6m → 8m | **A** | An accessor that reads `prepare` (before the cast object exists, Sk:159) | The hero is held for 1.8s (Act:26) |
| `W18-2` | Giant Form | Giant form 6s → 8s | **C** | A form buff: area +50% (`Cast.area`, ignored by W01/W02) and knockback immunity (`PushHero`) | Add the persistent effect to the allow list at ClassSkillPersistence.cs:47-48 |

### Ranger modifiers (28)

| ID | Name | Effect (rank 1 → max) | Category | Implementation point | Trap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A07-1` | Rapid Volley | 5 shots · D25% → D33% each | **A*** | `arrows`/`coef` (Fx:95,133). Damage basis E1 |  |
| `A07-2` | Scatter Shot | Targets 3 → 5 | **B** | A different target for each arrow with `Nearby(a.origin,range,n)` (repeat targets when enemies are few) | The release checks only the main target (Cast:170). Each hit connects to A18 (Idn:64) |
| `A07-3` | Finishing Arrow | 3rd arrow crit +30% → +70% | **B** | Pierce already exists (`Arrow(...,pierce)`). Forced crit and the crit damage argument are new plumbing (Dmg:70,73, `SkillHit` Fx:9-13) | Uses the same plumbing as A04-3 and Precision |

| `A01-1` | Ricochet | Bounces 1 → 3 | **C** | There is no bounce code or wall normal (RiftLayout.cs:32-43). Normal probing, storing the bounce count (`CombatProjectile`), the `hitIds` rule | The forecast (Forecast) cannot predict it |

| `A02-2` | Bouncing Arrows | Bounce damage 40% → 80% | **B** | On hit, send the SAB4 `extra` pattern (Set, no effects) to the nearest enemy not yet hit + a 'bounce' flag |  |
| `A02-3` | Focused Spread | Same-target arrows +10% → +30% | **B** | The LA02 `narrow` path already does the same thing (Proj:30). Change the `Stats.specials.Contains("LA02")` checks to modifier checks | The same-target bonus uses `victim.hits` (Proj:84) |
| `A04-1` | Decoy Projection | Decoy taunt 2.0s → 3.0s | **B** | Create the A11 effect (Fx:136, enemy AI, expiry blast) at `a.origin` from the LA03 hook. The taunt of 2→3s is `tauntSeconds` | AP14 reads the literal `Fx("A11")` (Pas:110) |

**Do not**: re-write the rules (points, tiers, modifier rank) in the combat code. Do not carry modifiers in the option system. Do not quietly carry over the current bonus effects that are not in the design (W11 guard and resource, W12 +15% block, A12 +20% speed and so on) (question C-5).

| C-2 | The basis of the `%` and `D%` units | `D%` = a coefficient based on weapon damage, `%` = the quantity that the word before it on that line points to. Decide ambiguous lines (A14-1, A02-2, A01-3, A07-3) one by one in the PR and write them in the table |
| C-3 | Costs, cooldowns and durations not in the design | Keep the current ones |
| C-4 | Does a forced crit (A07-3, AP20, A04-3) count toward the crit counter | Yes, it counts |
| C-5 | Current bonus effects that are not in the design | Remove them (the design is the basis) |
| C-6 | When the design text and the implementation differ | The design's `effectKo`/`value` wins (plan 8.2) |
| C-7 | Where to put the legacy rank tables (cost, duration, stun) | Read them data-driven (extend `runtime_parameters.json` + `SkillTreeD4.json`). The fingerprint update goes in the PR |
| C-8 | Caps on placed and summoned objects (traps 2, turret 1, orbs 3, decoy, clone) | Give each skill a per-caster cap and remove the oldest one when it is exceeded (A03-3 turret 1, M11-2 orbs 3, A18-1 clone 1) |

**Warrior**

| # | Question | Default |
|---|---|---|
| W-1 | Is the W09-2 "+20% per stack" additive or multiplicative | Additive to the bleed damage per stack |
| W-2 | The design's resource notation is inconsistent: W09 "Resource on hit +8→12", W08 "Resource gain +10→18", W08-1 "Extra resource +4→12". Per hit or per cast | All once per cast (when there is at least one hit) |
| W-3 | If W01-3 shortens the tick interval, does the cost change too | Reduce the tick cost in proportion to the interval so that the cost per second stays the same |
| W-4 | Is the W03 base a single strike or a 100° multi-hit | Keep the current 100°. The design owner fixes the design text (SD4:581) |
| W-5 | The relation between W02-3 "2 charges, recharge 8→6s" and the base skill's cooldown 8→6.4s | Build a new charge model (a dedicated `charges` state, saved). While the modifier is chosen it **replaces** the cooldown, the recharge time is the modifier rank's from→to (8→6s), and the base rank's cooldown reduction does not apply |
| W-8 | W06-3 "resource regeneration stops for 6 seconds" versus the implementation (borrow and repay) | Stop regeneration as the design text says. Do not use the loan code |
| W-13 | WP13 "70% or below" versus `<` | The design (≤) |

**Ranger**

| # | Question | Default |
|---|---|---|
| R-1 | The base effect and element of A06 (Elemental Imbuement), and which shots consume it | Base: the next 3 shots deal +25→35% extra damage (no element). The shots that consume it are BASIC, A01 and A02 (the old rule). Forks, echoes, turrets and rain do not consume it |
| R-2 | The A01-1 bounce rules (`hitIds`, `maxHits`) | A target is hit only once, and the number of bounces is the rank value (1, 1, 2, 2, 3 from `rank_values.json`), each reflecting off the wall normal. The forecast shows only the first segment |
| R-3 | A03-2 Frost Snare: a zone or one-shot (the old A10 is a one-shot blast) | A zone, as in the design (slow 30→50% while the trap exists) |
| R-4 | Movement and interruption during A05-1 aiming | Stop auto-movement while aiming, and cancel when damage is taken (plan section 8) |
| R-5 | A07 resource: the design "+8→12" vs the code cost 12 and a 25% reserve | Change to the design (gained on hit) and remove the cost entry |
| R-6 | The duration of the A17-1 8 waves, and the meaning of A17-2 "Narrow area ×1.6→2.0" | A17-1 uses `ticks` 8 and a duration of 4s. A17-2 uses radius ×0.5, damage per wave ×1.6→2.0, period .25, and keeps the duration (`ticks` 10) |
| R-9 | The definition of A18-2 "fading" | Burst on expiry, consumption and removal over the cap |

**Mage**

| # | Question | Default |
|---|---|---|
| M-1 | Values where the design text and `effectKo` differ (M01-1 ×1.4→1.8 vs "area ×1.5, damage ×1.6", M02-2, M03-1, M03-3, M04-2, M04-3, M06-3, M08-1·2·3, M11-2, M18-1) | `effectKo`/`value` wins (C-6). The design owner fixes the text |
| M-2 | M07: today it costs 18 with cooldown 3, but the design's only base value is "Mana on hit +6→10", a T1 generator | Keep the cooldown, cost 0, mana +6→10 (once per cast, when there is a hit). The auto-cast condition is "while mana is not full" |
| M-3 | Does M04-3 keep M05's last-element reaction | Keep it (the `lastElement` record is needed by M17-1 and M18-2) |
| M-4 | Is the M08-1 circle a disc or a ring, and does it follow the hero | A disc that follows the hero |
| M-5 | `lastElement = 0` in M17-1 | Substitute fire |
| M-6 | The radius, cap and targets of MP20 Shatter | Radius 2.5m, 5 targets, and bosses burst on stun (stagger) |
| M-7 | The window and reset of MP21 Align the Elements | When all three elements have touched one enemy once each, it bursts and resets. No time window. Damage over time and `EXTRA:` hits do not count |
| M-9 | M18's cost −20% and 3-element blast | Keep them (they are in the code but not in the design's base text: the design owner fills in the text) |
| M-12 | MP07 and MP09 12→20, MP16 8→12 | The design values (from→to) |

Among the questions above, **those that need a user decision** (those whose default changes behaviour or balance significantly: W-4, R-1, C-5, M-9) have been carried over to plan section 17 as D21~D24.

Updated: 2026-10-12 · For: Codex implementation work · 한국어

Author: Claude (specification and research). Codex implements, verifies and commits.

This document expands section 8 (combat) of the plan document `D4_Skill_Tree_Plan_20261012.en.md` to a level at which it can be implemented. Its basis is the research notes, written by reading the code only (Docs/Design/D4SkillTree/research/combat_{warrior,ranger,mage}.md, save_migration.md, dependents.md). Line numbers are against main a3fe67c5, so they drift when the code changes. Find the code again by function and class name. The source of the numeric values is skill_tree_d4.json and golden/rank_values.json; for rules and decisions, the plan document takes precedence.

0. Scope

  • In scope: per-rank values for the 30 actives (10 per class, including 2 ultimates), the 84 modifiers, the 24 passives and the 6 key passives, the 3 ultimate ranks, cleanup of the absorbed and removed legacy skills, and where all of this meets auto-battle.
  • Out of scope: the skill window screen (UI spec), save and migration (plan section 7, step 2), icons (step 3), and tutorial, edict and quick edit (step 6). This document lists only what those steps require from the combat side.
  • All combat changes are switched on behind SkillTreeD4.Enabled, and the shipping path does not change until step 7.

Classification result of the 84 modifiers (the categories are defined in section 3):

ClassA (values only)A* (needs a modifier value accessor)B (new behaviour on an existing path)C (new mechanism or state)Total
Warrior6018428
Ranger1119728
Mage0321428
Total74581584

1. What the new system requires from combat (summary)

  1. A base skill has ranks 1–5 (ultimates 1–3). Per-rank values are linear from → to (golden/rank_values.json is the golden file).
  2. For each skill you choose one modifier (only one takes effect), and its rank is at most min(base rank, max). A modifier effect changes the shape or the extra effect of the base skill.
  3. Passives unlock by hero level only (no separate condition in combat), and of the two key passives only one can hold points.
  4. Only the 4 equipped actives plus 1 ultimate are cast. A skill that has not been learned (rank 0) cannot be equipped.
  5. Hero level cap 60, points = level (plan section 3).

2. Common framework (the first job: step 5.0)

The per-class work (5a, 5b, 5c) starts after this common framework is finished. The common framework is one PR.

2.1 The two engines

EngineSkillsExecution pathSource of values
Legacy hero actionWarrior W01–W06, Ranger A01–A06, Mage M01–M04·M06 (+ passives 01–06)TryClassSkillCore → StartHeroAction (Act:49-82) → ResolveSkill (Sim:291-353)GameCatalog.cs, SkillEffects.cs, literals. Changing ClassSkills.json does not change combat
Native castWarrior W08·W09·W17·W18, Ranger A07·A14·A17·A18, Mage M07·M08·M11·M17·M18, absorbed legacy skillsClassSkillCast → ResolveClassSkill (Fx:93-163) → ClassSkillEffect tick (Fx:167-271)ClassSkills.json (catalog.json + runtime_parameters.json)

17 of the 30 new skills are legacy and 13 are native. The rank curve of a legacy skill lives in the code (SE, Cost()): values such as cost (e.g. W01 6→4, W03 25→21, M01·M03 25→21), duration (Blizzard 6→8), stun (Nova 1.5→1.9) and reuse time (M04) have no rank term today. These values are covered by the file that pins GameCatalog.cs and SkillEffects.cs by sha256 (tools/class_skills.py) and by the Balance1000 hash (tools/balance_1000.py:222-231): when you change them, update the fingerprints in the same PR and rerun python3 tools/balance_1000.py.

2.2 Source of values and ranks

  • Data-driven. Per-rank values of skills, modifiers and passives are read from SkillTreeD4.json (value: {from, to, unit}). Do not put the formula (×(1+0.1(r−1))) in code. Today this formula happens to fit most values, but some values do not fit (section 4). golden/rank_values.json gives the golden value for each rank (linear; for count units 명 회 발 개, floor).
  • Base skill damage comes from the base rank, and a modifier's values come from the modifier rank's from→to (plan 5.4). A modifier value does not multiply the base-rank scale again. Native SkillHit, Dot and Placement multiply by a.rankScale (Fx:12-13,40,84), so pass modifier values through a path that does not multiply (a separate source or a bypass argument).
  • Ultimates (all three classes): RankScale is fixed at 1 for ultimates (Cat:65). Change it to 1 + 0.2(r−1) (rank 3 = 1.4). The persistence validation cap (ClassSkillPersistence.cs:37, rankScale ≤ 1.401) accommodates this. The cooldowns 60/55/50 are set inside the shared timer of the two ultimates (floor 45s, Sk:163, validation 45–60 Pers:26).
  • The gear +1 rank (HeroStats.Blacksmith.cs:17) is not applied to passives, ultimates or modifiers (plan D5).
  • Legacy rank rule: a hit labelled "M0x" gets the base rank (runeSkillPower +10% per rank, Sim:494, Dmg:66-67), and "EXTRA:M0x" does not. Where the design requires the modifier rank (M04-1 and so on), the label must be changed.

2.3 Extension point: ClassSkillCast

Options (ClassSkillOptions, 55 groups · 166 choices) change only when, to whom and where the hero stands, and never what the skill does. A modifier cannot be carried in the options (there is no rank field, entries are capped at 55 and defaults are cleaned up, and the preset copy rules apply). Instead:

  1. Save: add modifier (−1..2, ultimates −1..1) and modifierRank to SkillInvestment (v5). JsonUtility keeps the field's initial value for a missing key, so modifier = -1 is the right default (0 means "modifier 1 selected"). In v5, Rank(id) returns 0 for a missing id (it returns 1 today).
  2. Cast object: add mod (starting from 1; 0 = none, so old saves stay valid) and modRank to ClassSkillCast (ClassSkillState.cs:28-38, saved), and fill them once in CaptureClassCast (Ps:20-46). Both engines pass through this function (native Sk:161, legacy OriginalClassCast at Sk:223). Validate next to rankScale (Pers:37).
  3. Reading side: effect code finds the cast object with Cast(root) (Sk:54) and looks at a.mod/a.modRank. The decision side (planner, cost, forecast, aiming, auto-cast) has no cast object, so it reads Loadout.Modifier(id) (next to Rank(), Sk:84). An effect whose cast object is null (30-second cleanup, Sk:218) or that outlives its cast (Ps:124) must copy the values when it is created (Placement is the precedent, Fx:84).
  4. Value override: SkillTreeD4Values.Modifier(id, key, rank), which overlays the modifier value on N(id,key) (Sk:28).
  5. Test fixture: many tests call non-public methods by reflection (positional arguments, Single(name): RT:17-22, PT:21). Do not create overloads; append optional arguments at the end.

2.4 Effect ids and the cleanup rule (the most common trap)

  • Effects, DoTs and shields of ids that are not equipped are cleared every tick (ResetClassSkillEquipment, Sk:237-239). The absorbed legacy skills (W07·W10–W16, A08–A13·A15·A16, M05·M09·M10·M12·M14·M16) are never equipped in the new system. A modifier effect must create a new id or attach the base skill id as its source. For the same reason, the "is equipped" checks in InspectClassSkill's NOT_EQUIPPED (Sk:122) and Reduce (Sk:72), in the cancellation of a cast in progress (HuntEdictChanges.cs:46) and in the resume validation (Pers:39-40) must also be changed to judge a modifier effect as parent + modifier.
  • The secondary damage that a modifier effect deals (forks, bounces, echoes, turrets) is DamageKind.Set with id EXTRA:<original>: no crit, not Native, not a direct hit (Fx:12, Ps:101,121). Keep the existing "it is not another skill" rule.
  • There are many hardcoded ids ("W07", "M12", "A11", "M05" …). When reusing an absorbed body, replace the literals with a modifier check. The locations are in the "Trap" column of each row.
  • The gear and set hooks DES_LW41–45 and DES_LM41–46 hang off absorbed skills. Apply them only when that modifier is chosen (plan section 12).

2.5 Auto-battle and forecast

  • Auto-cast: TryAutomaticClassSkill (Cast:179-201) walks through Loadout.order. The condition of a legacy skill is always true, and the real decision is in the edict planners (PlanEdictWhirlwind/Leap/IronWall/Shout/Slam/…, Rules:159-262). The condition of a native skill is ClassAutoDefaultCondition (Au:97-147).
  • The forecast and the release must match (enforced by the Identity:107-117 test). A modifier that changes the shape (W03-1 cone → circle, W04-2 circle → line, M01-1 Meteor, M03-2 reflection …) must change the planner and the forecast too.
  • Cautions from plan 8.5: a modifier that stops to aim (A05-1), placed objects (the A03-3 turret, the 3 orbs of M11-2), a zone that follows the hero (M02-1) and a clone (A18-1) collide with auto-movement. Decide each item's auto-battle behaviour before implementing it and pin it with a test (the defaults in section 8).

2.6 Save and resume

  • A modifier's mod/modRank live in ClassSkillCast, so a cast in progress and its effects look the same after a resume (ClassSkillRuntimeState saves them). Adapt the allow list of the persistence validation (ClassSkillPersistence) (Pers:42,47-50: the only intent ids are W02/M13, and the only persistent effects are the M13 channel and the W15 loan) to the new persistent effects (A03-3 turret, M11-2 orbs, W18-2 form buff and so on). An id that is not on the list throws an exception on resume, so the saved run can no longer be read.
  • If a run is in progress during migration, handle it on the safe side (save research F1, the new decision in plan section 17).
  • Skill id strings in statistics and logs (statistics.skills, damageEvents, procHits …) are not validated on load. A modifier effect's definitionId uses the base skill id, and the modifier number goes in a separate field.

2.7 Test fixture

  • Basic fixture: ClassSkillRuntimeTests.Fixture(skill, passive, equipment) (RT:23-41). A level 40 hero (change it to a level 60 hero), equipped [skill], one stationary enemy with 100000 HP (2m ahead), Stats overwritten with damage 100, HP 1000 and crit 0, and decisionTime = 100000, so only manual casts run, seed 42. Helpers: Advance (RT:42), CastSkill (RT:44), Use (PT:24), AddSkill (RT:49), ExtraEnemy (GT:12), Begin/Land/Status (PT:12-23).
  • Legacy path: T/ActionTests.cs:12-24, SkillRankEffectTests.cs:17-33 (ContentTestAccounts.Legacy()). The projectile and trap count tests and the forecast = release tests are here.
  • Reading results: State.damageEvents (definitionId, kind, critical, finalDamage, rootCastId), effectEvents, classSkills.{casts,effects,dots,cooldowns}, projectiles, traps, shields and the ClassSkillChanged stream.
  • Determinism: Hit always draws from State.rng (Dmg:70). A new roll shifts all later rolls, so compare with crit 0 and the same seed.
  • Mage tests must know that Stats.passives = new bool[6] (RT:38) turns off MP05 and MP06 (turn them on with sim.Stats.passives[4|5] = true, or use the legacy Mage fixture PassiveTests.cs:21-33).
  • One test per modifier (paired test): run the same fixture with no modifier (modifier = -1) and with the modifier, and assert the difference.
// helpers are real; r.modifier / r.modifierRank are the new v5 fields
int HitsOnSide(int modifier){
  var s=Fixture("W09");var r=s.State.build.classSkills.ranks.Single(x=>x.id=="W09");
  r.modifier=modifier;r.modifierRank=modifier<0?0:1;
  var side=ExtraEnemy(s,s.State.position+Vector2.right*2);Call(s,"Sense");
  Assert.IsTrue(CastSkill(s,"W09"));Advance(s,.6f);
  return s.State.damageEvents.Count(d=>d.definitionId=="W09"&&d.kind==DamageKind.Direct&&d.targetId==side.id);
}
[Test] public void SpinningRendReachesBesideTheCone(){Assert.AreEqual(0,HitsOnSide(-1));Assert.AreEqual(1,HitsOnSide(2));}
  • Tests that will break (to be rewritten): RT:16,54-66 (counts 37/16/19), PT:11,36-96, Identity:88-150, SkillPresetCombatPreviewTests.cs:105-115, ClassSkillNativeSmoke.cs:47-66, and the ability measurement tool ClassSkillPassiveMeasurement (old id names; its requirement of empty passive slots is forbidden in v3+).

2.8 Acceptance criteria for one modifier (common to every row)

  1. Values: at rank 1 and at the maximum rank they equal the design's from → to (golden/rank_values.json).
  2. Behavioural difference: the paired test shows the difference between no modifier and the modifier.
  3. Forecast: for a skill that has a forecast, the forecast and the release match.
  4. Auto-battle: auto-cast does not stall or spin idle.
  5. Resume: saving and restoring a cast or an effect gives the same result.
  6. Cleanup rule: the effect does not disappear when absorbed ids are cleaned up (2.4).
  7. Old behaviour kept: with no modifier chosen, the base skill behaves as the design's default "no modifier" form (e.g. M07 is fire element with no extra effect, plan D8).

3. The 84 modifiers

Categories: A = only values change (keys and literals are turned into values). A\* = values only, but the value comes from the modifier rank (needs the accessor from 2.3). B = new behaviour on top of an existing code path. C = needs a new mechanism or state (a state field, a new effect kind, a new check). Abbreviations: Sk = CombatSimulation.ClassSkills.cs, Fx = …ClassSkillEffects.cs, Au = …ClassSkillAuto.cs, Ps = …ClassSkillPassives.cs, Po = …ClassSkillPolicies.cs, Id = …SkillIdentity.cs, Sim = CombatSimulation.cs, Act = …Actions.cs, Dmg = …Damage.cs, Eff = …Effects.cs, Cs = …ClassSets.cs, Proj = …Projectiles.cs, Fc = …Forecast.cs, Aim = …EdictAim.cs, Cast = …ClassSkills.cs. The other abbreviations and the exact locations are at the head of each file of the research notes. The modifier number follows the design order (1–3), and the implementation's modifier number modifier is 0–2.

pages.body:
# Combat positioning panel and movement AI (2026-10-11)

The battle HUD positioning group uses the reference's First Engagement and During Combat tabs. Opening choices are Rush In, Stay Put, Keep Distance and Lure to Chokepoint; combat choices are Pack Center, Stay Put, Keep Distance and Edge. Shared slots, fixed panel height and fixed navigation/undo/play leave only the description and sub-options scrollable when necessary.

## UI and persistence

This is an adapter in `GameUI.EdictSheet`, using `UiSafeArea`, `UiTheme`, `UiFonts`, the existing quick-edit Canvas and transaction. Landscape avoids the settings button. Rotation preserves the selected tab and undo history. Distances span 0–10 m in 0.5 m steps. Drag updates the displayed world radius; release saves through `SheetApply` and `GameStore.CommitHuntEdict`. Stay in my area is a combat-only toggle.

Global v6 appends `position.engageApproach=SKILL`, `position.engageDistanceSource=BASIC_RANGE`, `position.engageDistance=2` and `position.lureMode=NEARBY` without changing v5 option IDs or positional order. Documents and HED2/HED3/HED4/HED5 envelopes retain strict checks against their original version before migration. ORBIT becomes DISTANCE; the hidden clockwise value survives. Hero, legacyEdict and preset copies share canonical migration. Opening and combat distance choices are independent.

## Movement and previews

`ClassSkills.BasicReach` supplies Warrior 2 m and Ranger/Mage 10 m. Opening Walk blocks offensive Leap and support predictions based on Leap while preserving emergency evasions. Opening distance moves both inward and outward with a ±0.75 m deadband.

Chokepoints derive from narrow corridor widths, connected doors and junction entrances. Only explored candidates qualify, sorted by distance, x and y. Known selects the nearest; Scout uses unvisited-exit ranking until it discovers a candidate; Nearby holds position without a known candidate within 8 m. Arrival faces back toward the approach and holds. Incoming damage or the time cap ends the opening. Pack Center finds a legal gap near the observed centroid within 5 m of the target; Edge approaches the outside of the enemy farthest from that centroid. Existing safety, collision, path and transaction checks remain active.

The expected marker ends at the detached simulation's `ForecastHeroPath` endpoint. Reused lines, rings, sprites and shared world labels show the gold dashed expected ring, hero distance ring/range label, known chokepoint or scouting direction, nearby search boundary, and the red observed-pack ring. Close and Play hide previews.

The four supplied PNGs are registered byte for byte. The [asset manifest](../Art/EdictPosition/edict-position-icons-manifest.json) retains hashes, alpha metrics, unknown model provenance and `productionApproved: false`. Mobile uses 128 px ASTC 4×4 and desktop 256 px. Faint alpha dots are preserved for visual review.

## Behavior differences and provisional constants

Default ORBIT becomes fixed 2 m DISTANCE. A stationary target no longer produces continuous circling after the desired distance is reached, changing movement, firing angles, afterimage accumulation and associated passive measurements. The stored `mobile-crossfire` preset ID survives; its label and description now describe 4 m distance keeping and effects triggered by actual distance-adjustment movement.

The planned provisional values are named constants: narrow width 4 m, nearby radius 8 m, opening cap 10 s. Review them with authored chokepoint metadata and corresponding regressions when the owner confirms new values. A saved 0 m distance retains normal actor collision clearance.


Opening Approach stops at basic attack reach independently of combat distance. Stand does not approach an out-of-range target; Edge holds an outer gap rather than circling. Skill regression fixtures and winning puzzle inputs now explicitly select approach/evasion where required. The previous assumption that Edge alone continuously avoids dangerous attacks no longer describes the new mode.

The paired measurement uses level 40, rank 1 class skills, item level 30, no set/legendary gear, a group scenario, 20 seconds and two seeds. Each of three representative builds is measured with all passives and with each of three passives removed: 24 samples before and 24 after.

| Default recommended build | Before mean damage | After mean damage | Change | Survival |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Warrior `BUILD_REF_SW01` | 9,184.2 | 9,509.1 | +3.5% | 2/2 → 2/2 |
| Ranger `BUILD_REF_SA01` | 1,858.6 | 1,852.2 | −0.3% | 2/2 → 2/2 |
| Mage `BUILD_REF_SM03` | 13,882.7 | 13,462.2 | −3.0% | 2/2 → 2/2 |

Paired damage differences against removing a passive are AP09 54.5→60.8, MP01 2,364.5→2,350.6 and MP14 −70.0→−207.9. These depend on positioning and enemy motion; they are not a general balance verdict. Raw [before](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/passive-before.json) and [after](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/passive-after.json) results are retained.

Final-validation corrections reuse the shared owners: BASIC_RANGE combat movement closes inside actual attack reach, legacy simplification imports pass through strict versioned migration, the guide explicitly uses range distance, and Warrior puzzle level 7 explicitly uses pack center. Keyboard selection survives saves and rotation. The PREVENT shield example uses an imminent ranged attack; an early ground telegraph can correctly trigger walking before damage enters shield lookahead.

With the new center movement, puzzle level 15 can clear with one omitted hazard: Warrior without direct dodge takes 526 cumulative HP loss (780 max HP), and Mage without area dodge takes 306 (390 max HP). Their corresponding all-dodge samples take zero HP loss. Tests verify these actual costs and terminal outcomes rather than assuming every omitted single policy necessarily kills the hero.

## Validation and artifact lifecycle

The merged-main full Edit Mode run executed once: 5,742 cases, 5,722 passed, 16 failed and four explicitly skipped. After repairing the connected regressions, all 419 failed/directly affected cases and new regressions passed, including every original failure. Unchanged passing coverage was reused. The 24 passive samples reproduced the same results on the final combat source. Fifteen shared UI contract regressions and static refresh checks (14 bindings/176 sources) pass.

The native macOS development player normally resumed an isolated saved hunt. The final position preview passed all ten KO/EN matrices at 440×956, 956×440, 1600×900, 1600×1000 and 2100×900: persistence, undo, rotation, keyboard focus, fixed geometry, visible hero/endpoint/labels and play/close restoration (exit 0, 31 captures). Actual sheet, graph and top/bottom HUD occlusion was corrected with the existing world camera's viewport and bounds. Floating graphs are hidden only during the preview, with the normal camera/graphs restored on play, close, dimming or page changes.

The previously failed outside tap and remaining four-view panels passed independently (exit 0, 13 captures). Shared Play/Pause captions are distinct from the Renewal equipment affix; two English views passed the caption regression (exit 0, five captures). Unchanged passing potion matrices and skill/potion equip coverage were reused. [Validation summary and source hashes](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/validation-summary.json) record the scope. Physical iOS/Android, the WebGL game player and production live-ops connectivity were not validated.

Actual development player captures:

![KO portrait](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/ko-portrait-distance.png)
![KO landscape](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/ko-landscape-distance.png)
![EN portrait](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/en-portrait-distance.png)
![EN landscape](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/en-landscape-distance.png)
![KO desktop](EdictPositionEvidence20261011/pc-ko-distance.png)

Task outputs are recorded in `validation-codex/artifact-lifecycle.json`. Preserve source, original icons, reports and captures; permanent removal requires approval.

# Completed Work Integration

Updated: 2026-09-28 · [한국어](Completed_Native_Work_Integration_2026_09_28.md)

Completed changes from the separate worktrees were integrated into current `main`, preserving the previously merged tutorial staging and hero/enemy/boss model rendering.

- Added models and textures for N08, N09, N10, N13 and N14.
- Integrated [field environments](Field_Environments.en.md) and [hero skill effects](Hero_Skill_Effects.en.md).
- Connected [new enemy and boss attack sounds](New_Content_Sounds.en.md) to existing recordings.
- Added [battle escape and power saving buttons](Battle_Escape.en.md).
- Set the [new-hero Hunt Edict](Hunt_Edict_Overview.en.md) to Balanced. Existing saved heroes keep their settings.

The training-ground UI wiring remains unfinished, and the user stopped the Web build. These changes and unfinished additional model tooling were preserved in full checkout and Git-history backups, without adding them to the game.

## Integration validation

- **157/157 focused Unity 6000.6.0f1 Edit Mode tests** passed. [Fixture results](CompletedIntegrationEvidence/editmode-summary.txt)
- The shared UI contract and its **9/9 tests**, and **25/25 world-art tests**, passed. All 119 installed world resources passed missing-file, hash and budget checks. The art validator now distinguishes a dynamically concatenated path prefix from a complete filename, with a regression test.
- The macOS development build completed without errors. [Build result](CompletedIntegrationEvidence/build-summary.txt)
- Battle controls passed **24 combinations** of portrait, landscape, PC 16:9/16:10/21:9, Korean/English and text sizes. [Battle controls](CompletedIntegrationEvidence/battle-escape.txt)
- The world, enemy and skill-effect gallery passed **59 scenes**. [Gallery](CompletedIntegrationEvidence/art-gallery.txt)
- The Hunt Edict window passed **20 layout combinations**, pointer actions, defaults, editing and saving, followed by reloading in a separate process. [Window checks](CompletedIntegrationEvidence/edict-overview.txt) · [Reload check](CompletedIntegrationEvidence/edict-reload.txt)

The first Hunt Edict run stopped at its resolution assertion because macOS opened a window at twice the requested size. A fresh process with explicit startup dimensions passed all layout and persistence checks. The unsuccessful attempt was not counted as a pass.

The full Edit Mode suite was not rerun for this integration. Earlier full-suite evidence records 47 existing failures, so these results do not imply an entirely passing full suite. Input acceptance used synthetic macOS pointers; physical-mobile testing is not included.
