pages.title: Monster Codex development plan
pages.summary: 원본의 정책·구현 범위와 검증 내용을 보존합니다.
pages.body:
# Monster Codex development plan

Updated: 2026-10-11 · For: Codex implementation · [한국어](Monster_Codex_Plan_20261011.md)

## 1. Goal

Add a Monster Codex window that records the enemies the player has killed. An enemy with at least one kill shows its portrait, name, stats and skills; one never killed stays hidden as `?` and `???`. On the detail screen a rift tier slider runs from tier 1 to `best clear + 1`; it shows the stats and skill damage that enemy would have if it were placed in a rift of the chosen tier.

## 2. Reference mockup

- Design canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/MgykAGP9nxCmpwthfRN9P4
  - Row 1: landscape 956×440, Korean (list / enemy detail / boss detail)
  - Row 2: landscape 956×440, English
  - Row 3: portrait 440×956, three Korean then three English screens
  - Every screen works. Tap a card to open the detail; the slider, `−`/`+` and the Normal/Elite switch change the numbers.
  - The link is private. For a Codex account to open it, the user has to share it from the Share menu. If it cannot be opened, sections 3–6 of this document are the reference.
- Numbers in the mockup (kill counts, 18/25 discovered, best clear 22) are sample data. The game uses the save data.
- Do not copy hex colours from the mockup. Use the `UiTheme` tokens and `UiFonts`. The mockup colours already come from the Obsidian & Gilt values in `UiTheme`.

## 3. Entry point: HUD content dock icon

- Position: the content dock under the settings gear at the top right of the battle and plaza screens (`AddContentDock` in `GameUI.ContentDock.cs`). The user marked the slot **directly below the Hunt Edict icon**.
  - Implementation: right after `contentDockEdict=Add("사냥 칙령",...)`, add `Add("몬스터 도감","menu-monster-codex",ShowMonsterCodex)`. The Rune Board and Storage move down one slot.
  - The user's screenshot was a tutorial stage battle (Voice of the Edict, level 3). Show the icon under the same conditions as the Hunt Edict, outside the `prologue` branch, so it appears there too. Confirm this with the user (section 9).
- Icon art: a round `menu-monster-codex` medallion made with Codex/GPT image. Variants A and B, the prompt and the manifest are in `Docs/Art/MonsterCodex/`. **The user picked variant A.** Copy `Docs/Art/MonsterCodex/menu-monster-codex-A.png` unchanged to `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Art/GlobalHUD/menu-monster-codex.png` (1254×1254, transparent corners, imported at 512 max). Do not hand-draw it or draw shapes in code.
  - Texture budget: the `Art/GlobalHUD/menu-` row in `ResourceTextureBudget` (512, ASTC 6×6) already covers it, so no new row is needed. Match the import settings of the other `menu-*.png` `.meta` files, and commit the `.meta` Unity rewrites from the build clone.
- Opening behaves like the other dock buttons (Hunt Edict, Storage): opening it in battle pauses the game like those windows, and closing restores it.

## 4. Data

### 4.0 Prerequisite: the monster registry

On 2026-10-11 the user approved a larger roster: 6 fields × 20 monsters plus 18 bosses (N01–N120, B01–B18, 138 in total). A daily routine adds 20 monsters at a time to both the game and the codex. The roster document is `Docs/Design/HELLSCRIPT_Monster_Roster_20261011(.en).md`, currently on the `claude/monster-roster` branch. So the codex follows **the list the registry defines**, not 25 fixed entries.

- Registry contract (branch `claude/monster-registry`, to be merged into `main` before the codex):
  - Data: `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Monsters/MonsterRegistry.json`
  - Runtime: the static class `MonsterRegistry` in `Runtime/Core`
    - `All`: `IReadOnlyList<MonsterDefinition>` in codex order (field order, then ID)
    - `ById(string)`, `ForKind(int kind)`, `ForBoss(int pattern)`
    - `IdOf(EnemyState e)`: bosses map to a B id by pattern, everything else to an N id by kind. Elites count as their base kind; goblins return `null`.
  - `MonsterDefinition`:
    - Identity: `id` ("N01".."N120", "B01".."B18"), `boss`, `kind` (N number − 1, −1 for bosses), `pattern` (B number − 1, −1 for regular monsters)
    - Display: `name` (Korean string key, English in en.txt), `field` (`GameCatalog` field index; bosses have a home field too: B02 fortress, B03 cavern), `role`, `family`, `unlockTier`, `portrait` (Resources path, e.g. `Art/Monsters/Portraits/N21`)
    - Skills: a `skills` list of `{name key, description key, tags, damage multiplier or 0}`
  - The existing 25 keep their current kind/pattern numbers; new monsters are appended.
  - New monsters' stats also come from `CombatSimulation.EnemyStats(kind or pattern …)`. Extending the per-kind multipliers (`KindHealth`/`KindAttack`/`KindSpeed`, `BossCombat.Profile`) belongs to the registry/roster work; the codex keeps no formula of its own.
- **Start condition**: if `MonsterRegistry` is not on `main`, do not start the codex work; tell the user.

### 4.1 Codex entries (registry-driven)

- Entries: all of `MonsterRegistry.All`, in that order. Do not hard-code a table or a count. Today it holds the existing 25; the routine adds 20 a day (138 at the end).
- Field tabs: split by `definition.field`. The tabs are All, the six fields and Boss; the Boss tab is `boss == true`. Compute each tab's `found/total` from the registry every time.
- Names: the `definition.name` string key (`Loc.T`). Field names: `GameCatalog.FieldNames`. A boss's field chip uses `definition.field` (B02 Ruined Fortress, B03 Dank Cavern). Do not use the mockup's `Rift boss` label.
- Strings: the English for existing monsters, fields and boss skills is already in `Localization/en.txt`.
- Shadow wording: the English for `암흑` is **standardized on Shadow** (the user's decision, matching `암흑 저항`=`Shadow Resistance`). Fix the two en.txt lines that still say Dark:
  - `암흑`=`Dark` → `Shadow`
  - `다음 사격 3회에 암흑 추가 피해.`=`Adds dark damage to the next 3 shots.` → `Adds shadow damage to the next 3 shots.`
- Portraits: `definition.portrait`. The existing 25 point at `Art/TrainingGround/Portraits/{N01..N20,B01..B05}`.
- Skill rows:
  - The existing 25: read from the code definitions in 4.3 (`EnemyCombat.OwnHit`, `BossCombat.Hit`, and so on).
  - New monsters: read from `definition.skills`. The element chip comes from the element in its tags (Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Poison, Shadow); leave the damage cell empty when the multiplier is 0.
- Boss skill icons: for existing bosses, `Resources/Art/Boss/skill-{BossCombat.Definition(attack)}.png`. Show the six attacks of `BossCombat.KitOf(pattern)` in order, with `BOSS_ROAR` (Roar) inserted between phase 1 and phase 2. Skills without an icon (normal enemies, new bosses without art yet) are text only.

### 4.2 Kill record (new save field)

- Add kill counts keyed by ID to `AccountSave`:
  ```csharp
  [Serializable] class MonsterKill { public string id; public int count; }
  [Serializable] class MonsterCodexSave { public List<MonsterKill> kills = new(); }
  ```
  - JsonUtility loads a missing list as empty. Old saves start empty; do not rename existing save keys.
- When to record: in `CombatSimulation.Deal`, at the moment an enemy dies (next to `State.kills++`), get the ID with `MonsterRegistry.IdOf(e)` and increment a per-ID counter on the running `RunState`. Add it to the account in the existing `GameStore` path that commits the run settlement. Do not add a second save path.
  - Ignore a `null` ID and any ID not in the registry.
  - Elites and minions follow the `IdOf` rules.
  - What counts (default): real combat counts, including rifts, tutorial and guide stages, and puzzles. **The training ground does not count.** Any enemy can be spawned there, so counting it would fill the codex at once. Confirm with the user (section 9).
  - Keep the counter in the run snapshot and add it once at settlement, so suspend/resume and restore never count a kill twice.
- An entry is discovered when its ID has `count > 0`. The progress bar's total is `MonsterRegistry.All.Count`, which grows every day.

### 4.3 Estimated stats

- Do not write the formula again. Call `CombatSimulation.EnemyStats(stage, kind, elite, boss, pattern, rift: true, introductory: IntroductoryRift.Applies(stage), tuning)`, where `tuning` is the current live-ops rift setting.
  - For reference, with live-ops multipliers at 1: HP = 70×1.08^(tier−1) × kind multiplier (boss 45×profile) × elite 3; attack = 18×1.055^(tier−1) × kind multiplier (boss 3×profile) × elite 1.5. Tiers 1–5 add the introductory reduction. The mockup numbers follow this formula and match the training ground's tier 10 boss (HP 6,297, attack 87).
- Slider range: 1 to `account.Hero.highestClear + 1`, the same rule as rift entry (`RiftEntry`: `run.stage <= highestClear + 1`). It starts at `highestClear` (1 when that is 0).
- Shown values follow the Diablo IV monster composition (4.4): Life, Attack, Movement Speed, Damage type, and Defenses (Physical Resistance, Non-Physical Resistance, Shield, Crowd control, plus Stagger for bosses).
  - Movement Speed is the same at every tier (`Same at every tier`).
  - Sub lines: `+8% per tier` / `+5.5% per tier`; with Elite `Elite ×3` / `Elite ×1.5`; on tiers 1–5 `Intro rift`.
- Skill damage = attack × the skill multiplier. Each skill gets an element chip (Physical, Fire, Cold, Poison, Shadow).
  - Read multipliers and elements from the code instead of writing them in the UI: `EnemyCombat.OwnHit`, the hazards and death effects in `CombatSimulation.Enemies`, `BossCombat.Hit` and `CombatSimulation.Bosses`. `Element` values: 0 Physical, 1 Fire, 2 Cold, 4 Poison, 5 Shadow.
  - Show damage over time per second. For example, ×0.375 every 0.25 s is ×1.5 per second.
  - Leave the damage cell empty for skills with no multiplier (summons, auras, healing).
  - The mockup's multipliers were checked against the code. Examples: Executioner Hook ×1 Physical, Grave Toll ×1 Shadow, Chorister Focused beam ×1.5 Shadow per second, Devourer Chain explosion ×1.5 Shadow each, Tyrant Triple Eruption ×1.2 Fire each, Roar ×0.8 Shadow.

### 4.4 Diablo IV monster composition

The user asked for the monster composition to follow Diablo IV's actual composition. From research (2026-10, including Maxroll's Season 11 elite affix page), a Diablo IV monster is made of the parts below. Monsters have no numeric armor or per-element resistances; resistances, barriers and immunity come only from elite affixes.

| Diablo IV part | In Diablo IV | In our game today | Shown in the codex |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monster level | Damage dealt and taken is adjusted by the level gap with the hero | Rift tier scaling | Rift tier slider |
| Rank | Normal / Elite (more Life and damage, 2–4 affixes) / Minion (spawns with an Elite, more Life) / Boss | Normal / Elite (Life ×3, attack ×1.5, 1–2 traits) / Boss | Rank chip, Normal/Elite switch |
| Life and damage | From rank and level | `EnemyStats` | Life, Attack |
| Damage types | Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Poison, Shadow | Physical, Fire, Cold, Poison, Shadow (no enemy uses Lightning) | Damage type chips, per-skill element chip |
| Physical / Non-Physical Resistance | Only from the `Physical Resistance` / `Non-Physical Resistance` affixes | None. The elite traits Life link (-20% damage taken) and Volley barrier (-50% from frontal projectiles) play a similar role | 0%; for elites, "Only from traits" |
| Barrier | The `Reprisal` affix occasionally grants a Barrier worth 25% of max Life | None | None |
| Immune / Unstoppable | The `Shielded` (immune for a few seconds) and `Unstoppable` affixes | None | (shown as elite trait rows once built) |
| Boss crowd control | CC does not apply; it fills the stagger gauge, and a full gauge staggers the boss for a while | Immune to root, stun and freeze (slow applies); Stagger 100 → incapacitated 3 s → immune 10 s | Crowd control "Immune", Stagger cell |
| Elite affixes | 30+ (fire, cold, lightning, poison, shadow and generic families) | E01–E07 (below) | "Elite traits" group when Elite is selected |

The closest Diablo IV affix to each of our traits (reference only; never show Diablo IV names in the game):

| Our trait | Closest Diablo IV affix |
|---|---|
| E01 Homing flame | Mortar / Fire Enchanted |
| E02 Ice ring | Frozen |
| E03 Life link | Life Link |
| E04 Volley barrier | Suppressor |
| E05 Corpse blast | (none, ours only) |
| E06 Rage buildup | Berserker / Soul Drinker |
| E07 Gravity Collapse | Tempest |

**First codex build**: implement only the "Shown in the codex" column. Every value is one the game already has. Do not add new combat rules.

**Follow-up candidates (separate steps, after the user approves)**: moving the Diablo IV composition into combat itself needs the items below. Each changes combat balance, so each needs a before/after rift simulation on the same seeds.
1. Raise elite traits from 1–2 to 2–4.
2. A Minion rank: more Life for normal enemies that spawn with an elite. Diablo IV publishes no multiplier, so a design value is needed.
3. New elite traits: Physical Resistance, Non-Physical Resistance, Reprisal (Barrier worth 25% of max Life), Shielded (immune for a few seconds), Unstoppable, and other Diablo IV affixes.
   - Resistance percentages and immunity times are not published for Diablo IV, so design values are needed.
   - Enemy barrier and immunity need new HUD feedback.
4. An enemy that deals Lightning damage. None does today.
5. Boss stagger length: Diablo IV gives at least about 12 s; ours incapacitates for 3 s.
6. Level-gap damage adjustment between hero level and rift tier.

Sources:
- [Maxroll: Elite and Affixes Overview](https://maxroll.gg/d4/resources/elites-affixes) (updated 2025-12-09, Season 11): elites carry 2–4 affixes; minions have more Life; the Physical/Non-Physical Resistance, Reprisal barrier, Shielded and Unstoppable affixes.
- [Fextralife: Stats and Attributes](https://diablo4.wiki.fextralife.com/Stats_and_Attributes): level-gap damage adjustment.
- [PureDiablo: Stagger Meter](https://www.purediablo.com/diablo4/Stagger_Meter), [WePC: How to Stagger Bosses](https://www.wepc.com/gaming/how-to-stagger-bosses-in-diablo-4/): boss CC immunity and the stagger gauge.
- Only normal enemies have the Normal/Elite switch. Bosses show a `Boss grade` chip instead.

## 5. Screens

Common: create `MonsterCodexWindow` (`ContentWindowView`) with `python3 tools/new_content_ui.py MonsterCodex`, and use the shared title, back button, scrolling and safe area. The list and the detail switch inside one window, as in the mockup. Back returns from the detail to the list, and from the list closes the window.

### 5.1 List

- Header: back, the `HELLSCRIPT` wordmark (landscape only), the title `Monster Codex`, and on the right a `Discovered` progress bar with `18 / 25`. In portrait, hide the wordmark and shorten the bar.
- Field tabs: All, the six fields, Boss. Each tab shows `found/total`. Tabs scroll horizontally when they overflow.
- Grid: 8 columns in landscape, 4 in portrait. The entry count grows daily up to 138, so the grid scrolls vertically and must cope with that many cards (reuse the shared scroll parts, e.g. a recycled list or skipping off-screen cards). Each card has a square portrait with the codex ID at the bottom right. Bosses get a `Boss` band at the top left and a gold border. Below the portrait: name and `Killed N`.
- Undiscovered card: a disabled button showing `?` instead of the portrait, `???` as the name and `Undiscovered`. Tapping it does nothing.
- At the user's request, leave out the "Any enemy you have killed is recorded" hint.

### 5.2 Detail

- Landscape: on the left, a 230 px portrait panel with a rank chip (Normal/Elite/Boss), a kill chip, ID, name, and field and role chips. On the right:
  - one row of four tiles: Life, Attack, Movement Speed, Damage type chips
  - one Defenses row: Physical Resistance, Non-Physical Resistance, Shield, Crowd control, plus a Stagger cell for bosses
  - a scrolling skill list. Switching to Elite adds an `Elite traits · 1–2 at random` group (E01–E06) at the top.
  - Fixed bottom bar: the `Rift tier` label with `Best clear: tier N`, `−`, the slider (with a tick at the best clear), `+`, the large tier number with a status line (`Cleared` / `Next challenge` / `Intro rift reduction`), and the Normal/Elite switch.
- Portrait: the portrait panel spans the full width at the top (about 260 high), the stats and the defenses each form a 2×2 grid (three rows of defenses for bosses), and the skill list scrolls in the remaining height. The bottom bar has two rows: label, tier number and grade on the first; `−`, slider and `+` on the second.
- Skill row:
  - Bosses only: a 44 px icon with a gold border for phase 1 and a red border for phase 2 and Roar.
  - Name and a tag chip (Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase shift, On death, Weak spot, Healing, Aura, Poison, Fire, Cold, Slowed, 2 hits).
  - Description.
  - On the right: damage (`Damage`, `Damage per sec`, `Damage each`, `Damage every 0.5 s`) and `Attack ×mult`.
- Touch targets are at least 44 px. The slider supports both dragging and `−`/`+`.

## 6. Text and localization

- Put every string through the string table keys (`Loc.T`/`Loc.F`) and fill the English in `en.txt`, following the mockup's English.
  - New keys, for example:
    - 몬스터 도감=Monster Codex, 발견한 적=Discovered, 미발견=Undiscovered, 처치 {0}=Killed {0}
    - 생명력=Life, 피해 유형=Damage type, 방어 구성=Defenses, 물리 저항=Physical Resistance, 군중 제어=Crowd control, 모두 적용=All apply, 면역=Immune, 제압=Stagger, 정예 속성=Elite traits
    - 피해 감소 없음=No damage reduction, 단계와 무관=Same at every tier, 사용 기술=Skills
    - 최고 클리어 {0}단계=Best clear: tier {0}, 다음 도전 단계=Next challenge, 클리어한 단계=Cleared, 입문 균열 보정 적용=Intro rift reduction
    - 보스 등급=Boss grade, 1페이즈=Phase 1, 2페이즈=Phase 2, 페이즈 전환=Phase shift, 사망 시=On death
    - 근접 추적=Melee chaser, 사망 폭발=Death burst
  - Element keys exist too: 물리=Physical, 화염=Fire, 냉기=Cold, 독=Poison, 비물리 저항=Non-Physical Resistance, 보스 제압=Boss staggered. The English for `암흑` is **standardized on Shadow** (the user's decision, matching `암흑 저항`=`Shadow Resistance`). Fix the two en.txt lines that still say Dark: `암흑`=`Dark`→`Shadow`, and `다음 사격 3회에 암흑 추가 피해.`=`Adds dark damage to the next 3 shots.`→`Adds shadow damage to the next 3 shots.`
  - Existing keys: 균열 단계=Rift tier, 정예=Elite, 일반=Normal, 보스=Boss, 공격력=Attack power, 이동 속도=Movement Speed, 원거리=Ranged, 장판=Zone, 지원=Support, and all monster, field and boss skill names.
  - The skill names and descriptions of normal enemies and the boss skill descriptions are new text. Use the mockup's Korean and English as written.
- Key template trap: keys shaped like `{0}/{1}` have swallowed saved combat lines before. Give new keys names that do not collide with existing ones.

## 7. Verification

- EditMode:
  - Kills are recorded per kind: elites under their base kind, bosses by pattern, minions under their own kind.
  - The training ground is excluded, and suspend/restore never counts a kill twice.
  - Loading an old save gives an empty kill list.
  - Detail values equal `EnemyStats` at tiers 1, 5, 6 and best+1, and for elites.
  - Each skill's element and multiplier match the code (`EnemyCombat.OwnHit`, `BossCombat.Hit`, hazards and death effects).
  - Boss defenses match the real rules: immune to root, stun and freeze, slow applies, Stagger 100 → 3 s → immune 10 s.
  - The slider range is 1 to highestClear+1, and undiscovered entries do not open.
  - Iterate the registry (never a hard-coded count): every entry has Korean and English names, a portrait and `EnemyStats` values. Existing bosses' skill icons load too.
  - Kills of an ID not in the registry, or where `IdOf` is `null`, are not saved.
  - With a test registry that has one extra entry, the list, tab counts and progress-bar total follow automatically.
  - No Korean or English string shows as empty or as a key name.
- UI contract: `python3 tools/check_ui_contract.py --verify`.
- Native check (macOS development build smoke): capture these at portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440 and PC 16:9/16:10/21:9, in Korean and English. Check for clipping, overlap and touch target size. Do not run text-size tests.
  - The dock icon position (below the Hunt Edict)
  - The list
  - A normal enemy detail
  - A boss detail
- Run the full EditMode suite and the runtime smokes once, after the last code change and the `main` integration. Follow the wiki publishing procedure at merge.

## 8. Suggested steps

0. Check that `MonsterRegistry` is on `main` (4.0). If not, stop and tell the user.
1. Save field, kill recording and tests.
2. `MonsterCodexWindow` list and detail (landscape) and the string keys.
3. Portrait layout, boss skill icons and the Roar row.
4. Dock icon resource and the `ContentDock` entry point.
5. Native captures, UI contract, documentation and wiki.

## 9. Open questions for the user

1. Whether to take on the follow-up candidates in 4.4 (moving the Diablo IV composition into combat rules), and if so which first. The first codex build goes ahead either way.
2. Should training ground kills count (default: no)?
3. Should the codex icon also show in the prologue and tutorial screens (default: yes, like the Hunt Edict, per the screenshot)?

Decided: the dock icon is variant A; the English for `암흑` is Shadow; the codex list is driven by `MonsterRegistry` (requested by the roster session, 2026-10-11).
pages.html:
Updated: 2026-10-11 · For: Codex implementation · 한국어

1. Goal

Add a Monster Codex window that records the enemies the player has killed. An enemy with at least one kill shows its portrait, name, stats and skills; one never killed stays hidden as ? and ???. On the detail screen a rift tier slider runs from tier 1 to best clear + 1; it shows the stats and skill damage that enemy would have if it were placed in a rift of the chosen tier.

2. Reference mockup

  • Design canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/MgykAGP9nxCmpwthfRN9P4
  • Row 1: landscape 956×440, Korean (list / enemy detail / boss detail)
  • Row 2: landscape 956×440, English
  • Row 3: portrait 440×956, three Korean then three English screens
  • Every screen works. Tap a card to open the detail; the slider, −/+ and the Normal/Elite switch change the numbers.
  • The link is private. For a Codex account to open it, the user has to share it from the Share menu. If it cannot be opened, sections 3–6 of this document are the reference.
  • Numbers in the mockup (kill counts, 18/25 discovered, best clear 22) are sample data. The game uses the save data.
  • Do not copy hex colours from the mockup. Use the UiTheme tokens and UiFonts. The mockup colours already come from the Obsidian & Gilt values in UiTheme.

3. Entry point: HUD content dock icon

  • Position: the content dock under the settings gear at the top right of the battle and plaza screens (AddContentDock in GameUI.ContentDock.cs). The user marked the slot directly below the Hunt Edict icon.
  • Implementation: right after contentDockEdict=Add("사냥 칙령",...), add Add("몬스터 도감","menu-monster-codex",ShowMonsterCodex). The Rune Board and Storage move down one slot.
  • The user's screenshot was a tutorial stage battle (Voice of the Edict, level 3). Show the icon under the same conditions as the Hunt Edict, outside the prologue branch, so it appears there too. Confirm this with the user (section 9).
  • Icon art: a round menu-monster-codex medallion made with Codex/GPT image. Variants A and B, the prompt and the manifest are in Docs/Art/MonsterCodex/. The user picked variant A. Copy Docs/Art/MonsterCodex/menu-monster-codex-A.png unchanged to Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Art/GlobalHUD/menu-monster-codex.png (1254×1254, transparent corners, imported at 512 max). Do not hand-draw it or draw shapes in code.
  • Texture budget: the Art/GlobalHUD/menu- row in ResourceTextureBudget (512, ASTC 6×6) already covers it, so no new row is needed. Match the import settings of the other menu-*.png .meta files, and commit the .meta Unity rewrites from the build clone.
  • Opening behaves like the other dock buttons (Hunt Edict, Storage): opening it in battle pauses the game like those windows, and closing restores it.

4. Data

4.0 Prerequisite: the monster registry

On 2026-10-11 the user approved a larger roster: 6 fields × 20 monsters plus 18 bosses (N01–N120, B01–B18, 138 in total). A daily routine adds 20 monsters at a time to both the game and the codex. The roster document is Docs/Design/HELLSCRIPT_Monster_Roster_20261011(.en).md, currently on the claude/monster-roster branch. So the codex follows the list the registry defines, not 25 fixed entries.

  • Registry contract (branch claude/monster-registry, to be merged into main before the codex):
  • Data: Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Monsters/MonsterRegistry.json
  • Runtime: the static class MonsterRegistry in Runtime/Core
  • All: IReadOnlyList<MonsterDefinition> in codex order (field order, then ID)
  • ById(string), ForKind(int kind), ForBoss(int pattern)
  • IdOf(EnemyState e): bosses map to a B id by pattern, everything else to an N id by kind. Elites count as their base kind; goblins return null.
  • MonsterDefinition:
  • Identity: id ("N01".."N120", "B01".."B18"), boss, kind (N number − 1, −1 for bosses), pattern (B number − 1, −1 for regular monsters)
  • Display: name (Korean string key, English in en.txt), field (GameCatalog field index; bosses have a home field too: B02 fortress, B03 cavern), role, family, unlockTier, portrait (Resources path, e.g. Art/Monsters/Portraits/N21)
  • Skills: a skills list of {name key, description key, tags, damage multiplier or 0}
  • The existing 25 keep their current kind/pattern numbers; new monsters are appended.
  • New monsters' stats also come from CombatSimulation.EnemyStats(kind or pattern …). Extending the per-kind multipliers (KindHealth/KindAttack/KindSpeed, BossCombat.Profile) belongs to the registry/roster work; the codex keeps no formula of its own.
  • Start condition: if MonsterRegistry is not on main, do not start the codex work; tell the user.

4.1 Codex entries (registry-driven)

  • Entries: all of MonsterRegistry.All, in that order. Do not hard-code a table or a count. Today it holds the existing 25; the routine adds 20 a day (138 at the end).
  • Field tabs: split by definition.field. The tabs are All, the six fields and Boss; the Boss tab is boss == true. Compute each tab's found/total from the registry every time.
  • Names: the definition.name string key (Loc.T). Field names: GameCatalog.FieldNames. A boss's field chip uses definition.field (B02 Ruined Fortress, B03 Dank Cavern). Do not use the mockup's Rift boss label.
  • Strings: the English for existing monsters, fields and boss skills is already in Localization/en.txt.
  • Shadow wording: the English for 암흑 is standardized on Shadow (the user's decision, matching 암흑 저항=Shadow Resistance). Fix the two en.txt lines that still say Dark:
  • 암흑=Dark → Shadow
  • 다음 사격 3회에 암흑 추가 피해.=Adds dark damage to the next 3 shots. → Adds shadow damage to the next 3 shots.
  • Portraits: definition.portrait. The existing 25 point at Art/TrainingGround/Portraits/{N01..N20,B01..B05}.
  • Skill rows:
  • The existing 25: read from the code definitions in 4.3 (EnemyCombat.OwnHit, BossCombat.Hit, and so on).
  • New monsters: read from definition.skills. The element chip comes from the element in its tags (Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Poison, Shadow); leave the damage cell empty when the multiplier is 0.
  • Boss skill icons: for existing bosses, Resources/Art/Boss/skill-{BossCombat.Definition(attack)}.png. Show the six attacks of BossCombat.KitOf(pattern) in order, with BOSS_ROAR (Roar) inserted between phase 1 and phase 2. Skills without an icon (normal enemies, new bosses without art yet) are text only.

4.2 Kill record (new save field)

  • Add kill counts keyed by ID to AccountSave:
  [Serializable] class MonsterKill { public string id; public int count; }
  [Serializable] class MonsterCodexSave { public List<MonsterKill> kills = new(); }
  • JsonUtility loads a missing list as empty. Old saves start empty; do not rename existing save keys.
  • When to record: in CombatSimulation.Deal, at the moment an enemy dies (next to State.kills++), get the ID with MonsterRegistry.IdOf(e) and increment a per-ID counter on the running RunState. Add it to the account in the existing GameStore path that commits the run settlement. Do not add a second save path.
  • Ignore a null ID and any ID not in the registry.
  • Elites and minions follow the IdOf rules.
  • What counts (default): real combat counts, including rifts, tutorial and guide stages, and puzzles. The training ground does not count. Any enemy can be spawned there, so counting it would fill the codex at once. Confirm with the user (section 9).
  • Keep the counter in the run snapshot and add it once at settlement, so suspend/resume and restore never count a kill twice.
  • An entry is discovered when its ID has count > 0. The progress bar's total is MonsterRegistry.All.Count, which grows every day.

4.3 Estimated stats

  • Do not write the formula again. Call CombatSimulation.EnemyStats(stage, kind, elite, boss, pattern, rift: true, introductory: IntroductoryRift.Applies(stage), tuning), where tuning is the current live-ops rift setting.
  • For reference, with live-ops multipliers at 1: HP = 70×1.08^(tier−1) × kind multiplier (boss 45×profile) × elite 3; attack = 18×1.055^(tier−1) × kind multiplier (boss 3×profile) × elite 1.5. Tiers 1–5 add the introductory reduction. The mockup numbers follow this formula and match the training ground's tier 10 boss (HP 6,297, attack 87).
  • Slider range: 1 to account.Hero.highestClear + 1, the same rule as rift entry (RiftEntry: run.stage <= highestClear + 1). It starts at highestClear (1 when that is 0).
  • Shown values follow the Diablo IV monster composition (4.4): Life, Attack, Movement Speed, Damage type, and Defenses (Physical Resistance, Non-Physical Resistance, Shield, Crowd control, plus Stagger for bosses).
  • Movement Speed is the same at every tier (Same at every tier).
  • Sub lines: +8% per tier / +5.5% per tier; with Elite Elite ×3 / Elite ×1.5; on tiers 1–5 Intro rift.
  • Skill damage = attack × the skill multiplier. Each skill gets an element chip (Physical, Fire, Cold, Poison, Shadow).
  • Read multipliers and elements from the code instead of writing them in the UI: EnemyCombat.OwnHit, the hazards and death effects in CombatSimulation.Enemies, BossCombat.Hit and CombatSimulation.Bosses. Element values: 0 Physical, 1 Fire, 2 Cold, 4 Poison, 5 Shadow.
  • Show damage over time per second. For example, ×0.375 every 0.25 s is ×1.5 per second.
  • Leave the damage cell empty for skills with no multiplier (summons, auras, healing).
  • The mockup's multipliers were checked against the code. Examples: Executioner Hook ×1 Physical, Grave Toll ×1 Shadow, Chorister Focused beam ×1.5 Shadow per second, Devourer Chain explosion ×1.5 Shadow each, Tyrant Triple Eruption ×1.2 Fire each, Roar ×0.8 Shadow.

4.4 Diablo IV monster composition

The user asked for the monster composition to follow Diablo IV's actual composition. From research (2026-10, including Maxroll's Season 11 elite affix page), a Diablo IV monster is made of the parts below. Monsters have no numeric armor or per-element resistances; resistances, barriers and immunity come only from elite affixes.

Diablo IV partIn Diablo IVIn our game todayShown in the codex
Monster levelDamage dealt and taken is adjusted by the level gap with the heroRift tier scalingRift tier slider
RankNormal / Elite (more Life and damage, 2–4 affixes) / Minion (spawns with an Elite, more Life) / BossNormal / Elite (Life ×3, attack ×1.5, 1–2 traits) / BossRank chip, Normal/Elite switch

First codex build: implement only the "Shown in the codex" column. Every value is one the game already has. Do not add new combat rules.

  1. Raise elite traits from 1–2 to 2–4.
  2. A Minion rank: more Life for normal enemies that spawn with an elite. Diablo IV publishes no multiplier, so a design value is needed.
  3. New elite traits: Physical Resistance, Non-Physical Resistance, Reprisal (Barrier worth 25% of max Life), Shielded (immune for a few seconds), Unstoppable, and other Diablo IV affixes.
  4. Resistance percentages and immunity times are not published for Diablo IV, so design values are needed.
  5. Enemy barrier and immunity need new HUD feedback.
  6. An enemy that deals Lightning damage. None does today.
  7. Boss stagger length: Diablo IV gives at least about 12 s; ours incapacitates for 3 s.
  8. Level-gap damage adjustment between hero level and rift tier.

Sources:

  • Maxroll: Elite and Affixes Overview (updated 2025-12-09, Season 11): elites carry 2–4 affixes; minions have more Life; the Physical/Non-Physical Resistance, Reprisal barrier, Shielded and Unstoppable affixes.
  • Fextralife: Stats and Attributes: level-gap damage adjustment.
  • PureDiablo: Stagger Meter, WePC: How to Stagger Bosses: boss CC immunity and the stagger gauge.

5. Screens

Common: create MonsterCodexWindow (ContentWindowView) with python3 tools/new_content_ui.py MonsterCodex, and use the shared title, back button, scrolling and safe area. The list and the detail switch inside one window, as in the mockup. Back returns from the detail to the list, and from the list closes the window.

  • Grid: 8 columns in landscape, 4 in portrait. The entry count grows daily up to 138, so the grid scrolls vertically and must cope with that many cards (reuse the shared scroll parts, e.g. a recycled list or skipping off-screen cards).   • Landscape: on the left, a 230 px portrait panel with a rank chip (Normal/Elite/Boss), a kill chip, ID, name, and field and role chips. On the right:
  • one row of four tiles: Life, Attack, Movement Speed, Damage type chips

  • Bosses only: a 44 px icon with a gold border for phase 1 and a red border for phase 2 and Roar.

  • Description.

  • Touch targets are at least 44 px. The slider supports both dragging and −/+.

pages.body:
# Monster Codex implementation record

Date: 2026-10-11 · [한국어](Monster_Codex_Implementation_20261011.md)

## Scope and base

Start from `23ed052c` (`origin/claude/monster-registry`) on `codex/monster-codex`, as explicitly authorized by the user. This replaces the plan's main-first prerequisite. Use the registry contracts and skills(tags/damage/icon), without hard-coded roster counts. Combat balance is unchanged.

Defaults: exclude training and tutorial replays; include real tutorials, the guide and puzzles; place the dock icon immediately below Hunt Edict, including the prologue. Merge main and merge this PR only after the registry has reached main.

## Progress

1. Save and kill tracking: complete. Persist ID counters and a settlement flag in the run snapshot; settle through existing GameStore writes and tutorial transactions. Restore codex data and flags on failed disk writes. Ignore unknown IDs, training and replays.
2. List, landscape detail and localization: complete. Read entries, field tabs and denominators from the registry, lock undiscovered cards, and share EnemyStats and combat skill coefficients. Convert sustained damage using its actual tick interval; update values without rebuilding the slider during drags. Both requested Dark translations now use Shadow. The current combat implementation converts boss slows into stagger, which the view describes.

# Monster Day 1: Registry, Data Combat and Hunyuan Models

Updated: 2026-10-12 · [한국어](Monster_Day1_Integration_20261012.md)

The foundation for adding the [monster roster per field](../Design/HELLSCRIPT_Monster_Roster_20261011.en.md) to the game 20 a day, and the day-1 result. The daily procedure is [adding 20 monsters a day](Monster_Daily_Pipeline.en.md); model conversion rules are in the [Hunyuan monster READY pipeline](Hunyuan_Monster_Ready_Pipeline.en.md).

## What landed

- **Monster registry** `Resources/Monsters/MonsterRegistry.json` and `MonsterRegistry`. The existing 25 (N01–N20, B01–B05) are described with their current kinds, patterns and numbers; new monsters fight from registry data. The Monster Codex reads this list (plan: [Monster Codex plan](Monster_Codex_Plan_20261011.en.md)).
- **Data combat**: attack parts (melee, projectiles, charge, leap, burrow, zones, support, summons), traits (auras, frontal reduction, retaliation, ambush, treasure and more), breakable structures (totems, banners, lanterns, cages, walls) and hero states (skill seal, curse, poison stacks, reduced vision). All 138 roster entries are written in this form with nothing deferred. Hunt Edict target types also come from the registry role.
- **Shipped**: N21, N22, N23, N33 and B06 are registered and spawn in rifts. They have no model or portrait yet (`artPending`) and show the primitive figure; the daily routine fills them from the day-2 generation.
- **20 Hunyuan models** (day 1): N01 N03 N04 N05 N06 N07 N09 N10 N11 N14 N15 N16 N17 N18 N19 N20, B01 B02 B04 B05, after automatic reduction (LOD 6,000/3,000/1,500, bosses 12,000/6,000/3,000), automatic rigging and a reviewed QA sheet. N08 was left out because its tunic lifted with the arm; it keeps its old model and will be regenerated with a new prompt.
- **19 Codex portraits** painted from the chosen model render, replacing the same IDs in `Resources/Art/TrainingGround/Portraits/`; records in `Docs/Art/Monsters/portrait-manifest.json`.
- **Daily routine tools** in `tools/monster_pipeline/` and the routine prompt `ROUTINE_PROMPT.md`.

## Fixed problems

- Five melee attacks (N21, N35, N42, N73, N85) started at a distance longer than their reach and always missed; their start distance now equals the reach. The registry tool rejects such data and `MonsterEngagementTests` checks that every data monster and boss of the full roster actually hits a standing hero.
- The skill text key `자폭` collided with the Hunt Edict target label (`EXPLODER`); it is now `자폭 돌진` (Self-Destruct Rush).

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Full EditMode (merge candidate after merging main) | 5,949 tests: 5,945 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped (54 min) |
| Related EditMode for the later changes (registry, combat, soak, field, server replay, READY, Hunt Edict targets + new `MonsterEngagementTests`) | 236 of 238 passed. The two new tests failed on their own setup (ambushers placed outside their wake radius, a boss threshold of two hits); after fixing the test `MonsterEngagementTests` passed 2/2 (the other 236 were not rerun because only the test file changed) |
| `tools/test_monster_registry.py`, `monster_registry.py validate` | 10/10, OK |
| `check_ui_contract.py --verify` | 15 OK |
| macOS development build runtime smoke `-hellscriptMonsterModelsSmoke` (1600×900) | Pass: 25/25 READY models shown as models; the four data monsters and boss B06 landed warned attacks (evidence: [boss-B01](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/boss-B01.jpg) · [boss-B02](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/boss-B02.jpg) · [boss-B03](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/boss-B03.jpg) · [boss-B04](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/boss-B04.jpg) · [boss-B05](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/boss-B05.jpg) · [boss-B06](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/boss-B06.jpg) · [fight-B06](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/fight-B06.jpg) · [fight-N21](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/fight-N21.jpg) · [fight-N22](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/fight-N22.jpg) · [fight-N23](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/fight-N23.jpg) · [fight-N33](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/fight-N33.jpg) · [lineup-N01-N05](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/lineup-N01-N05.jpg) · [lineup-N06-N10](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/lineup-N06-N10.jpg) · [lineup-N11-N15](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/lineup-N11-N15.jpg) · [lineup-N16-N20](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/lineup-N16-N20.jpg) · [lineup-N21-N33](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/lineup-N21-N33.jpg) · [runtime-monster-models-smoke](MonsterModelsEvidence20261012/runtime-monster-models-smoke.txt)) |

## Not verified

Physical devices (Android, iOS), APK and web build size (the HunyuanReady source PNGs in the repo are 197 MB; build size is after compression and must be measured separately), frame time and draw calls, the full runtime smoke bundle (only the new smoke related to this change ran), and public distribution approval of Hunyuan output (`productionApproved: false`).

# Monster Roster per Field and Hunyuan Model Plan

Updated: 2026-10-11 · [한국어](HELLSCRIPT_Monster_Roster_20261011.md)

This plan gives each of the six rift fields at least 20 regular monsters and at least 3 bosses: 120 regular monsters (20 existing + 100 new) and 18 bosses (5 existing + 13 new), 138 in total. Models are made with the Tencent HY 3D (Hunyuan) free allowance of 20 generations per day, 20 per day in the priority order below. Field rules follow [Six Rift Fields](HELLSCRIPT_Rift_Fields.en.md); existing enemy and boss numbers follow the [regular enemy and elite detail](HELLSCRIPT_Enemy_Combat_Detail.md) and the [boss combat detail](HELLSCRIPT_Boss_Combat_Detail.en.md).

## 1. Design principles

- **Look and feel**: as in Diablo IV, monsters are grouped into families, and one field shares materials and colours. Grim realistic gothic fantasy, weathered materials, bold silhouettes that read from the high top-down camera. The dark painterly portraits in `Resources/Art/TrainingGround/Portraits` are the reference. No gore such as wounds or exposed flesh.
- **One question per monster**: every monster asks the player (that is, the Hunt Edict) one question: whom to hit first, where to step, when to cast, whether to keep a movement skill, area or single-target damage. The `Edict test` column names that question.
- **Always avoidable**: all damage is shown first with the existing telegraph gauge (circle, ring, cone, line). No unavoidable damage, no loss of control longer than 1.5 s, no slow above 60%. As today, a projectile volley hits at most once per cast.
- **Roles inside a field**: each field has 5–6 melee, 2–3 charge or leap, 3 ranged, 3 zone or control, 3 support or summoner, 2 death effects and 1–2 special (ambush, stationary structure, treasure) monsters. A field never repeats a mechanic.
- **Numbers**: the stats and patterns of the existing 20 do not change. Numbers for new monsters are draft values; implementation fits them to the existing `EnemyCombat` shapes and the same damage-per-second budget (melee slot within ±15% of N01).
- **Current spawn table**: the current table (fields other than the graveyard share N02–N05) stays; new monsters shipped in the registry join the same role slot of their own field from their unlock tier (section 11).

## 2. Field summary

| Field | From tier | Families | Existing regular | New regular | Bosses |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Forgotten Graveyard | 1 | Risen corpses, skeleton legion, wraiths, grave cult, grave beasts | N01–N06 | N21–N34 (14) | B01 Executioner · B06 Bone Matron · B07 Crypt Lich |
| Dank Cavern | 1 | Cave ghouls, fungus, spiders, the drowned, rift crystal, cave beasts | N15–N16 | N35–N52 (18) | B03 Devourer · B08 Brood Queen · B09 Drowned Abyss King |
| Dusk Grassland | 1 | Thornhorn beastmen, werewolves and wolves, briar coven, standing stones and spirits | N17–N18 | N53–N70 (18) | B10 Thornhorn Warchief · B11 Dusk Wolf King · B12 Briar Mother |
| Ruined Fortress | 11 | Penitent order, fanatics, ember cult, cathedral statues, hell minions | N07–N12 | N71–N84 (14) | B02 Chorister · B13 Iron Inquisitor · B14 Forge Lord |
| Scorched Desert | 11 | Dune raiders, sandworms and beetles, tomb mummies, serpent cult, fire spirits | N13–N14 | N85–N102 (18) | B04 Tyrant · B15 Sand Pharaoh · B16 Sun-Eater Djinn |
| Snowbound Highland | 11 | Frost revenants, frost cult, snowfield beasts, ice spirits | N19–N20 | N103–N120 (18) | B05 Matriarch · B17 Frost Giant King · B18 Revenant King of the Ice Crown |

B02 and B03 had no fixed field. Here the Chorister belongs to the fortress (cathedral choir) and the Devourer to the cavern (rift crystal beast).

## 3. Forgotten Graveyard (wet flagstones, pale moonlight, teal fog)

The tiers in the table are where the new bosses (B06–B18) unlock in their home field. **Actual selection rule (implemented)**: the existing five bosses are picked first by the existing stage rule regardless of field (unlocking at tiers 1/11/21/31/41), and when a shipped data boss has this field as its home and its tier is reached, the two are pooled and the layout's hash picks one. So the cavern's Brood Queen and the grassland's Thornhorn Warchief are drawn alongside the Executioner from tier 1 (they do not replace it), and existing seeds keep their boss in every field and tier without a shipped data boss. Before tiers 31/41, the desert and highland keep showing other fields' existing bosses as today.

## 10. Hunyuan model plan

### 10.1 Daily allocation of 20

| Day | Targets | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 (2026-10-11) | N11, N15–N20, B04, B05 with no dedicated model; procedural N01, N03–N10, B01, B02 (20) | Replace enemies that already appear in the game |
| D2 | N14, graveyard N21–N34, B06, B07, cavern N35–N37 (20) | Tier-1 fields; finish the first field, the graveyard |
| D3 | Cavern N38–N52, B08, B09, grassland N53–N55 (20) | Tier-1 field |
| D4 | Grassland N56–N70, B10–B12, fortress N71, N72 (20) | Tier-1 field |
| D5 | Fortress N73–N84, B13, B14, desert N85–N90 (20) | Tier-11 field |
| D6 | Desert N91–N102, B15, B16, highland N103–N108 (20) | Tier-11 field |
| D7 | Highland N109–N120, B17, B18 (14) + 6 spare for regeneration | Tier-11 field, regenerate failures |

N02, N12, N13 and B03 already have Hunyuan models and are not regenerated. 134 models are generated over 7 days. A result that fails the silhouette, pose or material review is regenerated on the next day's spare slots; failures push the later order back by a day.

### 10.2 Generation procedure

- Site: https://hy3d.tencent.ai/ AI Creation → Text-to-3D, `3DGeneration-V3.1`, 50k faces, PBR. One request uses one of the daily generations and makes 4 candidates. At most 3 run at once (a 4th submission is refused with `The current concurrency exceeds the limit` and does not use the allowance).
- The user signs in by hand in the in-app browser. Submissions carry a signature, so they go through the page's text box and `Generate Now` button; results are read with `GET /api/3d/creations/detail?creationsId=…`.
- Prompt form (500 characters at most): `Full-body <appearance>. Neutral stance, limbs slightly apart from the body. Single isolated creature, no ground, base or background. Grim realistic dark gothic ARPG style, bold readable silhouette, weathered PBR materials, complete back.` The appearance follows the portraits and the concepts here, with the field colour as accent (graveyard teal, cavern teal fungus, grassland rose and violet, fortress orange embers, desert amber, highland ice blue).
- Of the 4 candidates, pick the one with the clearest silhouette, limbs apart from the body for rigging, and no ground or base.
- Original GLBs, prompts, hashes and selection reasons live outside the repository in `AssetDeliverables/Hunyuan/2026-10-11/` (and a folder per later day). Downloads happen after the user allows them.

### 10.3 In-game use (follow-up work)

- Reduction: bake with the existing `optimize_all.py --game` pipeline to 6,000 triangles and 512 px for regular monsters, 6,000–12,000 triangles and 1024 px for bosses.
- Rigging: install into `Resources/World/HunyuanReady/` with the existing `HunyuanReady` pivot rig (`Biped`, `Quadruped` and so on; N02, N12 and BOSS03 are the precedent), together with texture budget rows.
- Combat behaviour, spawn tables and localisation keys go in as registry data (section 11, `tools/monster_registry.py add`). Portraits (Codex images) and models are connected with `art-ready` once they exist, and the Monster Codex follows the registry list (25 growing to 138).
- Public distribution approval for Hunyuan output is still open; every record stays `productionApproved: false`.

## 11. Monster registry and data-driven combat (implemented 2026-10-11)

The foundation for adding monsters and bosses as data, without code changes. When the daily routine moves 20 monsters into the game with `tools/monster_registry.py add`, they spawn in rifts the same day.

### 11.1 Registry

- Game data lives in `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Monsters/MonsterRegistry.json`; the runtime is `Runtime/Core/MonsterRegistry.cs`. The contract the Monster Codex reads: `MonsterRegistry.All` (codex order: field index, regular before boss, then number), `ById`, `ForKind`, `ForBoss`, `IdOf(EnemyState)` (bosses map to the B id of their pattern, everything else to the N id of its kind, elites to their base kind, the golden goblin to null).
- Entry fields: `id` (N01–N120, B01–B18), `boss`, `kind` (N number − 1, −1 for bosses), `pattern` (B number − 1, −1 for regular), `name`/`role`/`family` (Korean localisation keys, English in `en.txt`), `field` (GameCatalog field index; bosses have a home field: B01 graveyard, B02 fortress, B03 cavern, B04 desert, B05 highland), `slot` (pack role 0 melee, 1 charger, 2 ranged, 3 zone, 4 support, 5 exploder), `unlockTier`, `portrait` (`Art/TrainingGround/Portraits/<ID>`), `art` (HunyuanReady key), `artPending`, `skills` (name and description keys, at least one element tag physical/fire/cold/lightning/poison/shadow, the damage multiplier of one hit or 0, optional `icon`), `hp`/`attack`/`speed`, for bosses `keepDistance`/`approach`/`body`, `attacks`, `traits`, `legacy`.
- The existing 25 are `legacy: true`: the entry only describes their current kind, pattern, stats and skills; their combat stays the existing code. Existing boss skill icons are `Art/Boss/skill-<definition>`. From the 21st kind and the 6th boss on, names, stats (`CombatSimulation.EnemyStats`, `BossCombat.ProfileOf`) and combat come from the registry.
- A monster whose art is not ready ships with `artPending: true`: `portrait` and `art` are empty strings, the world shows the existing primitive figure and the training ground an empty portrait frame. Another monster's portrait is never used as a stand-in.
- The design source is `Docs/Design/MonsterRoster/roster.json`: all 138 in the registry schema plus Korean and English text (`nameEn`, `roleEn`, `familyEn`, skill `nameEn`/`descriptionEn`), `shipped`, `day` and `deferred` (mechanics not implemented yet).

### 11.2 Data-driven combat primitives

`Runtime/Core/MonsterBehavior.cs` owns the geometry; `CombatSimulation.Monsters.cs` and `CombatSimulation.MonsterTraits.cs` own the execution. The simulation, the warning gauges (`EnemyCombat.Threats`) and the damage forecast (`ForecastIncoming`) read the same shape function. The existing 25 never enter this path, so existing seeds keep their results.

| Attack `type` | Behaviour | Main fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strike` | Circle, ring, sector or line, telegraphed on the caster (`at: self`), the hero (`hero`), the predicted spot (`predicted`) or where the hero last started a skill (`lastSkill`), moved `offset` along the aim. `hits` 2+ adds strikes `hitDelay` apart; `pattern` `row` (along the aim), `around` (centre plus a ring), `cross` (`count` directions, 4 by default) or `lanes` (side by side) | `shape`, `radius`, `inner`, `angle`, `length`, `count`, `spacing`, `spread` |
| `volley` | A fan of projectiles; the hero is hit at most once per volley. `returning` adds a return pass (still one hit), `impactZone` leaves a zone where each shot stops | `count`, `spread`, `speed`, `projectile`, `impactRadius`, `impactPower` |
| `charge` | Line charge; the body hits once as it passes. `growth` widens the contact per metre, `trail` leaves a zone along the path, `wallStun` stuns the charger for 2 s against a wall | `travel`, `speed`, `trail`, `trailPower` |
| `leap` / `burrow` / `blink` | Leap to 1 m short of the hero, tunnel to the hero and erupt, or blink behind (`blinkTo: behind`) or beside (`side`) the hero and strike. `retreat` springs back that far after landing | `travel`, `speed` |
| `zone` | Ground zone: every `interval` for `duration`, after `zoneDelay`; `moveSpeed` drifts, `endRadius` shrinks, `endInner` moves a ring's inner edge (freeze spreading from the edge, a closing safe circle), `spin` sweeps a beam, `follow` rides on the caster, `pull` pulls while waiting, `refuges` adds safe spots (`refugeRadius`), `trap` springs once when the hero steps in | `duration`, `interval`, `spin`, `endInner`, `refuges` |
| `attach` | A melee latch: on a hit it rides on the hero and drains `trailPower` every `interval`; a movement skill, a stun or `duration` ends it | `duration`, `interval`, `trailPower`, `leech` |
| `heal` / `shield` | Heal allies in range / give another ally a ward (`ward`) or projectile reflection (`reflect` seconds) | `heal`, `ward`, `reflect` |
| `summon` / `raise` / `harvest` | Summon (alternating with `summonAlt`, which falls back to `summon` until it ships) / raise from a corpse / absorb its own minions, healing `heal` per minion | `summon`, `count`, `cap` |
| `object` | Breakable objects (`obj`): `layout` `ring` (around the hero), `line`, `wall` (across the aim) or `around` (around the caster). `blocks` stops the hero walking (movement skills pass; at most 2 s around the hero, 5 s as walls), auras (`auraRadius`: attack, speed, damage reduction, healing, hero slow), `ownerReduction` (the owner takes less while it stands), `ownerInvulnerable`, `stunOwner` (breaking all staggers or stuns the owner), `link` (a beam from the owner to the object), `mimic` (a darkened decoy that only telegraphs the owner's phase-1 attacks), `burstPower` (explodes when broken) | `obj.*` |

- On-hit effects: `slow` (seconds) with `slowStrength` (35% by default, at most 60%), `root`, `knockdown`, `push`, `pull`, `chill`/`chillLimit`, `seal` (skills cannot start; basic attacks can), `curse`/`curseTime` (more damage taken), `poison`/`poisonPower`/`poisonCap` (stacking poison every 0.5 s), `leech` (heals by a share of damage dealt), `blind` (vision capped at 7 m), `rearPower` (bonus when biting from behind the hero, decided at announce). Loss of control and seals last at most 1.5 s and are reduced by control resistance. Hero statuses show as global HUD status icons.
- Other attack fields: `consume` (self-destruct), `trigger: hits` (retaliation only), `invulnerable` (the boss is invulnerable and holds still that long), `frenzy` (hastes nearby allies), `blind` (applied on release).
- Traits: frontal guard (`frontReduction`, dropped while stunned or frozen, phase 1 only with `shieldPhase1`), `frontProjectiles` (frontal projectiles do nothing), `rearBonus`, `idleReduction` (less damage while not acting), `guardHits`, `enrageBelow`, ally auras and `auraHeroSlow`, `stationary`, `flying` (moves straight over walls, drawn in the air), `ambushRadius` (hidden under a visible mound, untouchable and unseen), `fleeSeconds`/`bonusGold` (treasure: gold and materials), `pack`, `retaliateHits`/`retaliateAttack` (counterattack every N hits taken), `allyDeathHaste`, `hitHaste`, `hasteCap`, `hasteTime` (faster cooldowns), `shareHeal`, `blinkOnHit`/`blinkCooldown`, `blinkStep`/`blinkTrail` (moves in blinks leaving embers), `petrifyBelow`/`petrifySeconds`, `reviveHealth`/`reviveDelay` (rises after falling unless hit in between), `nearKind`/`nearRadius`/`nearAttack`, `corpseHeal`, death effects (`deathDelay`, `deathRadius`, `deathPower`, `deathDuration`, `deathSlow`, `deathSlowStrength`, `deathRoot`, `deathShards`), splitting.
- Data bosses: the 6 `attacks` are the kit (0–2 phase 1, 3–5 phase 2). They use BossCombat's slot order, cooldowns, the roar at 50% HP, movement, the minion cap (8) and stagger unchanged; the basic attack is the existing `BOSS_BASIC`.
- Attack definition ids: a regular monster's first attack is `N21`, later ones `N21_2`; bosses `B06_1`–`B06_6`; death effects `N33_DEATH`. Objects have no registry id, so `IdOf` returns null for them (not in the codex).

### 11.3 Spawn tables and bosses

- A pack slot's candidates are the slot's original kind plus every shipped monster of the same field and `slot` whose `unlockTier` is at most the current tier (in kind order). The pick is a hash of the layout's `encounterSeed` and the spawn index (`RiftGenerator.SpawnPick`), never a run or encounter stream value. A slot with one candidate spawns exactly as before, and positions, roles, elites and rewards never change. Tiers 1–5 still use slot 0 only.
- New regular monsters unlock at tier 6 in the tier-1 fields (graveyard, cavern, grassland) and tier 11 in the tier-11 fields (fortress, desert, highland), so tier 1–5 natural progression and the recorded results (FieldTests goldens, tier-1 fights) stay unchanged.
- A swarm's placed spawn leads `pack` − 1 followers. Followers count as adds (no reward, kill-gauge meter or corpse), so rift rewards stay as they were.
- Bosses: follow the "actual selection rule" in section 9. The boss the stage rule picks (unlocks at tiers 1/11/21/31/41, unchanged) is pooled with the shipped data bosses whose home is that field and whose tier is reached, and the layout's hash (`RiftGenerator.FieldBoss`) picks one. Fields and tiers without a data boss keep their boss.
- The training ground picker and the skill preview scenario check accept every registered kind.

### 11.4 Tool

- `python3 tools/monster_registry.py next 20`: the next unshipped ids in day order (`tools/monster_pipeline/day_order.json` when present, otherwise the roster's `day`).
- `python3 tools/monster_registry.py add <ID...> [--art-pending] [--allow-deferred]`: copies roster entries into the registry, writes English lines for missing Korean keys into `en.txt`, marks them `shipped: true` and validates; nothing is written when validation fails. Entries with `deferred` mechanics are refused without `--allow-deferred`.
- `python3 tools/monster_registry.py refresh <ID...>`: re-copies a shipped entry after its roster entry changed (keeps the art-pending state).
- `python3 tools/monster_registry.py art-ready <ID...>`: once the portrait and model of an art-pending entry land, sets the roster's `portrait`/`art` and validates.
- `python3 tools/monster_registry.py validate`: schema, unique ids, kind/pattern agreement, text completeness (missing English, object names included), element tags, slow strength 60%, seals 1.5 s, curse/vision/poison caps, object layout and blocking time (2 s around the hero, 5 s as walls), retaliation setup, damage-per-second budget (melee slot within ±15% of N01, other slots at most N01 + 15%, boss hits at most 2.0×), telegraphs of 0.4 s or more, loss of control at most 1.5 s, slows at most 3 s, registered summon/split kinds, and portrait/model files for entries that are not art-pending.
- Regression checks: `python3 tools/test_monster_registry.py` and Edit Mode `MonsterRegistryTests`, `MonsterPrimitiveTests`, `MonsterMechanicTests`, `MonsterSpawnTableTests` (the same rules again in C#).

### 11.5 Shipped monsters (2026-10-11)

N21 Grave Maggot Swarm, N22 Skeleton Shieldbearer, N23 Skeleton Spearman, N33 Bone Bomber and B06 Bone Matron shipped art-pending. Every skill description matches what it does (B06's bone prison is a breakable 2 s ring of bone walls, grave legion summons 2 each of N22 and N23).

### 11.6 Deferred and limits

No roster entry has deferred mechanics; the daily routine ships without `--allow-deferred`. Known limits:

- Walls and cages only stop the hero walking. Enemies pass, and the hero's pathfinding does not know them, so it stops at a wall and attacks it or waits for it to expire.
- Vision loss shows as the 7 m perception cap and a HUD status; there is no screen fog.
- The Hunt Edict does not seek refuge spots (the flood tide's rocks), as with the existing Hymn of Silence refuges.
- Flying changes movement and drawing height only; the hero's ground effects still hit flyers.
- Decoys mimic only the owner's non-projectile phase-1 attacks.

Updated: 2026-10-11 · 한국어

This plan gives each of the six rift fields at least 20 regular monsters and at least 3 bosses: 120 regular monsters (20 existing + 100 new) and 18 bosses (5 existing + 13 new), 138 in total. Models are made with the Tencent HY 3D (Hunyuan) free allowance of 20 generations per day, 20 per day in the priority order below. Field rules follow Six Rift Fields; existing enemy and boss numbers follow the regular enemy and elite detail and the boss combat detail.

1. Design principles

  • Look and feel: as in Diablo IV, monsters are grouped into families, and one field shares materials and colours. Grim realistic gothic fantasy, weathered materials, bold silhouettes that read from the high top-down camera. The dark painterly portraits in Resources/Art/TrainingGround/Portraits are the reference. No gore such as wounds or exposed flesh.
  • One question per monster: every monster asks the player (that is, the Hunt Edict) one question: whom to hit first, where to step, when to cast, whether to keep a movement skill, area or single-target damage. The Edict test column names that question.
  • Always avoidable: all damage is shown first with the existing telegraph gauge (circle, ring, cone, line). No unavoidable damage, no loss of control longer than 1.5 s, no slow above 60%. As today, a projectile volley hits at most once per cast.
  • Roles inside a field: each field has 5–6 melee, 2–3 charge or leap, 3 ranged, 3 zone or control, 3 support or summoner, 2 death effects and 1–2 special (ambush, stationary structure, treasure) monsters. A field never repeats a mechanic.
  • Numbers: the stats and patterns of the existing 20 do not change. Numbers for new monsters are draft values; implementation fits them to the existing EnemyCombat shapes and the same damage-per-second budget (melee slot within ±15% of N01).
  • Current spawn table: the current table (fields other than the graveyard share N02–N05) stays; new monsters shipped in the registry join the same role slot of their own field from their unlock tier (section 11).

10.2 Generation procedure

  • Site: https://hy3d.tencent.ai/ AI Creation → Text-to-3D, 3DGeneration-V3.1, 50k faces, PBR. One request uses one of the daily generations and makes 4 candidates. At most 3 run at once (a 4th submission is refused with The current concurrency exceeds the limit and does not use the allowance).
  • The user signs in by hand in the in-app browser. Submissions carry a signature, so they go through the page's text box and Generate Now button; results are read with GET /api/3d/creations/detail?creationsId=….
  • Prompt form (500 characters at most): Full-body <appearance>. Neutral stance, limbs slightly apart from the body. Single isolated creature, no ground, base or background. Grim realistic dark gothic ARPG style, bold readable silhouette, weathered PBR materials, complete back. The appearance follows the portraits and the concepts here, with the field colour as accent (graveyard teal, cavern teal fungus, grassland rose and violet, fortress orange embers, desert amber, highland ice blue).
  • Of the 4 candidates, pick the one with the clearest silhouette, limbs apart from the body for rigging, and no ground or base.
  • Original GLBs, prompts, hashes and selection reasons live outside the repository in AssetDeliverables/Hunyuan/2026-10-11/ (and a folder per later day). Downloads happen after the user allows them.

11. Monster registry and data-driven combat (implemented 2026-10-11)

The foundation for adding monsters and bosses as data, without code changes. When the daily routine moves 20 monsters into the game with tools/monster_registry.py add, they spawn in rifts the same day.

11.1 Registry

  • Game data lives in Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Monsters/MonsterRegistry.json; the runtime is Runtime/Core/MonsterRegistry.cs. The contract the Monster Codex reads: MonsterRegistry.All (codex order: field index, regular before boss, then number), ById, ForKind, ForBoss, IdOf(EnemyState) (bosses map to the B id of their pattern, everything else to the N id of its kind, elites to their base kind, the golden goblin to null).
  • Entry fields: id (N01–N120, B01–B18), boss, kind (N number − 1, −1 for bosses), pattern (B number − 1, −1 for regular), name/role/family (Korean localisation keys, English in en.txt), field (GameCatalog field index; bosses have a home field: B01 graveyard, B02 fortress, B03 cavern, B04 desert, B05 highland), slot (pack role 0 melee, 1 charger, 2 ranged, 3 zone, 4 support, 5 exploder), unlockTier, portrait (Art/TrainingGround/Portraits/<ID>), art (HunyuanReady key), artPending, skills (name and description keys, at least one element tag physical/fire/cold/lightning/poison/shadow, the damage multiplier of one hit or 0, optional icon), hp/attack/speed, for bosses keepDistance/approach/body, attacks, traits, legacy.
  • The existing 25 are legacy: true: the entry only describes their current kind, pattern, stats and skills; their combat stays the existing code. Existing boss skill icons are Art/Boss/skill-<definition>. From the 21st kind and the 6th boss on, names, stats (CombatSimulation.EnemyStats, BossCombat.ProfileOf) and combat come from the registry.
  • A monster whose art is not ready ships with artPending: true: portrait and art are empty strings, the world shows the existing primitive figure and the training ground an empty portrait frame. Another monster's portrait is never used as a stand-in.
  • The design source is Docs/Design/MonsterRoster/roster.json: all 138 in the registry schema plus Korean and English text (nameEn, roleEn, familyEn, skill nameEn/descriptionEn), shipped, day and deferred (mechanics not implemented yet).

11.3 Spawn tables and bosses

  • A pack slot's candidates are the slot's original kind plus every shipped monster of the same field and slot whose unlockTier is at most the current tier (in kind order). The pick is a hash of the layout's encounterSeed and the spawn index (RiftGenerator.SpawnPick), never a run or encounter stream value. A slot with one candidate spawns exactly as before, and positions, roles, elites and rewards never change. Tiers 1–5 still use slot 0 only.
  • New regular monsters unlock at tier 6 in the tier-1 fields (graveyard, cavern, grassland) and tier 11 in the tier-11 fields (fortress, desert, highland), so tier 1–5 natural progression and the recorded results (FieldTests goldens, tier-1 fights) stay unchanged.
  • A swarm's placed spawn leads pack − 1 followers. Followers count as adds (no reward, kill-gauge meter or corpse), so rift rewards stay as they were.
  • Bosses: follow the "actual selection rule" in section 9. The boss the stage rule picks (unlocks at tiers 1/11/21/31/41, unchanged) is pooled with the shipped data bosses whose home is that field and whose tier is reached, and the layout's hash (RiftGenerator.FieldBoss) picks one. Fields and tiers without a data boss keep their boss.
  • The training ground picker and the skill preview scenario check accept every registered kind.

11.4 Tool

  • python3 tools/monster_registry.py next 20: the next unshipped ids in day order (tools/monster_pipeline/day_order.json when present, otherwise the roster's day).
  • python3 tools/monster_registry.py add <ID...> [--art-pending] [--allow-deferred]: copies roster entries into the registry, writes English lines for missing Korean keys into en.txt, marks them shipped: true and validates; nothing is written when validation fails. Entries with deferred mechanics are refused without --allow-deferred.
  • python3 tools/monster_registry.py refresh <ID...>: re-copies a shipped entry after its roster entry changed (keeps the art-pending state).
  • python3 tools/monster_registry.py art-ready <ID...>: once the portrait and model of an art-pending entry land, sets the roster's portrait/art and validates.
  • python3 tools/monster_registry.py validate: schema, unique ids, kind/pattern agreement, text completeness (missing English, object names included), element tags, slow strength 60%, seals 1.5 s, curse/vision/poison caps, object layout and blocking time (2 s around the hero, 5 s as walls), retaliation setup, damage-per-second budget (melee slot within ±15% of N01, other slots at most N01 + 15%, boss hits at most 2.0×), telegraphs of 0.4 s or more, loss of control at most 1.5 s, slows at most 3 s, registered summon/split kinds, and portrait/model files for entries that are not art-pending.
  • Regression checks: python3 tools/test_monster_registry.py and Edit Mode MonsterRegistryTests, MonsterPrimitiveTests, MonsterMechanicTests, MonsterSpawnTableTests (the same rules again in C#).

11.5 Shipped monsters (2026-10-11)

N21 Grave Maggot Swarm, N22 Skeleton Shieldbearer, N23 Skeleton Spearman, N33 Bone Bomber and B06 Bone Matron shipped art-pending. Every skill description matches what it does (B06's bone prison is a breakable 2 s ring of bone walls, grave legion summons 2 each of N22 and N23).

11.6 Deferred and limits

No roster entry has deferred mechanics; the daily routine ships without --allow-deferred. Known limits:

  • Walls and cages only stop the hero walking. Enemies pass, and the hero's pathfinding does not know them, so it stops at a wall and attacks it or waits for it to expire.
  • Vision loss shows as the 7 m perception cap and a HUD status; there is no screen fog.
  • The Hunt Edict does not seek refuge spots (the flood tide's rocks), as with the existing Hymn of Silence refuges.
  • Flying changes movement and drawing height only; the hero's ground effects still hit flyers.
  • Decoys mimic only the owner's non-projectile phase-1 attacks.

# Native puzzle waiting room implementation

> Updated: 2026-10-14 · the puzzle-level tutorial was retired; its code, tests and shipped assets were deleted. This page records that time. [Retirement record](Puzzle_Tutorial_Retirement_20261014.en.md)

2026-10-07. Stage 6 implementation. Native visual/input/performance acceptance remains scheduled for the final integrated player at stage 9.

`PuzzleHubWindow` uses the generated `ContentWindowView` entry point, shared host, safe area, theme, fonts and buttons. Its one-screen composition adapts the shared body to status, character art, a level board and fixed actions. Existing inventory, Hunt Edict, skill tree and settings remain their actual owners.

`GameController.Tutorials` prepares the current owned level and connects the hub to fresh attempts. Persisted `RecordPuzzleAttempt` results return to the hub. Prior levels use detached `CreateReplay` state. Town access remains locked until all 15 levels clear.

Menu transitions move the hub and existing destination window for 0.62 seconds. Portrait uses the X axis, landscape the Y axis; perpendicular swipes are ignored. The status stays fixed during transitions. Closing a destination or selecting Waiting room returns to the same hub.

The first status row contains actual HP/resource and the second full-width row XP. Selection reads saved progress, locks future levels, and switches the final cleared level action to Town. `StoreViewBinding` compares hero, progress, XP, skills and hint display dependencies and defers repaint during input, transitions and child windows. Language and safe-area changes invalidate layout.

The existing window host/camera lifecycle hides the world behind the opaque hub. Effects modify existing transforms, colors and fills without rebuilding UI each frame. Any performance result requires three matching launches of each real before/after player binary at final validation.

Import only necessary prototype HTML/tools/art/prompts; preserve unknown model provenance. Native textures receive a dedicated importer and ResourceTextureBudget entries. Historical screenshot batches are not imported.

Final acceptance: three classes, KO/EN, portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440, desktop 16:9/16:10/21:9; real arrow, replay, graduation, menu, axis swipe and save/reentry interactions; shared UI/refresh/binding checks. Full EditMode and native smoke run once on final integrated code. Physical mobile remains separately unverified.

Effect cost will compare two actual binaries of the same new hub, with effects disabled and enabled. The previous version has no hub and cannot represent the same screen. Capture three launches per binary with matching source, input, resolution, FPS and quality.

Integration: Unity drives overlay Canvas root geometry, so animate the existing window frame and fade its existing backdrop CanvasGroup. `ContentWindowView.FixedOverlay` owns the fixed status layer. Replay inventory/edict menus use real `GameStore.Sandbox` transactions, validation and commit notifications while changing only a detached copy without disk writes. Replay transactions and guide discoveries leave the original account unchanged.

Focused evidence: `stage6-hub-save-focused-repair.xml` initially passed 91 of 95 checks. The missing Play/Town translations and replay checkpoint rejection were repaired. `stage6-replay-checkpoint-repair.xml` passes the four failed checks plus 11 title-screen checks: 106 unique checks now pass, zero skipped. Real owned Hunt Edict commits, transaction rollback, original-account preservation, save bindings and swipe axes are covered. `tools/check_ui_contract.py`, `tools/test_ui_contract.py` (11) and `tools/check_ui_refresh.py` pass. The unchanged prepared HTML prototype report has 382 passing checks; it is separate from native-player acceptance.

2026-10-07 final acceptance: [stage 9 integration](Puzzle_Tutorial_Final_Acceptance.en.md) verifies 30 class/locale/layout combinations, 12 safe-area simulations and 12 full journeys. Its record identifies reused completed spans, failed-only retries and the source/save/input evidence.

2026-10-07 landscape layout correction (post-merge verification): in the merged build's landscape and wide screenshots (1280×720, 1600×900, 2100×900) the status bars stretched across the whole width and ran behind the level plate over the XP text, the level-name band covered the hero's face, and the light flow showed as a flat rectangle rather than a soft gradient. The geometry now lives in `PuzzleHubLayout` (a pure calculation) and follows the mockup's landscape rule: status cluster at the top left (260 wide), level plate at the top centre (200 wide), hero below it (62% of the height) and Play at the bottom right. On narrow landscape (16:9, 16:10) the plate steps aside to the right of the status area. Portrait is unchanged. The light flow uses one shared 32×1 soft-edged ramp sprite, created once. The English `Resource 100 / 100` that wrapped or ran over the frame in the narrower landscape bars is sized from its measured width so it stays on one line (Unity best-fit does not react to horizontal overflow, so it is not used). `PuzzleHubTests` checks status, plate, arrows, hero face and Play for overlap at six sizes, and the native smoke's `CheckHub` checks the same overlaps and that each status label fits its bar on the real screen. The earlier "controls are inside the safe area" check could not catch this.

2026-10-08 screen cleanup (user screenshots): (1) Windows opened from the hub (hunt edict, skills, inventory, settings) showed behind the fixed navigation buttons at the bottom in portrait and on the right in landscape. The band the navigation uses (118 units at the bottom, 98 on the right) is reserved with `UiSafeArea.Reserve`, so every window opened above it lays out in `UiSafeArea.Current`, the area that remains. The hub itself keeps the whole area through `ContentWindowView`'s `fullArea`. The reservation is taken when a menu opens and released when the hub returns home, closes or its owner is destroyed. (2) The level plate is smaller (240 units wide in portrait and 176 in landscape, was 350 and 200) and the level name sits under it on a soft pill shade. `PuzzleHubLayout` sizes the hero so the plate, name and progress dots never cover the top 22% of the picture where the head is (the hero is larger in portrait). (3) The two level arrows use the same picture, mirrored for the right one. Before, the shared button face covered the picture and only the right arrow carried a text glyph, so the pair looked different. An arrow that leads nowhere is only dimmed. For the same reason the original pictures of Play and the navigation buttons were hidden; they now use `UiButtonRole.Icon` (a press darkens the picture). The selected navigation button is shown by a soft golden light behind it and a bright label instead of a grey square. (4) The HP, resource and XP fills are pill shapes fitted to the transparent opening of the frame art (measured: rows 37-69 of 106 px, 75 px from each side), so they cannot poke out of the frame. The frame's end ornaments keep their proportions while only the middle stretches, and each value stays on one line that shrinks to the opening. Landscape stacks the bars in three rows. (5) The moving light block (`Light flow`) is gone from Play and from the bars. Under Play there is only a soft light that breathes in place (still under reduced motion, absent on the replay button). `PuzzleHubTests` checks the overlap of hero head, plate, arrows and dots and the plate size at nine sizes, whether the bar track lies inside the opening using the alpha of the real art, and that the reservation is released even when its owner is destroyed. The native smoke's `CheckHub` checks the arrow pair, the bar fills and the absence of a moving light, and `CheckHubChild` checks on the real screen, at every resolution and language, that an opened window never runs under a navigation button or label.

2026-10-08 follow-up: the level left/right buttons and keyboard arrows are gone (only the level to play shows). The status area slides with the page. Bottom menu number 3 changed from Skills to Blacksmith (it opens `BlacksmithWindow` as is) and skills are learned on the Hunt Edict's `Skills` tab. The art buttons' click sound is set with `UiButton.SoundCue`, and menu slides play `ui.open`/`ui.close`. Positions, names and the verification scope are in [Tutorial hub follow-up and per-hero tutorials](Tutorial_Hub_Followup_20261008.en.md).
