# Rift Gear Offer Cards Implementation Plan

Updated: 2026-10-13

[한국어](Rift_Gear_Offer_Cards_Plan_20261013.md)

For the Codex implementation task. The approved mockup is "Rift gear recommendation UI" (Claude artifact `https://claude.ai/artifact/1fVkuNDqhdWyHN7ZFmFMmp`, private). If it cannot be opened, the dimension and wording tables below are authoritative. The mockup is HTML: translate colours and gradients to `UiTheme`, `UiButton`, `StorageSurface` and `EquipmentGradePalette`; add no new colour literals (`tools/check_ui_contract.py` checks them).

## 0. Mockup contents

The artifact has 16 boards: four screens × (portrait 440×956 Korean / portrait English / landscape 956×440 Korean / landscape English).

| Screen | Boards |
| --- | --- |
| 1 Battle offer cards | `Main`, `MainEn`, `MainLand`, `MainLandEn` |
| 2 Details (nothing worn) | `Detail`, `DetailEn`, `DetailLand`, `DetailLandEn` |
| 3 Details (compare with worn) | `Compare`, `CompareEn`, `CompareLand`, `CompareLandEn` |
| 4 Recommended gear settings | `Settings`, `SettingsEn`, `SettingsLand`, `SettingsLandEn` |

English boards use the game's `en.txt` wording; for new strings the table in §4.4 is authoritative. Landscape boards were derived from the portrait ones, so if a layout looks off, fix the mockup first and then implement.

## 1. Current state and scope

Branch `claude/rift-gear-offer-actions` (commit `c48c24d5`, pushed, not merged) holds the pre-mockup implementation. Continue on that branch.

| Area | Already there (c48c24d5) | To do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Card | Name, icon, part, `score (+gain)`, Equip/Details buttons, gear, × (width 112) | **Remove Details, add a magnifier at the icon's top-right, centre a smaller Equip button, card width 92, apply mockup metrics and look** |
| Details | Card Details button → `RiftRecommendationWindow` (`compareFirst`) | The magnifier opens it; compare view when a worn item is replaced |
| Settings | `RiftGearSettingsWindow`, four sections, save | Match mockup wording, order and layout; add the items below |
| Rules | Settings gating, pickup-order queue, timer | Pin the lifecycle (town, end, re-entry) with tests |

## 2. Decisions (final)

1. Cards show **only on the battle screen**; leaving it hides them.
2. Re-entering the same run shows only items from that run that **match the conditions and are not yet equipped or closed**.
3. When the run ends (death, clear, give-up — anything that clears `suspendedRun`) all cards are gone.
4. **While in town via portal, no cards are shown.** They come back on return; the run has not ended, so nothing is deleted.
5. Eligibility is judged **once, at acquisition** (settings apply to gear acquired after saving). Cards already queued stay when settings change.
6. Rarities are Normal, Magic, Rare, Legendary, Set. **There is no Unique rarity in the game; do not add one.**
7. The queue is in **pickup order**, one card per slot; the next item of a slot appears after the previous is handled (equipped, closed, expired).
8. Time expiry is handled exactly like ×.

## 3. Open items (proceed with defaults, report them)

| Item | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Tapping the icon body | Opens details like the magnifier (larger touch target); the magnifier is the visible hint |
| Timer while a popup is open | Paused; restarts from zero on close (implemented) |
| Remaining-time indicator on cards | Not in the mockup; do not add |

## 4. Screen specification

### 4.1 Offer card (mockup board 1, reference width 440)

The strip sits at x=12, cards 4 apart, just above the bottom HUD (`BattleHudTopOnPage`), wrapping to more rows when needed. All values are px from the card's top-left.

| Element | Position (x, y) | Size | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Card | — | 92×150 (landscape: `slot+98` with a 54 icon) | 1px border, green family (`SuccessHex`) |
| Gear | (0, 0) | 24×24 | `StorageGlyph "gear"`, on every card, opens the same settings |
| × | top-right | 24×24 | Close as acknowledged |
| Item name | (3, 20) | 86×14, 10pt bold | Grade colour, one line, ellipsis |
| Icon | ((92−slot)/2, 36) | slot (52/54) | Existing `EquipmentSlotView` |
| Magnifier | inside the icon's top-right (x+33, y+1) | 18×18 | Named `rift-gear-inspect-{id}`, opens details |
| Part | (2, 91) | 88×13, 9pt | Gold |
| Score pill | (5, 105) | 82×17, 10pt bold, rounded | `500 (+400)`; gain only when something is replaced, negative in `DangerHex` |
| Equip | **centred** ((90−58)/2=16, 124) | **58×20**, 11pt | Primary gilt button; about 4 below, glow must not spill outside the card |

No Details button. Score format `0.#` (e.g. `149.6 (+28.6)`); it must not clip, also in English.

**On landscape screens (`root.width > root.height`: 956×440, 1600×900, …) the whole card is 75% of the portrait size.** Multiply every position, size and font size above by 0.75 (card about 69×112, icon slot also ×0.75). The strip's left start of 12 and the card gap stay, and the strip is aligned just above the HUD (about 8 above) for the reduced height. The mockup expresses it as `transform: scale(.75)`. Check that the shrunken text is readable at 956×440 in Korean and English; if not, do not change the ratio on your own — report it (consider 80–85%).

Rest of landscape: the bottom HUD is a single row (HP bar left, slots right) and the cards sit above it at the left.

### 4.2 Detail window (boards 2 and 3)

Keep `RiftRecommendationWindow` (shared `ItemDetailView` / `EquipmentComparisonView`). The magnifier opens with `compareFirst=true`: compare view when a worn item is replaced (worn left, candidate right, `score A → B` on the candidate, slot choice for rings and weapons), a single candidate otherwise. Footer `Equip` / `Close`; Close acknowledges (existing); a successful equip closes the window.

### 4.3 Recommended gear settings (board 4)

Inside the shared `ContentWindowView` (max 560×780), in this order. On landscape it is a centred 560×424 window whose body alone scrolls, with `Save`/`Close` (`Equip`/`Close` for the detail and compare windows) pinned at the bottom (the mockup shows it clipped); edit a draft, then `Save` (one transaction) or `Close`. Use localization keys with Korean and English filled.

1. **Rarities to recommend** — 3-column checkbox grid: Normal, Magic, Rare, Legendary, Set.
2. **Recommendation range** — Main hand, Off hand, Helmet, Chest armor, Gloves, Boots, Belt, Amulet, Ring; each row has an enable checkbox and `Details` (`Details enabled` when on).
   - Expanded panel: `Enable detailed filters` checkbox, a note (only gear meeting **every** selected option at or above its value is recommended; with none selected there is no condition), `Common options` rows (checkbox + name + number input + `or more`), enabled `Additional options`, `+ Add condition option` (the remaining options valid for that slot). One position expands at a time. Look and behaviour follow the bag auto-salvage detail settings (`EquipmentShopWindow.Settings`); data is separate.
   - Note under the list: non-matching or switched-off gear is not recommended; settings apply to gear acquired after saving.
3. **Recommendation rule** — radios: all equippable gear / gear with a higher score than what is worn (default).
4. **Popup duration** — radios: until I press cancel (default) / close after a set time. Only the latter enables the slider (1–60 s, default 10 s, value shown as `10s`) and the caption `1 s – 1 min (used only with a set time)`. An expiry/order note follows.

### 4.4 English wording (new items)

| Korean | English |
| --- | --- |
| 추천 장비 설정 | Recommended Gear Settings |
| 추천 표시 등급 / 추천 범위 / 추천 여부 / 팝업 시간 | Rarities to recommend / Recommendation range / Recommendation rule / Popup duration |
| 착용 가능한 모든 장비 | All equippable gear |
| 현재 착용중인 장비보다 점수가 높은 장비 | Gear with a higher score than what is worn |
| 취소 버튼을 누를 때까지 / 지정 시간 후 닫힘 | Until I press cancel / Close after a set time |
| ＋ 조건 옵션 추가 | + Add condition option |
| 1초 ~ 1분 (지정 시간 선택 시에만 사용) | 1 s – 1 min (used only with a set time) |
| 상의 | Chest armor |

For the three long notes, the wording already in `Resources/Localization/en.txt` is authoritative.

Check these differences between the mockup and the current build: slider caption, radio wording, five grades, panel spacing.

## 5. Rules and data

- Storage: `HeroSave.riftGearOffer` (`RiftGearOfferSettings`: `gradeMask` 31, `rangeMask` 511, `allWearable`, `timed`, `seconds` 1–60, per-position `RiftGearRange{id, details, thresholds}`). Per hero, account save; not device-local like language or orientation.
- Eligibility: `RiftGearRecommendations.CanOffer` → `RiftGearOfferSettings.Accepts` (rarity, range, required options), then the rule (`allWearable`: any valid equip plan; otherwise a higher post-swap score).
- Queue: `DropState.gearOrder` (`max+1` at acquisition), one card per slot. `gearHandled` is saved through the existing `DismissRiftGear`.
- Timer: `GameUI.GearRecommendations.ExpireGearRecommendation`, counted only for visible cards; expiry runs the same transaction as ×; a failed save retries after the next interval (avoid repeating toasts).
- Every new `HeroSave` field must be added to the per-hero copy list in `GameStore.Transact` (`target.riftGearOffer=source.riftGearOffer`); otherwise saved settings vanish from memory. Done; re-check for any similar field.

## 6. Steps

1. **Card layout** — `GameUI.GearRecommendations.cs`: width 92 and height (everything ×0.75 on landscape), remove Details, magnifier (`rift-gear-inspect-{id}`), centred 58×20 Equip, 24 px ×, 24 px gear, score pill; keep the constants in one place.
2. **Magnifier/icon behaviour** — both call `OpenGearRecommendation(id, compareFirst: true)`. Fix the smoke's assumption of toggling `rift-gear-compare` (it now opens in compare).
3. **Settings window** — diff `RiftGearSettingsWindow.cs` against 4.3 (wording, order, caption, spacing); English in `Resources/Localization/en.txt`.
4. **Lifecycle** — prove §2 items 1–4 with tests and smoke (below).
5. **Docs** — update the Rift recommendation section of `Docs/Implementation/Hunt_Edict_Control_Refinement.md` and both languages of this plan. If wiki sources change follow `AgentRules/Wiki_Publish.md`.

## 7. Verification

During work run only related checks; run the full Edit Mode suite and the macOS runtime smoke once after the final change and integration into `main` (global rule).

- Edit Mode (`Hellscript.Tests.RecommendedEquipmentTests` and related): rarity/range/required-option/rule gating, settings save and reload (**live hero included**), pickup-order queue, next card after expiry, `Visible` empty after the run ends, no card creation or display during the portal town visit (`run.portal`, `Page != "battle"`), re-entry restores only unhandled cards.
- Smoke: `-hellscriptEdictControlsSmoke -hellscriptEdictGearSmoke -hellscriptSavePath <empty dir> -hellscriptEvidence <empty dir>` (pass arguments as an array; isolated paths are required). Sizes 440×956, 956×440, 1600×900, 1600×1000, 2100×900 in Korean and English: cards above the HUD and inside the safe area (landscape at 0.75 with readable text); card controls (Equip, magnifier, gear, score) inside the card with no clipped text; magnifier → details (compare); Equip button; settings open, save and time expiry; hidden during the town visit and shown again after return.
- `python3 tools/check_ui_contract.py --verify`.
- Report what was checked and what was not (no physical device or touch; never report a macOS result as a device result).

## 8. Traps

- A resize rebuilds the battle page and closes popups without acknowledgement. A same-size language change can repaint and keep the detail window open. The smoke explicitly rebuilds the page before opening the next detail view. Settings drafts lost on page rebuild remain an accepted limitation.
- `JsonUtility` reads a missing list as `[]`: call `Normalize()` on read and never trust list lengths.
- The default smoke entry (`-hellscriptEdictControlsSmoke` alone) fails at the settings step regardless of this work; add `-hellscriptEdictGearSmoke` to run only the gear flow.
- Do not re-add the removed text-size adjustment or its 50–150% checks.
- Clean builds and temporary artifacts per `AgentRules/Artifact_Cleanup.md` and record the final state.

## 9. Implementation record · 2026-10-13

- Inspected all 16 board structures/strings and enlarged card/settings views in the verified in-app browser. Continued the existing `c48c24d5` implementation and plan on an isolated checkout containing latest `main` (`a5596519`); preserved both unrelated tutorial drafts in the original checkout.
- Translated the card metrics, 75% landscape scale, magnifier/icon hit area, centred Equip, score pill, ellipsis, settings sections/filters/wording and timer caption through shared owners. The magnifier opens comparison immediately. A content-specific `EquipmentComparisonView` choice keeps portrait offer cards side by side; other callers retain default portrait panes.
- Added acquisition-order and acquisition-once checks, portal/terminal boundaries and live-hero/reloaded-hero settings coverage. Normalize missing settings lists on load and suppress repeated identical expiry-save toasts.
- Defaults used: icon body opens details; popup duration pauses and restarts from zero on close; no remaining-time indicator.
- Final related checks and gear-only macOS acceptance results are consolidated here. Full Edit Mode, the full runtime batch and public wiki follow the once-at-main-merge validation/publishing rule.
- Artifact ownership/size/disposition is recorded in `Builds/RiftGearOfferCards20261013/artifact-lifecycle.json`. No new raster assets, dependencies or full project copies.

### Final verification

- [Validation record](RiftGearOfferCardsEvidence20261013/validation.json): 185 related Edit Mode tests passed, zero failed/skipped. Shared UI ownership, 15 validator regressions and UI refresh checks passed. Unchanged core/shared owners and their tests reused successful results.
- Native macOS checks covered five viewports in Korean and English: screen-pixel metrics, 75% scale, safe bounds, controls/labels and fixed actions. Cards reuse the HUD pixel canvas and sit above the floating Hunt Edict hit area. Visibility toggles only when its state changes.
- Verified magnifier/icon comparison, detail/quick equip/close, red negative gain, settings draft/additional conditions/save/cancel, live/reloaded hero equality, actual popup-time pause/restart/expiry, empty-slot details in ten combinations, inventory hiding, portal town/return, unhandled-only re-entry, run end and ended-run reload.
- After the initial gear flow, only failed/changed coverage was rechecked four times. Fixed the HUD input blocker, screen-pixel/glyph scaling, a test assumption about language-only detail repaint, modal timer resets and deferred inventory-page visibility. Unchanged settings/comparison results were reused.
- About 71 minutes elapsed after the artifact record; validation tools ran about 6 minutes, with zero approval/connection wait. One related Edit Mode run, one validator regression run, five native builds, one initial gear flow and four affected rechecks.
- Full Edit Mode/full runtime and wiki generation/public publishing await main merge. No WebGL or physical mobile/touch/notch checks. The 75% text was visually checked at 956×440 on macOS; the scale was not increased unilaterally.

![Native portrait cards and HUD crop](RiftGearOfferCardsEvidence20261013/cards-portrait-ko-crop.png)

![Landscape cards in English](RiftGearOfferCardsEvidence20261013/cards-landscape-en.png)

![Shared side-by-side comparison](RiftGearOfferCardsEvidence20261013/comparison-portrait-ko.png)

![Detailed filters in English](RiftGearOfferCardsEvidence20261013/settings-filters-portrait-en.png)

Fixed the HUD input blocker, screen-pixel/glyph scaling, a test assumption about language-only detail repaint, modal timer resets and deferred inventory-page visibility. Unchanged settings/comparison results were reused.

pages.body:
# Rift Stage Rarity: Implementation and Validation Record

Work date: 2026-09-12. [한국어](Rift_Rarity_Expansion.md). See the [detailed design](../Design/HELLSCRIPT_Rift_Rarity_Detail.en.md) for the formula and complete representative probability table.

## 1. Baseline and actual changes

The user designated their separately maintained `Downloads/HELLSCRIPT_GDD_v0.1.md` and `Downloads/HELLSCRIPT_Content_v0.1.xlsx` as the design baselines for this task. Both originals include the fixed reroll-cost update dated 2026-09-12. They are saved at the following project paths, where the stage-dependent probability changes are applied.

| Type | Project path and change location |
|---|---|
| GDD | `Docs/Design/HELLSCRIPT_GDD_v0.1.md`: rift rarity reward rules and economy table |
| Excel | `Docs/Data/HELLSCRIPT_Content_v0.1.xlsx`: economy/reward rows and stage probability verification table |
| Existing project specifications | `Docs/Design/HELLSCRIPT_Unity_Implementation_Plan.md` section 9.1 and reroll costs; `HELLSCRIPT_Itemization_Detail.md` sections 8.1 and 8.3; `HELLSCRIPT_Item_Quality_Detail.md` chapter 9 expected values |
| Shared formula | `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Core/RiftRarity.cs`: probability calculation and selection using source and current stage |
| Parameters | `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Core/RiftRarityBalance.cs`: baseline probabilities, legendary caps, shared growth rate, and data validation |
| Actual combat | `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Core/CombatSimulation.cs`: normal/elite kill rewards and `BossClear` |
| Sweeps and costs | `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Core/Economy.cs`: `Sweep`, `RerollGold` |
| Interface | `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Presentation/GameUI.RiftRewards.cs`, `GameUI.RiftKeeper.cs`, `GameUI.cs`, `Resources/Localization/en.txt` |
| Checks | `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Tests/Editor/RiftRarityTests.cs`, `ItemizationTests.cs`, `Runtime/Presentation/RuntimeRaritySmoke.cs` |

Other existing working-directory changes were preserved. Reward functions were connected to the existing processing flow; this feature did not change scenes, prefabs, packages, or game settings. The interface uses the existing Korean source-text keys and English translation table.

## 2. Calculation and preserved behavior

Define `t=max(0,R−1)`, `g=t/(t+49)`, and `legendary=p0+(cap−p0)×g`. Legendary baselines/caps are 1%/10% for normal enemies, 5%/25% for elites, and 15%/45% for bosses. Non-legendary grades are reduced proportionally using `baseline probability×(1−legendary)/(1−p0)`. All values are draft balance values for HELLSCRIPT.

Combat uses `State.stage`; sweeps use the relevant hero's `highestClear`. The 2% normal-enemy equipment-drop chance, one elite draw, three boss/sweep draws, item-level range, existing enhancement/dismantling/shop/crafting costs, gold and material amounts, individual legendary weights, and inclusion of sets are preserved. The new formula is not connected to shop, crafting, chest, or offline reward paths. Stored `Item` objects, `bossRewarded`, sweep receipts, and transaction structures remain intact, so finalized items are not rerolled during collection or reconnection.

## 3. Handling differences between code and documents

- Existing normal, elite, and boss probabilities and draw counts matched between the supplied files and code. They were retained as the stage 1 baselines.
- The code and existing project specifications still contained cost increases based on reroll count. The latest rule in the supplied files takes precedence, so the cost was corrected to `500×L+50×L×(L−1)`, where `L=max(1,item level)`. Cost is independent of reroll count; at L=30, every reroll costs 58,500 gold. The coefficients remain a test draft.
- The item-level cap of 60 specified in the project's earlier detailed item design is absent from the actual generation code. As requested, this task preserves the existing code's level calculation and documents the difference.
- The legendary generator applies class, slot, and individual member weights. `requiredSkill` is not currently an unlock filter for the generation pool. This feature changes neither the unlock policy nor the legendary/set lists added by later content expansions.
- The supplied GDD and workbook assign weight 1 to LW04, LA04 and LM04; the later project code and itemization design already use 10. The request explicitly preserves individual legendary weights, so the existing runtime value 10 remains, and unrelated baseline content rows were not overwritten. Stage rarity adjustment happens before this separate member selection.
- The supplied GDD proposes holding finalized sweep bundles when the bag is full; existing code instead rejects a sweep before drawing when fewer than three slots are free. The request preserves existing storage and duplicate-prevention behavior, so this change does not add pending sweep storage. Already-generated, unclaimed combat items were verified to survive saving and reconnecting unchanged.

## 4. Executed validation

Another Unity check was running in the shared working directory, so source, packages, and settings were copied to `/tmp/hellscript-rarity-work/unity` for validation. SHA256 hashes of the four reward Core files and two test files under validation match their originals. The Unity version is 6000.6.0f1, and the project's Test Framework version is 1.8.0.

### Unity Edit Mode

Across `RiftRarityTests`, `ItemizationTests`, `CoreTests`, `LocalizationTests`, and `OutcomeTests`, **115 tests passed with zero failures**. Of these, 28 are new rarity checks. Evidence is retained in `Artifacts/Validation/RiftRarity/focused.xml` and `focused.log`.

- Checked stage 1 baselines; treating negative and zero inputs as stage 1; monotonicity across stages 1–10,000; and probability ranges and totals at representative boundaries, stage one million, and `int.MaxValue`.
- Checked legendary, rare-or-better, and magic-or-better cumulative probabilities; ordering between sources; forbidden grades; adjustable parameters; and rejection of invalid data.
- Generated normal, elite, and boss kill rewards through the actual combat simulation's public `Tick`. Compared results that distinguish current stage 10 from highest-clear stage 50, along with random-state consumption.
- Tested sweeps while distinguishing the selected hero's highest-clear stage 50, another hero's stage 300, and a remaining stage 10 rift. Verified three draws, reward amounts, no first-clear or record updates, and rejection of duplicate requests.
- Saved and loaded unclaimed boss equipment on the ground, then checked that results and reward random state stayed unchanged after changing the highest-clear record and the stage requested for a new simulation. Repeated collection and reconnection did not duplicate rewards.
- Checked that offline settlement grants no equipment, reroll costs do not depend on reroll count, and insufficient funds leave existing state intact.

### Experiments using fixed random seeds

The tolerance for each sample was specified in advance as `max(0.001, 6×sqrt(p×(1−p)/N))`, measured in probability units. Grades with 0% probability must have exactly zero occurrences.

| Experiment | Samples and random seed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rarity by source | 3 sources × stages 1, 10, 50, and 1000 × 100,000 draws each; seed=20260912 | All tested distributions across 1,200,000 draws were within tolerance. Maximum absolute deviation was approximately 0.267464 percentage points. |
| Normal-enemy equipment drops | 50,000 kills each at stages 1 and 1000; seed=918273 | 1,075 drops (2.15%) and 1,080 drops (2.16%), both within tolerance of the 2% baseline. |
| Legendary member LW04 | 20,000 warrior necklaces already selected as legendary; seed=112681 | 1,846 occurrences (9.23%), within tolerance of the existing weight ratio 10/110=9.0909%. |

These results validate mathematical probabilities and automated selection. They do not measure actual players' farming distributions over extended play.

### macOS execution and Excel

The macOS development build **succeeded with zero errors**. An isolated test account in the native player verified the keeper button, Korean and English, 720×1280 and 1280×720 windows, no clipped labels or missing translations, and no account mutation from viewing chances. An active stage 10 remained the displayed stage despite a best record of 50 and selected stage 1. Automated UI checks and five saved screenshots were reviewed. Evidence includes `evidence/runtime-rarity-smoke.txt`, `evidence/player.log`, PNG files and `build.log`. This is a UI/flow fixture, not an extended manual combat playtest.

The workbook preserves the original 24 sheets and 23 tables and adds `24_균열등급확률`, bringing the total to 25 sheets. Only 12 existing explanatory cells were changed; the C27/EC13 fixed reroll rules remain identical to the source. Checks covered all 24 source/stage combinations and totals; linked results after changing growth span 49→98, normal legendary cap 10→12%, and baseline legendary 1→2%; and negative, zero, 1, 2, 49, 50, 51, one million and maximum Int32 stages. Defaults were restored before final recalculation and saving. Formula errors: zero. Rendered sheets were checked for layout. Recalculation was tested in the Artifact engine, not the native Microsoft Excel application.

## 5. Remaining limitations

Android/iOS device runs, extended economy balancing, and manual playtesting by the user have not been performed. The probability function was checked at very high stages, but this does not constitute unlimited-range validation of the complete monster-stat, currency, or item-stat systems at those stages. Changing parameters in Excel updates its verification table; runtime code data must still be updated separately. Existing local-save authority and duplicate-reward prevention were preserved; no new server-authority system was added.

## 6. Existing design updates and verification of the selected commit

Following the commit request on 2026-09-12, existing documents were checked again. The implementation plan and content catalog now link the supplied reference files at their project locations and describe the current reward policy. The rift exploration detail now covers stage-dependent normal, elite and boss rarity, the exclusion of chests, and sweeps using the selected hero's highest stage cleared in combat. Wiki status and related document histories were also updated.

The acquisition estimates in [itemization open items](../Design/HELLSCRIPT_Itemization_Open_Items.md) based on a fixed 15% legendary chance are labeled historical and recalculated using the current stage 30 formula. The legendary chance per boss equipment draw is approximately 26.153846%. With a necklace slot probability of 1/8 and the existing target member weight of 10/110, the chance of at least one target item per boss clear is approximately 0.888961%. This implies an average of 112.49 clears, or approximately 7.50 hours assuming four minutes per clear. These are theoretical boss-only values. The old combined field, elite and chest estimate is marked as requiring recalculation from current route counts. Individual legendary weights were not changed.

Because unrelated uncommitted features share the working directory, only the selected changes for this feature were exported into a separate Unity project and verified again. For the shared `CombatSimulation.cs`, `GameUI.cs` and English translation table, only this feature's changes are included. SHA256 hashes for all 16 selected code, test, localization and metadata files match the source under validation.

- All 115 relevant Unity Edit Mode tests passed again, with zero failures or skipped tests.
- The macOS development build from that source succeeded with zero errors.
- The new native player passed Korean/English, portrait/landscape, active stage 10 versus highest-clear stage 50, and account-immutability checks. All five saved screenshots were reviewed.
- Evidence is retained under `Artifacts/Validation/RiftRarity/publish/`: `publish-focused.xml`, `publish-focused.log`, `publish-build.log`, `publish-source-hashes.json` and `evidence/`. This path remains excluded from Git under existing project rules.

pages.body:
# Rift activity time graphs

2026-10-14 update: casual base HUD layout, independent graphs and top-right edict follow the [new source handoff](Casual_Battle_HUD_20261014.en.md). Historical runtime evidence below does not validate the new skin.

Updated: 2026-10-03 · [한국어](Rift_Activity_Time.md)

Rift battles show **Movement, Attack, Evasion and Farming** in real time. An independent HUD places one stacked 100% bar above four cumulative time/share labels and cumulative graphs. The horizontal axis is elapsed Rift time; the vertical axis is total seconds spent on that activity by that moment. Farming for 0.4 seconds, doing something else, then farming for another 0.4 seconds produces a flat stretch at 0.4 seconds followed by a rise to 0.8 seconds. The graph spans this play session's observation start through the current moment, rather than only the last 30 seconds. The hint above the graphs states the displayed start/end times.

| Activity | Recorded purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Movement | Actual travel toward unexplored areas, the boss room or other destinations |
| Attack | Basic/skill preparation, channeling and recovery; enemy pursuit, gathering and combat positioning |
| Evasion | Executed survival skills and retreat walking; a movement skill used for survival belongs here |
| Farming | Approaching loot or approaching/opening a chest |

Each simulation interval belongs to at most one activity. Within an interval, transitions use Evasion → Attack → Farming → Movement priority. Incidental pickups during attacks, projectiles and ongoing damage do not create additional activity time. Idle time and other stationary interactions are excluded from the four-activity denominator. Pause, town, portal maintenance and instantaneous post-battle collection add no time. Once activity exists, largest-remainder rounding makes the four displayed integer shares total exactly 100%. Before that, the bar is empty and shows a waiting hint.

Drag the heading to move the panel and press its left arrow to fold/unfold. **Position and folding are independent of DPS**. HUD rebuilds, orientation and language changes retain both. Position is device-only in `hellscript-activity-position-v1.json`; a new launch restores the position and starts expanded. Safe-area bounds and the lower log/controls constrain placement. Graphs and the share bar do not intercept gameplay input.

The existing `CombatFeedback` owns actual-purpose timing. Cumulative totals persist in `RunState.statistics.feedback` and completed records; live graph samples stay in memory. At completion, `CombatHistory.Capture` copies the actual timestamps and cumulative samples, including the final tick, into `CombatReview.activityHistory`. Checkpoint sampling rules remain the same; completed curves survive a file reload. Activity transitions and second boundaries are sampled. Long sessions coarsen intermediate samples to stay within 257 points while retaining the observation start, current endpoint and exact totals. The chart respects actual time spacing. Resuming starts the graph at the saved cumulative totals and does not infer the earlier detailed curve. Older timing lacks purpose evidence, so migration preserves skill evidence and starts a new timing observation at resumption.

The result's **View Graph** shows the four activities' final seconds, integer shares and curves below the existing DPS and cast inspection. It also reports active total and excluded idle time. Opening copies the completed evidence, so reflow and language changes never mutate owned records. Older records without curves show final totals with an explicit notice; missing or older-version activity aggregates show an unavailable-record message. Pre-resume curves are never inferred.

`RiftActivityPanel` is the shared activity presentation for the live HUD and result graph. `GameUI.RiftActivity` is a read-only adapter on the existing battle canvas. It reuses `TrainingDpsChart`, `DpsHudDrag`, `DpsHudPosition`, `UiTheme`, `UiFonts` and `Loc`, retaining the original DPS position file. No new content window, canvas or chart engine is introduced. Display interactions do not mutate account or combat evidence.

Sources: [Shared activity panel](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Presentation/RiftActivityPanel.cs), [Result graph](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Presentation/RiftCombatGraphWindow.cs), [Completed record](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Core/CombatHistory.cs), [Timing](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Core/CombatFeedback.cs), [HUD](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Presentation/GameUI.RiftActivity.cs), [Focused checks](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Tests/Editor/CombatActivityTests.cs), [macOS interaction checks](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Presentation/RuntimeTrainingGroundSmoke.Activity.cs).

## 2026-10-03: Final activity records and repeat settings shortcut validation

Completed reviews persist actual movement, attack, evasion and farming curves through the final tick. **View Graph** shows these beside the existing DPS and cast inspection. Result stages 1–14 always show a dimmed button and a two-second locked message. From stage 15, the compact **Go to settings** action opens the existing Hunt Edict repeat tab; closing it restores the same result.

Updated: 2026-10-03 · 한국어

Rift battles show Movement, Attack, Evasion and Farming in real time. An independent HUD places one stacked 100% bar above four cumulative time/share labels and cumulative graphs. The horizontal axis is elapsed Rift time; the vertical axis is total seconds spent on that activity by that moment. Farming for 0.4 seconds, doing something else, then farming for another 0.4 seconds produces a flat stretch at 0.4 seconds followed by a rise to 0.8 seconds. The graph spans this play session's observation start through the current moment, rather than only the last 30 seconds. The hint above the graphs states the displayed start/end times.

ActivityRecorded purpose
MovementActual travel toward unexplored areas, the boss room or other destinations
AttackBasic/skill preparation, channeling and recovery; enemy pursuit, gathering and combat positioning
EvasionExecuted survival skills and retreat walking; a movement skill used for survival belongs here
FarmingApproaching loot or approaching/opening a chest

Each simulation interval belongs to at most one activity. Within an interval, transitions use Evasion → Attack → Farming → Movement priority. Incidental pickups during attacks, projectiles and ongoing damage do not create additional activity time. Idle time and other stationary interactions are excluded from the four-activity denominator. Pause, town, portal maintenance and instantaneous post-battle collection add no time. Once activity exists, largest-remainder rounding makes the four displayed integer shares total exactly 100%. Before that, the bar is empty and shows a waiting hint.

Drag the heading to move the panel and press its left arrow to fold/unfold. Position and folding are independent of DPS. HUD rebuilds, orientation and language changes retain both. Position is device-only in hellscript-activity-position-v1.json; a new launch restores the position and starts expanded. Safe-area bounds and the lower log/controls constrain placement. Graphs and the share bar do not intercept gameplay input.

The existing CombatFeedback owns actual-purpose timing. Cumulative totals persist in RunState.statistics.feedback and completed records; live graph samples stay in memory. At completion, CombatHistory.Capture copies the actual timestamps and cumulative samples, including the final tick, into CombatReview.activityHistory. Checkpoint sampling rules remain the same; completed curves survive a file reload. Activity transitions and second boundaries are sampled. Long sessions coarsen intermediate samples to stay within 257 points while retaining the observation start, current endpoint and exact totals. The chart respects actual time spacing. Older timing lacks purpose evidence, so migration preserves skill evidence and starts a new timing observation at resumption.

pages.body:
# Rift combat journal and server analytics

Updated: 2026-10-02

Korean: [균열 전투 기록과 서버 분석 수집](Combat_Journal_Server.md) · [Live operations and configuration releases](Live_Operations.en.md)

The current [single Sites backend](Sites_Player_Logs.en.md) owns sign-in, operations and migrated records. Python/SQLite below is a local protocol reference and legacy data format; production deploys only `server/sites`.

## Player experience

The rift entry screen exposes **Battle records**, a newest-first account-wide list of the last 100 runs with an **All / Victories only / Defeats only** dropdown. Rows show device-local completion time and UTC offset, class, stage, combat duration and termination reason. Legacy timestamps and outcomes remain unknown when absent; localized result strings are never used to invent an outcome.

Defeats include death, timeout and returning before defeating the boss, distinguished by their termination reasons. Leaving loot after defeating the boss remains a victory. Training creates neither owned rift history nor analytics deliveries.

During battle a live text panel sits above the persistent bottom HUD. Narrow screens retain as many complete recent messages as fit and abbreviate the preview when necessary. Selecting a completed record opens the **shared combat text log directly**, chronological and paged in blocks of 100 entries. Rows use measured text height plus 12 units of vertical padding and 4-unit gaps. Closing restores the original list/filter/scroll, then the selected Rift entry stage. The obsolete full-screen record summary and its dedicated routes were removed. Stored summaries, final-five-second analysis, historical equipment/configuration and the separate death-analysis feature remain intact. See [screen verification](Rift_Entry.en.md).

The compact panel fills the rows above the current action with recent events. The expanded panel derives its row count from the actual font and available height, replacing the fixed three-event limit. Entries run chronologically from top to bottom; long messages are abbreviated only in their single-line previews. Panel dimensions, the expand/collapse control and stored events are preserved.

The journal joins observed movement/stop reasons, targets/destinations, rules, selected actions, cast phases, automatic/player triggers, cooldown/resource/range/position waits, hits, shield absorption, deaths, bosses, chests, potions, rewards and configuration changes. Enemy attack/hazard telegraphs retain preparation time and aim, with interruption and enrage events. Damage records retain source/target/root-cast IDs and actual HP loss separately from overkill. Death summaries use the observed final window's HP loss, largest damage source and blocked-skill reasons. Missing evidence is never reconstructed as fact.

## Ownership and persistence

`CombatSimulation` records through `CombatJournal` at existing decision, movement, damage and reward owners. UI only observes. Completed `CombatHistory` snapshots own their data. Journals were introduced in save schema 15; the current account schema is **16**, including live configuration and first-clear reward preservation. Legacy records remain readable.

`GameStore` commits the account first. `CombatJournalArchive` then creates derived files; failed account saves create no delivery. Export failures retain full records in the account for retry. Successful exports remove detailed events from the account's record, loading them from the per-run file when requested. A crash after an ACK and before the next account save retries the canonical file's exact bytes.

| Location | Purpose and retention |
| --- | --- |
| `<save directory>/combat-records/<runId>.json` | One JSON file per completed battle, containing readable messages and structured evidence. Only the latest 100 account records are retained. |
| Account `records` | Last 100 summaries, reviews and configuration snapshots; unexported records also retain their events. |
| `<save directory>/combat-outbox/<runId>.json` | Independent delivery queue; removal requires a matching server acknowledgment. Local 100-run pruning does not delete queued uploads. |
| `*.json.rejected` | Preserved server-rejected bodies, allowing later runs to proceed. |

Detailed events are capped at 20,000 per run. The start and newest window survive; omitted counts and sequence gaps are explicit, while full aggregates remain exact. Movement records use the actual movement override and distinguish survival responses from skill positioning; stale decisions are not reused as current triggers. Movement is sampled on state changes and every two seconds, repeated identical decisions every four seconds. This is not a frame-by-frame position replay. Event `damageEvents`, `rules`, `builds` and `edicts` are zero-or-one arrays so Unity does not materialize absent inline snapshots on reload. Files use compact JSON.

The outbox, including rejected evidence, is limited to 1,000 files or 256 MiB. Player files are still created when delivery capacity is exhausted, and unexported source data remains retryable within the latest 100 runs. If such a record ages out before export, `combatTelemetryLossCount` and subsequent `LOCAL_EXPORT_LOSS` explicitly report the gap. Collection must not be described as complete in that case.

## Analytics and trust

| Category | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Server-authenticated account ID, separate local account identifier, hero ID/class/start and end level, local attempt ordinal. No real name or advertising identifier is collected. |
| Environment/content | App version, build GUID, platform, save/item/map versions, stage, map fingerprint and seed. Configuration source, release version, hash and the admitted settings are retained. |
| Timing/progression | Client UTC start/end, simulation duration, existing attendance/fatigue duration, resume count, observed start; server receipt time is generated independently. |
| Loadout | Initial build/skills/ranks/options, Hunt Edict, equipped item instances, slot levels, rune configuration, potion state and final configuration; configuration-change events also capture the build. |
| Outcomes/rewards | Outcome/reason, kills/boss completion, awarded gold, equipment/rune counts, claimed/ignored drop states and exact item snapshots. Gold uses `RiftEarnings`, not wallet deltas. |
| Combat/integrity | Event sequence, cast/target/rule IDs, position, HP/resource, damage calculation inputs/results, final-window analysis and truncation/resume/export/clock trust markers. |

Client payloads are `client_observed`. SHA-256 provides retry byte identity, not anti-cheat authenticity. The receiver binds ownership to authentication, deduplicates account/run IDs and audits conflicting bodies. Suspicious speed, outcome or reward reports are investigation signals, never automatic sanctions.

The existing `AuthoritativeRiftVerifier` replays from a server-owned admission snapshot, clock and seed. Its completed `server_replay` copy is included in `HuntAuthorityCheckpoint.combatTelemetry` and committed by the same CAS as account/replay cursors. Client HTTP ingestion rejects this provenance. An internal host adapter must pass only committed checkpoints into `Repository.attach_authority`.

## Server integration

All current game authentication, operations and ingestion URLs use https://hellscript-player-logs.hoosung.chatgpt.site. `Resources/Data/ServerConnection.json` contains public origins only. An isolated QA file passed with `-hellscriptQaSessionFile` must match the Site and upload purpose. Ordinary Google players use in-memory sessions. Follow [Sites backend](Sites_Player_Logs.en.md) for persistence, authentication, migration and publishing.

`CombatTelemetryUploader` removes an outbox file only when `accepted`, `runId` and the exact-byte `payloadHash` match. Timeouts, authentication and transient failures retry with exponential backoff capped at 300 seconds; redirects are disabled. The Sites receiver acknowledges only after original R2 storage and the D1 summary succeed.

## Legacy receiver reference

Python and its tests remain local references for the earlier data and permission contracts. Do not deploy them as another production service. Container deployment files are removed. CI checks Python contracts, the existing operations web model, and the Sites build/Node suite. Historical platform deployment/volume/backup evidence remains in the [2026-09-25 operations record](Live_Operations.en.md#verification-record). Current storage and management belong to one Site.

### Results from the original journal implementation

The following evidence was collected when combat journals were introduced. Later configuration and QA-connection integration is recorded separately in [Live operations verification](Live_Operations.en.md#verification-record).

- Unity Edit Mode passed the 488/488 expanded regression run, 155/155 journal/enemy/boss/localization follow-up and 137/137 final natural-death/localization/movement-response run. These overlap and must not be summed into a whole-project count. See [validation](CombatJournalEvidence/validation.json) and [final death tests](CombatJournalEvidence/editmode-defeat.xml).
- The macOS development build succeeded with zero build errors. Normal Update first advanced the live journal, followed by direct fixed-step simulation. An unforced stage-one victory reported approximately 102.8 simulation seconds, 43 kills, 2,276 gold and five collected items. Attendance and simulation duration are separately recorded; this is not a claim of 102.8 seconds of real-time play.
- Portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440 and PC 1600×900, 1600×1000 and 2100×900 were checked in Korean/English at 100%/140% text size: 20 live-HUD and 20 history cases with rendered-text and HUD-overlap assertions.
- One actual run and 99 labeled list fixtures exercised 100 rows. EventSystem raycasts and pointer down/up/click opened the rift records entry, all three result filters and chronological details. Synthetic list fixtures were removed before the final save.
- A separate application process restored the full journal. Edit Mode covered 101st-record pruning without deleting delivery evidence, failed saves, full queues, ACK/crash recovery and rejected-body/crash recovery.
- Unity client → localhost HTTP receiver → SQLite commit → matching ID/SHA-256 ACK → outbox removal passed. Server tests passed 9/9 and all five analytics queries executed against the received run. [Runtime evidence](CombatJournalEvidence/runtime.json) records file size and hash.
- Shared-UI contract checks and 9/9 regression tests, wiki build/check, 10/10 Python wiki tests and JavaScript wiki checks passed. Physical mobile and production service integration are outside the verified scope.

![Large Korean live journal](CombatJournalEvidence/live-portrait-ko-large.png)

![Large English battle records](CombatJournalEvidence/records-landscape-en-large.png)

[Chronological text](CombatJournalEvidence/chronological-log.png) · [Defeat filter fixtures](CombatJournalEvidence/defeat-filter-fixtures.png) · [Separate-process restore](CombatJournalEvidence/restart-records.png)

Implementation sources: [CombatJournal.cs](../../Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Core/CombatJournal.cs) · [combat_telemetry.py](../../server/combat_telemetry.py) · [combat_analytics.sql](../../server/combat_analytics.sql) · [SHA-256](CombatJournalEvidence/source-digests.json)

Death summaries use the observed final window's HP loss, largest damage source and blocked-skill reasons. Missing evidence is never reconstructed as fact.

Ownership and persistence

CombatSimulation records through CombatJournal at existing decision, movement, damage and reward owners. UI only observes. Completed CombatHistory snapshots own their data. Journals were introduced in save schema 15; the current account schema is 16, including live configuration and first-clear reward preservation. Legacy records remain readable.

GameStore commits the account first. CombatJournalArchive then creates derived files; failed account saves create no delivery. Export failures retain full records in the account for retry. Successful exports remove detailed events from the account's record, loading them from the per-run file when requested. A crash after an ACK and before the next account save retries the canonical file's exact bytes.

LocationPurpose and retention
<save directory>/combat-records/<runId>.jsonOne JSON file per completed battle, containing readable messages and structured evidence. Only the latest 100 account records are retained.
Account recordsLast 100 summaries, reviews and configuration snapshots; unexported records also retain their events.
<save directory>/combat-outbox/<runId>.jsonIndependent delivery queue; removal requires a matching server acknowledgment. Local 100-run pruning does not delete queued uploads.
*.json.rejectedPreserved server-rejected bodies, allowing later runs to proceed.

Detailed events are capped at 20,000 per run. The start and newest window survive; omitted counts and sequence gaps are explicit, while full aggregates remain exact. Movement records use the actual movement override and distinguish survival responses from skill positioning; stale decisions are not reused as current triggers. Movement is sampled on state changes and every two seconds, repeated identical decisions every four seconds. This is not a frame-by-frame position replay. Event damageEvents, rules, builds and edicts are zero-or-one arrays so Unity does not materialize absent inline snapshots on reload. Files use compact JSON.

The outbox, including rejected evidence, is limited to 1,000 files or 256 MiB. Player files are still created when delivery capacity is exhausted, and unexported source data remains retryable within the latest 100 runs. If such a record ages out before export, combatTelemetryLossCount and subsequent LOCAL_EXPORT_LOSS explicitly report the gap. Collection must not be described as complete in that case.

Analytics and trust

CategoryEvidence
IdentityServer-authenticated account ID, separate local account identifier, hero ID/class/start and end level, local attempt ordinal. No real name or advertising identifier is collected.
Environment/contentApp version, build GUID, platform, save/item/map versions, stage, map fingerprint and seed. Configuration source, release version, hash and the admitted settings are retained.
Timing/progressionClient UTC start/end, simulation duration, existing attendance/fatigue duration, resume count, observed start; server receipt time is generated independently.
LoadoutInitial build/skills/ranks/options, Hunt Edict, equipped item instances, slot levels, rune configuration, potion state and final configuration; configuration-change events also capture the build.
Outcomes/rewardsOutcome/reason, kills/boss completion, awarded gold, equipment/rune counts, claimed/ignored drop states and exact item snapshots. Gold uses RiftEarnings, not wallet deltas.
Combat/integrityEvent sequence, cast/target/rule IDs, position, HP/resource, damage calculation inputs/results, final-window analysis and truncation/resume/export/clock trust markers.

Client payloads are client_observed. SHA-256 provides retry byte identity, not anti-cheat authenticity. The receiver binds ownership to authentication, deduplicates account/run IDs and audits conflicting bodies. Suspicious speed, outcome or reward reports are investigation signals, never automatic sanctions.

The existing AuthoritativeRiftVerifier replays from a server-owned admission snapshot, clock and seed. Its completed server_replay copy is included in HuntAuthorityCheckpoint.combatTelemetry and committed by the same CAS as account/replay cursors. Client HTTP ingestion rejects this provenance. An internal host adapter must pass only committed checkpoints into Repository.attach_authority.

Server integration

All current game authentication, operations and ingestion URLs use https://hellscript-player-logs.hoosung.chatgpt.site. Resources/Data/ServerConnection.json contains public origins only. An isolated QA file passed with -hellscriptQaSessionFile must match the Site and upload purpose. Ordinary Google players use in-memory sessions. Follow Sites backend for persistence, authentication, migration and publishing.

CombatTelemetryUploader removes an outbox file only when accepted, runId and the exact-byte payloadHash match. Timeouts, authentication and transient failures retry with exponential backoff capped at 300 seconds; redirects are disabled. The Sites receiver acknowledges only after original R2 storage and the D1 summary succeed.

Legacy receiver reference

Python and its tests remain local references for the earlier data and permission contracts. Do not deploy them as another production service. Container deployment files are removed. CI checks Python contracts, the existing operations web model, and the Sites build/Node suite. Historical platform deployment/volume/backup evidence remains in the 2026-09-25 operations record. Current storage and management belong to one Site.

Results from the original journal implementation

The following evidence was collected when combat journals were introduced. Later configuration and QA-connection integration is recorded separately in Live operations verification.

  • Unity Edit Mode passed the 488/488 expanded regression run, 155/155 journal/enemy/boss/localization follow-up and 137/137 final natural-death/localization/movement-response run. These overlap and must not be summed into a whole-project count. See validation and final death tests.
  • The macOS development build succeeded with zero build errors. Normal Update first advanced the live journal, followed by direct fixed-step simulation. An unforced stage-one victory reported approximately 102.8 simulation seconds, 43 kills, 2,276 gold and five collected items. Attendance and simulation duration are separately recorded; this is not a claim of 102.8 seconds of real-time play.
  • Portrait 440×956, landscape 956×440 and PC 1600×900, 1600×1000 and 2100×900 were checked in Korean/English at 100%/140% text size: 20 live-HUD and 20 history cases with rendered-text and HUD-overlap assertions.
  • One actual run and 99 labeled list fixtures exercised 100 rows. EventSystem raycasts and pointer down/up/click opened the rift records entry, all three result filters and chronological details. Synthetic list fixtures were removed before the final save.
  • A separate application process restored the full journal. Edit Mode covered 101st-record pruning without deleting delivery evidence, failed saves, full queues, ACK/crash recovery and rejected-body/crash recovery.
  • Unity client → localhost HTTP receiver → SQLite commit → matching ID/SHA-256 ACK → outbox removal passed. Server tests passed 9/9 and all five analytics queries executed against the received run. Runtime evidence records file size and hash.
  • Shared-UI contract checks and 9/9 regression tests, wiki build/check, 10/10 Python wiki tests and JavaScript wiki checks passed. Physical mobile and production service integration are outside the verified scope.

Chronological text · Defeat filter fixtures · Separate-process restore

Implementation sources: CombatJournal.cs · combat_telemetry.py · combat_analytics.sql · SHA-256

# Rift entry casual skin

2026-10-14 · [Korean report](Rift_Entry_Casual_Skin_20261014.md)

Source is frozen for one combined integration validation. Individual Unity/build plans are closed; native acceptance remains unverified.


## Final integration handoff and source freeze

Per the user's combined-test decision, task-18 stops source editing after this documentation commit. Resume only for a concrete defect request from integration owner `01a13790-39bc-7062-a516-b83a354000a8`. That owner uses a separate integration branch and the existing Library in `/Users/t8g-2410-pn-005/Documents/Codex/2026-10-14/task-6/skill-skin`. Historical individual-slot requests below are superseded. No branch, source or artwork is deleted.

Final implementation source: `8ed46741b35071c23633f6bb43bf1d2e97799f5b` on `codex/casual-rift-entry-skin`, in `/Users/t8g-2410-pn-005/Documents/Codex/2026-10-14/task-18/rift-entry-skin`. Worktree was clean before this documentation update, with no uncommitted source. Only this freeze documentation commit follows; its exact final HEAD is recorded in task-18/evidence/validation-queue.json and the parent reply. No model-capacity failure or unfinished available API connection remains.

Current integration observation: task-6 HEAD `873ea29062f19cfd769c3b57ffba7a385b2125b7` already contains both118371c7 and final source8ed46741 as ancestors. **Do not reapply source commits; only this freeze documentation commit remains.** The integration owner is active; do not checkout/reset to that observed HEAD. For recovery from a pure common0ccba80e baseline only, the screen non-merge commit order is: `302876d1b07acae77d125075f78a5bbe90dee7ba`, `ac6f49c08b7dd54a347d447d6da6c59835dd35d0`, `8c63d13c9638cf963a54066d6293bbe8dd8553d6`, `118371c77908ddfa1cf57097efa7c6c0c9391b0a`, `8ed46741b35071c23633f6bb43bf1d2e97799f5b`. Do not separately cherry-pick the common merge commits 2e03272a/70f76732. Task-18 does not modify the integration checkout.

Owned source: RiftEntryWindow.cs, RiftEntryWindow.Popups.cs, RiftEntryWindow.CasualSkin.cs and its new meta under Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Runtime/Presentation. Art is under Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Art/RiftEntry/Casual/ with folder metadata: 42 approved PNGs plus one generated portal, 33,952,354 bytes. Mapping/source hashes are linked below. Portal SHA256: `788b21ce4e5516262a5267b26f9d2853c8585878563f4531ae3c7b9980cc760e`. Preserve 49 legacy shared asset pairs. Common equipment359 PNGs belong to the common commit; this sparse source checkout is not the Unity validation project.

Remaining common improvements are a paid-button accent and RiftRewardList skin parameter. The existing one-face/three-label adapters preserve behavior; these are not unconnected available APIs. Entry owns no equipment/chart/combat/edict consumer. Further changes wait for the integration owner's concrete request.

Relevant EditMode filters: Hellscript.Tests.RiftEntryTests, RiftAdmissionTests, PotionLoadoutTests and StoreViewBindingTests, plus Hellscript.Tests.RewardBoxTests for first-clear reward coverage. Runtime entry points are `RuntimeRiftEntrySmoke.cs` / `-hellscriptRiftEntrySmoke` and `RuntimeRiftEntrySmoke.Pickers.cs` / `-hellscriptRiftPickerSmoke`. Preparation/parity/portal flags remain targeted options in their existing partials. Use a development player, disposable `-hellscriptSavePath`, task-owned `-hellscriptEvidencePath` and muted audio. The base entry smoke does not enforce the save-isolation argument and has no built-in mute, so the runner must supply both. PickerFlow finishes at1680×720. The current harness executes the first matching branch, so passing several smoke flags to one process does not execute them all. The integration owner sequences these within the combined validation plan/build.

The existing entry smoke covers440×956,956×440,1600×900,1600×1000,2100×900 in KO/EN; it does **not** cover2868×1320. Add that required viewport, actual Canvas scale and documented Mac safe-area assumptions, glyph fitting/locked-slot markers, masks/gauges, English truncation, input/scroll/save/error, potion swap/unequip and entry/reward states to integration acceptance. Artboards remain32 DOM/1 expanded visual, and no native after-capture or physical-device validation exists. The richer portal glow, portrait art strip and other owners' skill/reward-detail chrome remain known visual differences.

Reuse prior static evidence (Runtime834:0 errors/47 warnings, UI15/15, refresh16/193). No generation, source test, Unity execution or build is repeated for this freeze handoff. The integration owner records validation against the final combined input. Retain current source/art/small evidence and existing task-18 static outputs for review on2026-10-28.

## Shared follow-up integration — 0ccba80e (latest source record)

Merged parent-approved `0ccba80eef0da4703cb7ffcd1fb8e22848002b3d` at `70f767327ddbfa7f825f5122bb326bf4ffae5186`, preserving prior Rift commit `118371c7`, artwork and behavior. This section supersedes the first API integration record below.

Verified actual Noto400/700/900 cmap coverage for ◆◇ and removed 31 lines of local string replacement/diamond rendering. Original legend and locked-slot strings now use shared Noto without changing font sizes, rectangles or the existing fitting algorithm. The font diamond is wider than the temporary vector; KO/EN fatigue legend fitting and locked-slot markers still require native verification. Shared Muted contrast improvements apply through the existing API use.

Rift entry has no equipment/chart/combat-HUD/edict-skin consumer. The merged Git history includes the approved provider and 359 shared equipment PNGs; the sparse source checkout does not materialize those unused PNGs or copy them into Rift artwork. The parent validation project supplies common Resources. Existing coin/potion/chest/portal mappings remain. No new art was generated.

The paid-action accent and RiftRewardList skin APIs remain absent, so the one purple button face and three neutral-label adapters remain. TextColor was not applied to all local colors because it would change gold titles and surface colors. All 28 imported common source/test/font files match the requested SHA byte-for-byte.

Final static checks: **834 Runtime sources, 0 errors / 47 warnings**, reading 296 existing references in place; **15/15 UI contract cases**, refresh **16 bindings / 193 UI sources**, and diff whitespace checks passed. [Evidence summary](RiftEntryCasualEvidence20261014/common-followup/summary.json) records source/font/art hashes and logs. The only authored source edit in this follow-up is RiftEntryWindow.CasualSkin.cs. Approved Rift art 42/42 and the portal hash are unchanged.

Unity execution, new Library uploads and new art generation remain zero for this follow-up. Artboard coverage remains 32 DOM / 1 expanded visual. Parent reported external Unity PID30116 still active at 07:50 UTC. This task did not act on that process; the proposed first Unity slot remains unassigned pending a parent-selected project and slot.

## First shared API integration record

The parent-approved common commit `cdb9c140fbf8b778bd3c0bbc0fbcc68a5d9e3fa8` and its preceding documentation were merged locally at `2e03272a529bf24336042608f8740e30f40ea7f3`. Previous Rift implementation `8c63d13c` and approved art remain. This update supersedes the initial implementation description below.

Main and popup windows now pass `skin:UiSkin.Casual`. General and choice buttons use Casual chrome, close uses CasualClose, and the help icon explicitly receives common chrome. The private frame/general-button renderer, blanket child-text recoloring and button-list polling were removed. Fatigue/empty-slot/badge panels use SetSkin; gauges and transparent layers preserve their colors. Main scroll/actions use the common rounded clip with the frame's exact pivot and full size; the conservative inset covers frame border plus shadow (`7*frameLine`). Source review found and corrected the reparenting-origin and bottom-shadow overlap risks. Pixel acceptance remains pending.

The shared LabelFont policy supplies Noto400 when Jua lacks symbols; explicit Noto700 emphasis and the two vector diamond markers remain. Semantic Success/Danger/paid text uses shared contrast-aware colors. The reward list currently lacks a skin argument, so only its three neutral labels are adapted explicitly.

One known API gap remains: ApplyChrome has no paid/semantic accent parameter. Only the purple `rift-enter-fast` face keeps a small screen-local RiftEntryPaidButtonGraphic while preserving the original UiButton's role, handlers, disabled and focus state. Request an optional common accent API and a RiftRewardList skin input. EquipmentArtProvider applies to equipment, not this screen's coins/potions/chests/portal; existing verified mappings remain and no missing art/chart/battle API was invented.

Imported shared source/tests match cdb9c140 byte-for-byte. Authored source edits remain restricted to the three assigned Rift files. An asset check caught the sparse checkout excluding the local art after merge; the dedicated art path was re-included and all 42 approved hashes plus the portal remained unchanged. The final checkout contains approximately 104MB of file data (about 111MiB allocated on disk), including Git objects, sources, art and documentation, with no Unity cache.

Static Roslyn compilation reads 296 existing Unity references in place and compiles 831 Runtime sources. Outputs are isolated under task-18/evidence/static-common-api; no Editor/player starts. The result is **0 errors and 47 warnings** (CS0108:1, CS0618:45, CS0414:1), matching the common baseline warning distribution. All 831 current source hashes match the compiler receipt. The UI contract suite passed **15/15**, refresh audit passed **16 guarded bindings / 192 UI sources**, and diff whitespace checks passed. [Evidence summary](RiftEntryCasualEvidence20261014/common-api/summary.json), logs and input hashes are committed under common-api. These are not Unity or EditMode execution results. Runtime queue status remains pending: the parent reported external Unity PID30116 and has not assigned a slot. No action was taken on that process. Artboard counts (32 DOM/1 visually expanded), existing Library IDs and the absence of a player after-capture remain unchanged.

The isolated branch `codex/casual-rift-entry-skin` starts at `2e193c336c6176d80b9ddbdff7269246bf2590fb`; validated game code is `4139a77e2df495cee009c07c6094b2eea9b1aeaa`. At initial implementation, documentation HEAD `df2e366c18ba01eaf8a2ceaa145dfb8c940e5f7a` had no Presentation source differences. The current imported API baseline is cdb9c140 above. Only RiftEntryWindow.cs, RiftEntryWindow.Popups.cs and the new RiftEntryWindow.CasualSkin.cs/meta were changed, with screen-local art and evidence. Shared source has no authored edits; the parent-approved API commit was imported. Domain/save contracts, localization, project settings and original checkout/staging are untouched. No Unity cache or build was copied or started. The initial source workspace was approximately 63MB; after the shared API merge it contains approximately 104MB of file data.

The user reported 32 Claude artboards. All 32 were read as DOM inventory; exactly one PC 16:9 Korean artboard was expanded and visually inspected. Observed interactions covered stage 24→25, the disabled next-stage button, opening/cancelling fast entry and opening/closing the potion picker. This is not 32-artboard visual acceptance. Future browser use must first verify the user-designated Chrome profile.

Source-level before/after: dark sanctuary becomes a sky/cream art panel with a violet portal; legacy fonts become Jua display text and Noto400 body/700 emphasis; original UiButton hit areas and handlers receive shared rounded light faces with green entry and coral close states; only purple paid entry retains a local face adapter. Fatigue fills retain their capacity calculation and are clipped inside a rounded track. Text is styled before preferred-height measurement. Existing fit scales, font sizes and best-fit bounds remain; runtime must measure whether new font metrics affect the resulting fit. There is no player before/after capture yet.

Potion swap, unequip, immediate-save behavior and real first-clear rewards are preserved despite prototype differences. Restocking, repeat settings, records, inventory readiness, admission pending/cancel, suspended-run resume/restart and next-content hints remain. Other screens and nested reward detail windows retain their owners.

Forty-two approved PNGs match their source SHA256: one coin, three basic potions, 36 elixirs and two chests. A new portal makes 43 images, 33,952,354 bytes, with 43 unique import GUIDs. The coin keeps its legacy sprite-name contract. All 49 audited legacy assets remain because other screens use their dynamic Resources paths.

Portal: `Assets/HELLSCRIPT/Resources/Art/RiftEntry/Casual/rift-entry-portal-casual-v01.png`, SHA256 `788b21ce4e5516262a5267b26f9d2853c8585878563f4531ae3c7b9980cc760e`, 1,097,923 bytes, actual 1254×1254 RGBA, alpha 0–254. Created with built-in image_gen under delegated ownership after no approved replacement was found. Parent visual review remains. The saved prompt and asset mapping are in RiftEntryCasualEvidence20261014.

Final static UI contract suite: 15/15 passed. Refresh audit: 16 guarded bindings and 192 inventoried UI source files passed. `git diff --check` passed for the final base-to-head diff. The first staged check exposed trailing whitespace in new metadata; 46 new meta files were normalized and the full diff rechecked. Actual bundled font cmaps revealed missing Jua punctuation and missing Noto diamonds: punctuation now uses the shared Noto400 fallback, while explicit emphasis remains Noto700 and diamonds are non-raycast vector markers. Independent source review found no further definite defect. The initial checks did not establish C# compilation; the shared-API follow-up now passes a separate Roslyn compile, while runtime correctness remains unverified.

Library: Claude reference capture `libfile_f1f61ec6c4a48191a6f5659566bc34da` version 1 (1325×746); portal `libfile_c60dd4966560819186473c6a951e9fcb` version 0. There is no runtime after-capture ID yet.

Pending validation requires the parent to assign a single Unity slot and execution project. Suggested EditMode scope: RiftEntryTests, RiftAdmissionTests, PotionLoadoutTests and StoreViewBindingTests, with RewardBoxTests if reward behavior is exercised. Runtime priority: `-hellscriptRiftEntrySmoke` and `-hellscriptRiftPickerSmoke`, plus relevant preparation/portal scenarios. Use disposable saves and muted audio. Cover KO/EN, PC 16:9/16:10/21:9, mobile portrait/landscape including 2868×1320, disabled/selected/empty/error states, swap/unequip, scrolling, cancel/pending and reward states. Record actual scale; DPR3 safe-area margins left/right102, bottom54, top0 are assumptions, not physical iOS validation.

Remaining visual differences: the generated portal has richer light texture than the prototype's simple oval, portrait retains the existing art-strip structure with a faint portal backdrop, and shared skill icon/nested reward chrome is outside this ownership boundary. The other 31 artboards, pixel parity, device behavior, accessibility and performance are unverified. Suggested shared improvements are native verification of the expanded font-symbol coverage and extensions to the supplied API for a paid-action accent and RiftRewardList skin input. The fixed 430-look catalog and font files were not modified.

Keep sources, art, captures and small receipts through parent integration; review retention on 2026-10-28. No legacy deletion, remote push, public sharing, main merge or web build was performed.

The final checkout contains approximately 104MB of file data (about 111MiB allocated on disk), including Git objects, sources, art and documentation, with no Unity cache.

The UI contract suite passed 15/15, refresh audit passed 16 guarded bindings / 192 UI sources, and diff whitespace checks passed. Evidence summary, logs and input hashes are committed under common-api. These are not Unity or EditMode execution results. Runtime queue status remains pending: the parent reported external Unity PID30116 and has not assigned a slot. No action was taken on that process. Artboard counts (32 DOM/1 visually expanded), existing Library IDs and the absence of a player after-capture remain unchanged.

Keep sources, art, captures and small receipts through parent integration; review retention on 2026-10-28. No legacy deletion, remote push, public sharing, main merge or web build was performed.

# Rift gear recommendations — unified integration handoff

2026-10-14 · [한국어](Casual_Rift_Gear_Skin_20261014.md)

**Shared follow-up and approved equipment provider are connected. Individual Unity/build plans are closed; source editing is frozen after this handoff.** All screens will be validated together by common owner `01a13790-39bc-7062-a516-b83a354000a8` on a separate integration branch in task-6/skill-skin using the existing Library. Resume edits only for a specific integration defect request.

## Input and integration order

Branch `codex/casual-rift-gear-skin`, task-10/rift-skin. Original baseline2e193c336c6176d80b9ddbdff7269246bf2590fb contains validated game code4139a77e2df495cee009c07c6094b2eea9b1aeaa. Apply screen consumer commits in order:12880d713ac720e2b177d3f8383bf48584a3aa3e,35fd4986c0d4bf0779dd067dbb3c1850a9b20fac, then the final provider consumer commit containing this document. Exact final SHA/dirty/bundle are recorded in task-10/evidence/FINAL_INTEGRATION_HANDOFF.md.

Common cumulative tip0ccba80eef0da4703cb7ffcd1fb8e22848002b3d includes6cdf2df690941b7c9f751c39235ea36ce4ff9ed9 (geometry/symbols) and f25e67aab62d72f9792b5c0d49e6692bfbca5eed (art). Do not cherry-pick only the last tip commit: its ancestors contain those dependencies. Common merges in this screen branch are f02d6f4c4e2fce6d923a13891888b32fc9e6eacf and b22a82c220884e33c88aeacc6ad649b3b3af3107. Integration may merge the full branch or apply the ordered screen commits over the cumulative common tip.

Only assigned runtime files were authored here: GameUI.GearRecommendations.cs, RiftRecommendationWindow.cs and RiftGearSettingsWindow.cs. All774common files match the supplied tip. Original checkout/index/refs and other work remain unchanged. Sparse checkout relies on original Git object alternates; preserve these objects until integration. This folder lacks complete Resources and Library and is not a Unity execution project.

## Completed connection and approved art

RiftGearSkin.Current caches one `UiSkin.Casual.WithEquipmentArt(CasualEquipmentArt.Provider)` instance. HUD cards, both windows, slots, details/comparison and their replacement paths receive this scope. No screen-owned shared API connection remains. Chart/edict APIs are outside this screen's ownership.

Resources root: `Art/Casual/Equipment/{ID}`. [Shared receipt](../../tools/casual_equipment_art_receipt.json) SHA256:52b29468e0932e9d40e80ed007b27345a69ad08188ae3eb47b004dd3defa3020. Shared verify passed359PNGs,330item keys,30emblems,362GUIDs and preservation of336legacy assets. Total69,753,836bytes. IDs/B28-to-B32 alias/catalogue/unlock rules remain. Independently matched source359/shared359SHA and CSV/director/QA/index hashes: [art evidence](CasualRiftGearSkinEvidence20261014/approved-art-followup-audit.json). Local image generation/copies/deletions:0. New bundle excludes common art ancestry as a prerequisite, avoiding another359PNG archive. ## Design, before/after and remaining differences

Design:https://claude.ai/artifact/JfwkCuft9ZivYvSNvYwceJ . Declared16boards; DOM/content/iframe source/state16; enlarged visual views3. Incomplete14/16PDF is not the design basis. A subsequent EN landscape accessibility inspection is not an additional visual capture. No Chrome used this follow-up; future browser work requires dakrdong@gmail.com profile verification. Original key capture Library:`libfile_547bac59b30c81918af6cfff2aa6fff0`. Game captures:0.

Final reference acceptance remains pending along with long EN labels, original fullwidth-plus Noto fallback width, scroll/input/error states, rounded corners and new art rendering.

Direct coordinates/font sizes/eight v.Button callbacks/comparison/numeric/slider callbacks remain. Card width92, slot+98height (portrait150/existing landscape152), landscape.75scale, HUD position, legacy best-fit7-10 and ellipsis are unchanged. No new shrink/widen/Canvas/update loop. Timer/equip/dismiss/transaction/lifecycle tail is byte-identical to original baseline. Draft/Normalize/atomic save/portal-return contracts are preserved.

Four prior common geometry differences are restored in source: score13/16pt and plaque52/64; original major-divider height; greater-affix inset16; socket24/inset28. [Independent review](CasualRiftGearSkinEvidence20261014/common-followup-review.md). Six runtime geometry cases and font wrapping are unexecuted. Legacy ItemCardArt Badge/Divider/Star/Socket resources still provide presence/dimensions; do not retire them as unused decoration.

## Completed static checks

Latest contract15passed/22.499s: [receipt](CasualRiftGearSkinEvidence20261014/ui-contract-followup.json), [log](CasualRiftGearSkinEvidence20261014/ui-contract-followup.log). Refresh16bindings/192sources passed. [Source/tree/glyph audit](CasualRiftGearSkinEvidence20261014/shared-followup-audit.json) passed774shared identities, provider scope, callbacks/direct geometry and Noto glyphs. [Script](CasualRiftGearSkinEvidence20261014/audit-shared-followup.py). Shared installed-art verify and source/shared359SHA comparison passed. Source RGB is not device certification. Independent review found no new consumer defect. Earlier failed/invalidated receipts are retained as historical evidence.

This screen ran no C# compiler, Unity, EditMode, player, build or game capture. Roslyn reference preflight was read-only; separate compile/test proposals are superseded by the unified integration instruction. Completed checks were not rerun.

## Unified validation targets

Related Hellscript.Tests filters: RecommendedEquipmentTests, SharedUiTests, ItemComparisonTests, StoreViewBindingTests, UiButtonTests, CasualUiSkinTests, EquipmentArtTests. Integration owner selects against final inputs without duplicating common checks.

Entry controls: rift-gear-icon-{id}/rift-gear-inspect-{id} open detail/comparison; rift-gear-quick-equip-{id}; rift-gear-settings-{id}; rift-gear-dismiss-{id}. Existing smoke flags:`-hellscriptEdictControlsSmoke -hellscriptEdictGearSmoke`.

KO/EN440x956,956x440,1600x900,1600x1000,2100x900,2868x1320. Empty/selected/disabled/error, save/cancel/invalid numbers/add-option/scroll, comparison target/repaint, equip/dismiss/expiry/portal return, round icon edges/panel corners/long labels. Isolated save, muted audio. Mac resolution simulation is not physical iOS; integration runner records safe-area assumptions.

Parent observed external Unity PID30116 running at07:50; this task did not manipulate it. Individual queue is closed in favor of the unified run. Preserve source/branch/evidence. No remote push/public sharing/main merge/web build/deployment. Proposed shared rules: separate decoration from geometry/font approval, contrast against actual backgrounds, and scoped-art persistence through redraw.
